Name: adaptive_block_size
Title: Adaptive Block Size: Dynamic Context Window Adjustment for Efficient Training
Experiment: Modify the model to dynamically adjust its block size during training, starting with a smaller block size and gradually increasing it. This could potentially lead to faster initial training and better long-range dependency learning.

Name: layerwise_learning_rates
Title: Layer-wise Learning Rate Adaptation: Optimizing Training Dynamics in Transformer Models
Experiment: Implement layer-wise learning rates, where each transformer layer has its own learning rate. Modify the configure_optimizers function to assign different learning rates to different layers, with deeper layers having lower learning rates. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model.

Name: auxiliary_future_heads
Title: Auxiliary Future Heads: Multi-Horizon Supervision for Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Add optional auxiliary linear heads to GPT that predict future characters at fixed horizons such as 2, 4, and 8 steps ahead, while keeping the original tied lm_head for standard next-token prediction and generation. Modify get_batch() to sample block_size + max_horizon tokens and return shifted targets for each horizon, with the primary target corresponding to horizon 1. Modify GPT.forward() or the training loop to compute loss_1 plus weighted auxiliary losses, for example loss = loss_1 + 0.2 * loss_2 + 0.1 * loss_4 + 0.05 * loss_8. During evaluation, log both the combined objective and the ordinary next-token validation loss, and compare models primarily by best next-token validation loss, final_train_loss, convergence speed, and generation throughput. At inference time, use only the original lm_head, so generation behavior and runtime remain unchanged.

Name: ema_self_distillation
Title: EMA Self-Distillation: Temporal Smoothing as a Regularizer for Small Language Models
Experiment: Add a frozen exponential-moving-average teacher copy of the GPT model after initialization, before optional torch.compile is applied to the student. During training, compute the usual next-token cross-entropy loss from the student. After warmup_iters, periodically add a small distillation term, for example every 4 iterations, using KLDivLoss(log_softmax(student_logits / T), softmax(teacher_logits / T)) * T * T with temperature T=2.0 and a ramped weight from 0.0 to 0.2. Keep the teacher in eval mode under torch.no_grad(). After each optimizer step, update teacher parameters with ema_param = decay * ema_param + (1 - decay) * student_param, using ema_decay=0.995 or 0.999. During evaluation, log ordinary next-token validation loss for both the student and EMA teacher, while generation and throughput reporting use a single model only. Compare against baseline using best validation loss, train-val gap, convergence speed, total training time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: short_context_distillation
Title: Short-Context Distillation: Improving Context-Robust Language Modeling from Full-Context Predictions
Experiment: Modify the training loop to use the normal full block_size next-token cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup, every few iterations, also create a fixed short-context suffix view, such as the final 64 tokens of the same batch. Run a second forward pass on this short view, compute its next-token cross-entropy, and add a small KL consistency loss from detached full-context logits on the aligned final 64 positions to the short-context logits, using temperature 2.0 and a ramped weight up to 0.1 or 0.2. Keep generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, and compare against baseline using best full-context validation loss, short-context validation loss, convergence speed, total training time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: context_length_dropout
Title: Context Length Dropout: Robust Language Modeling Across Variable Context Budgets
Experiment: Modify the training loop so that, after warmup, each iteration samples an effective context length L from [32, 64, 128, 256], with full length 256 used with higher probability such as 0.5 to preserve clean long-context performance. Replace model(X, Y) with model(X[:, -L:], Y[:, -L:]) for the sampled L, keeping generation unchanged. Log the sampled context length and effective supervised tokens per iteration so comparisons can distinguish wall-clock speed from token budget. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary next-token validation loss at fixed context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256 by slicing validation batches to the final L tokens. Compare against the baseline using best full-context validation loss, mean validation loss across context lengths, short-context robustness gap, convergence speed, total train time, effective supervised tokens, and inference tokens per second.

Name: dataset_conditioned_multitask
Title: Dataset-Conditioned Multitask Character Modeling Across Text Domains
Experiment: Add a multitask training mode that trains one GPT across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Build a union character vocabulary from each dataset's meta.pkl, create local-to-global token id maps, and remap memmap batches inside get_batch(). Modify get_batch() to sample datasets uniformly or round-robin and return X, Y, and dataset_id. Extend GPTConfig/GPT with num_datasets and an optional learned dataset embedding added to token and position embeddings in GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, dataset_id=None). Train and compare three settings: the existing separate per-dataset models, a shared pooled model without dataset conditioning, and a shared pooled model with dataset conditioning. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary next-token validation loss separately for each dataset plus their mean. During sampling, condition on each dataset id and decode with the global vocabulary, logging invalid or out-of-domain character rates when generated characters fall outside that dataset's original vocabulary. Compare methods using per-dataset best validation loss, mean validation loss, parameter count, total train time, convergence speed, generation quality diagnostics, and inference tokens per second.

Name: confidence_gated_early_exit
Title: Confidence-Gated Early Exits for Adaptive-Depth Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT to expose intermediate exits after selected transformer blocks, for example layers 2 and 4 in the 6-layer model. Add one small LayerNorm per exit and reuse the existing tied lm_head for exit logits, avoiding large extra output heads. During training, compute the standard final next-token cross-entropy plus a modest auxiliary next-token loss from the exits, for example loss = loss_final + 0.2 * mean(exit_losses). Modify generation to support both fixed-depth exits and a simple confidence-gated mode: after each exit, compute predictive entropy or max probability, stop early if confidence exceeds a threshold, otherwise continue to deeper layers. Calibrate a few thresholds on validation batches to produce different average depths. Extend estimate_loss() to report validation loss at each fixed exit depth and final depth. Compare against the baseline using final-depth validation loss, shallow-exit validation loss, adaptive-exit speed-quality curves, average layers used per token, total training time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_embedding_denoising
Title: Causal Embedding Denoising: Robust Autoregressive Language Modeling from Partially Erased Prefixes
Experiment: Add an optional learned mask_embedding parameter to GPT with the same dimension as token embeddings. Modify GPT.forward() to accept an optional input_mask argument; after computing tok_emb, replace masked token embeddings with mask_embedding before adding positional embeddings. In the training loop, after warmup_iters, sample a Bernoulli mask over X positions with a small ramped probability such as 0.0 to 0.10, corrupt only the input embeddings, and keep Y unchanged. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy loss and leave generation unchanged by calling forward without an input_mask. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary clean validation loss and a corrupted-context validation loss using the same mask probability. Compare against the baseline using best clean validation loss, corrupted-context validation loss, train-val gap, convergence speed, total train time, generation quality, and inference tokens per second.

Name: position_embedding_dropout
Title: Position Embedding Dropout for Robust Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to accept an optional pos_dropout_p argument. After computing pos_emb, during training only, randomly drop entire positional embedding vectors with probability pos_dropout_p using a mask of shape (t, 1), optionally rescaling kept positions by 1 / (1 - pos_dropout_p). Keep token embeddings, targets, model size, and generation unchanged. In the training loop, ramp pos_dropout_p from 0.0 after warmup_iters to a small maximum such as 0.10 or 0.15, and log the active value. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary clean validation loss plus validation losses when batches are sliced to context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256. Compare against the baseline and a small ablation over maximum dropout probability using best full-context validation loss, mean validation loss across context lengths, short-context robustness gap, train-val gap, total training time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: support_gated_ngram_cache
Title: Support-Gated N-Gram Cache Fusion for Small Character Language Models
Experiment: Train the GPT models normally. After training, build a bounded backoff n-gram cache from each dataset's train.bin using suffix lengths such as 2, 4, and 8, storing next-character counts and pruning very low-count entries to control memory. Add helper functions that find the longest matching suffix for each context and return a smoothed cache distribution plus its support count. Evaluate GPT alone, cache alone, fixed interpolation, and support-gated interpolation where the effective cache weight is alpha * count / (count + tau). Tune alpha and tau on a fixed calibration slice of val.bin and report losses on the remaining validation slice to reduce overfitting. Modify sampling to optionally use the same support-gated fusion at each generated token. Log baseline validation loss, cache-only loss, fused validation loss, best alpha and tau, cache hit rate by suffix length, cache size, generation throughput, and sample text across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: self_corruption_recovery
Title: Self-Corruption Recovery: Training Language Models to Recover from Their Own Prefix Errors
Experiment: Modify the training loop to add a lightweight self-corruption auxiliary objective after warmup_iters. On normal iterations, train exactly as before with clean next-token cross-entropy. Every few iterations after warmup, use the detached clean logits from the standard forward pass to sample plausible replacement tokens for X[:, 1:] from logits[:, :-1, :], restricted to top_k predictions and sampled with temperature 1.0 or 1.2. Apply a Bernoulli corruption mask with a small ramped probability, such as 0.0 to 0.10, leaving the first token unchanged, to create X_corrupt. Run one additional forward pass model(X_corrupt, Y) and optimize loss = clean_loss + lambda_corrupt * corrupt_loss, with lambda_corrupt ramping to about 0.25 or 0.5. Keep generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary clean train/validation loss as the primary metric and a corrupted-prefix validation loss as a robustness diagnostic. Add simple generation diagnostics such as repeated character rate and distinct n-gram fraction. Compare against the baseline using best clean validation loss, corrupted-prefix validation loss, generation repetition diagnostics, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: directional_reverse_lm
Title: Direction-Conditioned Reverse Language Modeling as Auxiliary Supervision for Causal Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPTConfig and GPT to optionally include a learned two-entry direction embedding, added alongside token and position embeddings in GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, direction_id=0). Use direction_id=0 for ordinary left-to-right training and generation. In the training loop, always compute the standard forward next-token loss on X, Y. After warmup_iters, every k iterations such as k=2 or k=4, construct a reverse-factorization view of the same contiguous examples with X_rev = torch.flip(Y, dims=[1]) and Y_rev = torch.flip(X, dims=[1]), then compute an auxiliary reverse loss with direction_id=1. Optimize loss = forward_loss + lambda_reverse * reverse_loss, ramping lambda_reverse from 0.0 to 0.25 or 0.5. Keep sampling unchanged by always using direction_id=0. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary forward train/val loss as the primary metric and reverse train/val loss as a diagnostic. Log the auxiliary update frequency and extra forward-pass cost. Compare against the baseline and, if runtime permits, a compute-matched baseline that spends the same extra passes on normal forward batches. Report best forward validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, total train time, reverse validation loss, generated samples, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: rarity_balanced_ce
Title: Rarity-Balanced Cross-Entropy for Calibrated Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to compute token frequencies. Build clipped normalized target weights w_i = clamp((freq_i + eps)^(-alpha), w_min, w_max), then normalize so the expected weight under the training distribution is 1. Modify the training loop to compute logits with model(X, Y) but replace the optimization loss with a convex mixture loss = (1 - lambda_rare) * ce_loss + lambda_rare * balanced_ce_loss, where balanced_ce_loss is per-token cross-entropy weighted by w[target]. Ramp lambda_rare from 0 after warmup_iters to 0.25 or 0.5, and test alpha values such as 0.25 and 0.5. Keep generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train/val loss as the primary metric plus validation loss by target-frequency buckets, rare-token accuracy, common-token loss regression, generated character-frequency KL against the validation distribution, and distinct n-gram rate. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss, rare-bucket validation loss, generation diversity, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: detached_segment_memory
Title: Detached Segment Memory Tokens for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify get_batch() to support an adjacent-segment mode returning prev_X, X, and Y, where prev_X is the block immediately before the current supervised block. Extend GPTConfig with num_memory_tokens and add a memory projection plus optional learned memory-position embeddings. Refactor GPT so hidden states can be computed from token indices, then add forward_with_memory(prev_idx, idx, targets): encode prev_idx under torch.no_grad(), compress its final hidden states into K memory tokens using chunked mean pooling followed by the learned projection, prepend those memory tokens to the current token embeddings, run the transformer causally over memory plus current tokens, and compute cross-entropy only on the current-token positions. Set the internal model block size to block_size + K while keeping the supervised current sequence length fixed. Compare K values 0, 4, 8, and 16, using K=0 as the adjacent-segment control. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss, adjacent-context validation loss, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare methods using best adjacent-context validation loss, standard validation loss, gain per memory token, convergence speed, and wall-clock overhead.

Name: context_gain_weighting
Title: Context-Gain Weighted Language Modeling: Focusing Training on Tokens That Need Long Context
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute the normal full-context logits for X, Y and the ordinary mean next-token cross-entropy loss. After warmup_iters, every k iterations such as k=4, also evaluate a short-context suffix X[:, -L:], Y[:, -L:] with L=64 under torch.no_grad(). Compute unreduced per-token cross-entropy for the aligned final L positions from both the full-context logits and the short-context logits. Estimate detached context_gain = short_loss - full_loss, convert positive gains into weights with weights = 1 + gain_scale * clamp(context_gain, min=0), cap weights at 3.0, and normalize them to mean 1. Add a ramped auxiliary weighted loss on the final L full-context positions, for example total_loss = ordinary_loss + aux_weight * weighted_suffix_loss with aux_weight ramping from 0 to 0.3 after warmup. On non-auxiliary iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, plus mean positive context gain and validation loss on high-gain versus low-gain token positions. Compare against the baseline using best full-context validation loss, mean multi-context validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: future_chunk_contrastive
Title: Future-Chunk Contrastive Prediction for Long-Range Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states in addition to logits and loss. Add two small projection layers to GPT: a query projection from hidden states to a contrastive dimension and a key projection from pooled future-token embeddings to the same dimension. During normal training, keep the standard next-token cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every k iterations such as k=4, sample anchor positions with room for a future chunk of length C, for example C=16 or 32. For each anchor, use the final hidden state at that position as the query. Build the positive key by mean-pooling the detached token embeddings of the next C target characters, then passing the pooled vector through the key projection. Use other sampled future chunks in the minibatch as negatives and compute an InfoNCE loss with temperature 0.1 or 0.2. Optimize total_loss = ce_loss + lambda_cpc * contrastive_loss, ramping lambda_cpc from 0.0 to 0.1 or 0.2 after warmup. Keep generation unchanged by using only the original lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss plus validation future-chunk retrieval accuracy. Compare against the baseline using best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, retrieval accuracy, generation repetition or distinct n-gram diagnostics, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: matrix_sam_lm
Title: Matrix-Only Sharpness-Aware Optimization for Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional periodic Sharpness-Aware Minimization mode to the training loop while keeping GPT architecture, batching, evaluation, and generation unchanged. After warmup_iters, every sam_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, replace the normal optimizer step with a two-pass SAM step. First compute the ordinary next-token cross-entropy gradient on the current batch. After unscaling gradients when using fp16, compute the global gradient norm only over matrix-shaped parameters with ndim >= 2, perturb those parameters by epsilon = rho * grad / global_grad_norm, and leave LayerNorm scales and biases unperturbed. Recompute the loss on the same batch at the perturbed weights, restore the original weights, and apply the existing AdamW update using the second gradient. On non-SAM iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Sweep rho values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 with sam_interval values such as 4 and 8. Log ordinary train and validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, gradient norm, estimated sharpness loss increase, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline at equal optimizer steps and, when practical, a compute-matched baseline. Sampling remains unchanged, so any gains reflect improved training dynamics without extra inference cost.

Name: ambiguity_gated_ngram_smoothing
Title: Ambiguity-Gated N-Gram Target Smoothing for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to build sparse suffix-to-next-character count tables for one or two suffix lengths such as 4 and 8, pruning suffixes below a minimum support threshold and storing only compact count distributions. Keep the GPT architecture and generation code unchanged. Add helper functions that, for a sampled subset of batch positions, find the longest supported suffix, compute its empirical next-character distribution, support count, and entropy. In the training loop, always optimize ordinary next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every ngram_interval iterations, add a small auxiliary KL loss from the empirical n-gram distribution to the model distribution only on supported ambiguous contexts, using a gate based on count / (count + tau) and normalized empirical entropy. Ramp lambda_ngram to 0.1 or 0.2. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, plus calibration error, validation loss on high-support ambiguous contexts, train-val gap, and generation diversity diagnostics. Compare against the baseline and uniform label smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, calibration, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: surprise_replay_sampling
Title: Surprise Replay Sampling: Prioritized Training Windows for Efficient Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify get_batch() so it can return the sampled memmap offsets and optionally accept explicit offsets. In the training loop, compute unreduced per-token cross-entropy from the normal logits, average it per sequence window, and insert high-loss window offsets into a bounded replay buffer after warmup_iters. On later iterations, replace a modest fraction of each batch, such as 25%, with offsets sampled from this buffer while keeping the rest uniformly sampled. Use score decay or periodic replacement so stale hard examples do not dominate. Train with the same GPT architecture, standard next-token objective, evaluation, and generation code. Log replay fraction, mean replay-window loss, buffer turnover, and total overhead. Compare against the baseline uniform sampler and a random replay-buffer control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, validation loss on hard-window buckets, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Include small ablations over replay fraction and buffer size.

Name: causal_embedding_mixup
Title: Causal Embedding Mixup for Smooth Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally accept mix_idx and mix_lambda during training. When these are provided, compute token embeddings for idx and mix_idx, mix them per sequence as mix_lambda * emb(idx) + (1 - mix_lambda) * emb(mix_idx), then add the usual positional embeddings and run the transformer normally. Keep the standard integer-token path unchanged for evaluation and generation. In the training loop, always compute the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on the clean batch. After warmup_iters, on a fraction of iterations such as 0.25, shuffle the batch to form paired examples, sample one lambda per sequence from Beta(alpha, alpha) with alpha values such as 0.2 and 0.4, run the mixed forward pass, and compute mixup_loss = lambda * CE(logits_mix, Y) + (1 - lambda) * CE(logits_mix, Y_shuf). Optimize total_loss = clean_loss + lambda_mix * mixup_loss with lambda_mix ramped from 0.0 to 0.2 or 0.3. Extend evaluation to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, plus train-val gap and expected calibration error. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, calibration, total train time, generation samples, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: entropy_gated_smoothing
Title: Entropy-Gated Target Smoothing for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute a smoothed and flattened unigram character distribution, for example q_i proportional to sqrt(freq_i + eps), normalized over the vocabulary. In the training loop, compute unreduced per-token next-token cross-entropy from the logits. After warmup_iters, compute detached normalized predictive entropy for each token position and use batch-relative entropy percentiles to assign a smoothing coefficient: near zero for low-entropy positions and capped at a small value such as 0.05 to 0.15 for the highest-entropy positions. Optimize the convex mixture of the hard target loss and the soft cross-entropy to the fixed flattened unigram distribution, ramping the maximum smoothing coefficient after warmup. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation cross-entropy as the primary metric, expected calibration error, validation loss by predictive-entropy bucket, rare-token validation loss, train-val gap, generated character-frequency KL against validation, repeated-character rate, and distinct n-gram fraction. Compare against the baseline and fixed uniform label smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, calibration, generation diversity, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: surprisal_curriculum_sampling
Title: Surprisal-Curriculum Sampling for Efficient Character-Level Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, build a lightweight backoff character n-gram scorer from train.bin using short suffix lengths such as 1, 2, and 4 with additive smoothing. Score a fixed random pool of valid training offsets by average n-gram surprisal over each block window, then bucket offsets into easy, medium, and hard thirds. Modify get_batch() to optionally sample some examples from these buckets while preserving a uniform-sampling floor for coverage. Use a simple schedule: early training emphasizes easy and medium windows, then anneals toward mostly uniform sampling with a modest hard-window boost after warmup. Keep the GPT architecture, next-token cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and generation unchanged. Extend logging to record bucket mixture weights and sampled difficulty. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss plus validation loss on held-out easy, medium, and hard validation buckets scored with the same fixed n-gram proxy. Compare against the baseline uniform sampler and a shuffled-bucket control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, hard-bucket validation loss, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: hidden_correlation_penalty
Title: Hidden-State Correlation Penalty for Representation Geometry in Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return the final hidden states after ln_f in addition to logits and loss. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy objective unchanged on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every corr_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, flatten the batch-time hidden states, randomly sample at most 1024 vectors, cast them to float32, center and normalize each feature dimension, compute the feature correlation matrix, and add a penalty equal to the mean squared off-diagonal correlation. Ramp lambda_corr from 0.0 to a small value such as 0.005, 0.01, or 0.02 after warmup. Keep generation unchanged. Extend logging and estimate_loss with ordinary train and validation loss, train-val gap, hidden-state off-diagonal correlation, effective rank, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, using validation loss as the primary metric and representation isotropy as the diagnostic.

Name: depth_biased_droppath
Title: Depth-Biased DropPath for Elastic Character-Level Language Models
Experiment: Add a small DropPath helper and modify Block.forward() so the attention and MLP residual updates can be multiplied by a stochastic keep mask and rescaled by 1 / keep_prob during training. Modify GPT.forward() to accept optional droppath_p and max_depth arguments. After warmup_iters, ramp a maximum DropPath probability such as 0.05, 0.10, or 0.20, with lower layers dropped rarely and higher layers dropped more often. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, data loader, and default full-depth generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary full-depth train/validation loss plus validation loss using prefix depths such as 2, 4, and all 6 layers. Benchmark generation at these depths to measure tokens per second and basic sample diagnostics. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best full-depth validation loss, train-val gap, degradation under shallow prefix inference, speed-quality curves, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: detached_kv_recurrence
Title: Detached KV Recurrence for Efficient Long-Context Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend CausalSelfAttention.forward to optionally accept detached past key/value tensors and return current key/value tensors. When past keys are present, concatenate past and current keys/values and use an explicit causal attention mask that lets each current token attend to all cached prefix positions plus causal positions within the current block. Extend GPT.forward with optional past_key_values, return_cache, and position_offset arguments. Increase positional embedding capacity to block_size + max_prefix_len for cache experiments. Modify get_batch() to optionally sample adjacent windows, returning prev_X, X, and Y where prev_X immediately precedes X. During training, use a mixture of ordinary no-cache batches and cached-prefix batches: for cached batches, run prev_X under torch.no_grad() to produce detached per-layer KV caches, then optimize ordinary next-token cross-entropy on X, Y while attending to those caches. Sweep max_prefix_len values such as 0, 64, 128, and 256, with 0 as the baseline, and tune a simple cache training probability such as 0.5. Keep generation unchanged by calling GPT.forward without cached prefix states. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss and adjacent-context validation loss with each prefix length. Compare best ordinary validation loss, cached-context validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, memory overhead, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: position_origin_consistency
Title: Position-Origin Consistency for Origin-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Separate the training sequence length from the model positional capacity: keep train_seq_len at 256, but initialize GPTConfig.block_size to a larger capacity such as 512. Modify get_batch(split, seq_len=256) to sample windows of the requested length. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, pos_offset=0) so positional indices are arange(pos_offset, pos_offset + T), asserting that pos_offset + T <= config.block_size. During training, sample a random valid position offset for the ordinary next-token cross-entropy pass. After warmup_iters, every consistency_interval iterations, run a second forward pass on the same X with a different random offset and add a small ramped KL consistency loss between the two logit distributions using temperature 2.0 and lambda up to 0.1. Keep generation unchanged except that it can use the larger positional capacity. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss at offset 0, mean and standard deviation of validation loss across several random offsets, and offset-consistency KL. Optionally report validation loss for longer sequence lengths such as 384 or 512 as a secondary diagnostic. Compare against the original baseline, an enlarged-position-table baseline without random offsets, and random-offset training without consistency. Use best offset-0 validation loss as the primary metric, with offset sensitivity, consistency KL, total train time, and inference tokens per second as secondary metrics across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: one_step_embedding_adversary
Title: One-Step Adversarial Embedding Regularization for Small Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally accept an embedding_delta tensor that is added to token embeddings after transformer.wte(idx) and before positional embeddings. Keep the default path unchanged for evaluation and generation. In the training loop, compute the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every adv_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, create a small zero or Gaussian initialized perturbation tensor with requires_grad=True for the current token embeddings, run one perturbed forward pass, compute the gradient of the perturbed CE loss with respect to the perturbation, normalize this gradient, and create a detached adversarial embedding_delta with radius epsilon such as 0.01, 0.03, or 0.05. Run one final perturbed forward pass and optimize total_loss = clean_loss + lambda_adv * adv_loss, with lambda_adv ramped from 0.0 to 0.2 after warmup. Add a random Gaussian embedding-noise control using the same perturbation norm but no gradient direction. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary clean train/validation loss, adversarially perturbed validation loss, train-val gap, expected calibration error, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and random-noise control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best clean validation loss as the primary metric.

Name: position_matched_span_order
Title: Position-Matched Span Order Discrimination for Coherence-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small auxiliary binary classifier that takes pooled hidden states from two equal-length spans, using features such as concat(h_a, h_b, h_b - h_a), and predicts whether the second span is the true continuation of the first. In the training loop, always optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every order_interval iterations, sample adjacent span pairs within each training window as positives. Construct hard negatives by keeping the first span fixed and replacing the continuation span with a span from the same relative positions in another batch element, avoiding trivial absolute-position cues. Use span lengths such as 16 or 32 characters and a small ramped auxiliary weight, for example total_loss = lm_loss + lambda_order * order_loss with lambda_order up to 0.05 or 0.1. Keep generation unchanged and ignore the auxiliary classifier at inference. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss plus validation span-continuation accuracy. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, span-continuation accuracy, total train time, generation diversity diagnostics, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: attention_span_curriculum
Title: Attention Span Curriculum for Context-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept an optional attn_span argument. If attn_span is None or greater than or equal to the current sequence length, use the existing full causal attention path. Otherwise, use an explicit banded causal mask so each token attends only to itself and the previous attn_span - 1 tokens; for flash attention, pass this mask through scaled_dot_product_attention rather than using is_causal=True. Propagate attn_span through Block.forward, GPT.forward, and GPT.generate. In the training loop, keep the ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective unchanged, but sample attn_span from values such as [32, 64, 128, 256]. Use a simple curriculum that starts with more probability on short spans and linearly anneals toward mostly full-span attention, ending with full span sampled with high probability such as 0.75. Extend estimate_loss to report validation loss under fixed attention spans 32, 64, 128, and 256, with full-span validation loss as the primary metric. Keep default generation full-context, but optionally benchmark generation quality and tokens per second under fixed attn_span values. Log sampled span, full-span validation loss, mean local-span validation loss, local-to-full degradation, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and context-length dropout to test whether regularizing attention connectivity, while keeping full-length supervision and positional coverage, improves robustness to reduced context access without adding parameters.

Name: attention_head_diversity
Title: Attention Head Diversity Regularization for Small Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to optionally return the per-head attention outputs before concatenation and c_proj, and propagate an optional return_head_outputs flag through Block.forward and GPT.forward. Keep the usual next-token cross-entropy objective as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, every diversity_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, run the normal training forward pass with return_head_outputs=True. For each layer, sample at most 512 batch-time positions from the per-head outputs, flatten each head's sampled vectors, center and L2-normalize them, form the head-by-head similarity matrix, and add a penalty equal to the mean squared off-diagonal similarity. Ramp lambda_head_div from 0.0 to small values such as 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01. On other iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Evaluation and generation use the unchanged ordinary forward path. Log ordinary train/validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, mean inter-head similarity by layer, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 to test whether reducing head redundancy improves generalization without changing inference cost.

Name: dropout_prediction_consistency
Title: Dropout Prediction Consistency for Robust Character-Level Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Modify the training loop so that after warmup_iters, every consistency_interval iterations such as 4, the same batch X, Y is passed through the model twice in training mode with independent dropout masks. Compute ce_loss = 0.5 * CE(logits_a, Y) + 0.5 * CE(logits_b, Y), then add a symmetric softened KL consistency loss between the two predictive distributions using temperature T=2.0, with detached targets in each KL direction and scaling by T * T. Ramp lambda_consistency from 0.0 after warmup to values such as 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2. On non-consistency iterations, train exactly like the baseline with a single forward pass. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary deterministic train/validation loss as the primary metric, plus train-val gap, expected calibration error, and dropout disagreement KL measured from repeated stochastic validation forwards. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best validation loss, calibration, convergence speed, total train time, equal-step performance, and unchanged inference tokens per second. If runtime permits, include a compute-matched control that performs the extra forward pass without the KL term.

Name: learned_soft_attention_spans
Title: Learned Soft Attention Spans for Multi-Scale Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional use_learned_spans flag to GPTConfig and CausalSelfAttention. When enabled, disable the flash attention path for that model and add one learnable span parameter per attention head in each layer. Parameterize tau_h = softplus(raw_tau_h) + 1 and initialize tau_h on a log-spaced range from local to global, for example 8 to block_size across heads. In the manual attention logits, before softmax add a causal distance bias bias[h, i, j] = -(i - j) / tau_h for valid positions i >= j, while keeping future positions masked to -inf. Keep the language modeling objective, optimizer, data loader, generation API, and sampling procedure unchanged. Log ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metrics, plus learned tau_h values by layer, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, with two simple ablations: frozen initialized spans and all heads initialized to the same global span. The hypothesis is that learnable soft locality helps small Transformers allocate heads across local spelling patterns and longer-range structure, improving convergence or validation loss with interpretable head specialization.

Name: gated_local_conv_adapters
Title: Gated Local Convolutional Adapters for Small Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional lightweight local convolution adapter to each transformer Block. Implement a CausalConvAdapter module that applies LayerNorm, left-padded depthwise Conv1d over the sequence dimension, a pointwise Linear projection back to n_embd, and dropout. Add one learnable scalar gate per block initialized to 0.0 so the model begins as an exact baseline and can learn how much local mixing to use. Modify Block.forward to apply the usual attention residual, then x = x + gate * conv_adapter(x), then the usual MLP residual. Add GPTConfig fields use_conv_adapter, conv_kernel_size, and conv_gate_init. Keep the data loader, next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation, and generation API unchanged. Compare the baseline, gated convolution adapters with kernel sizes 3, 5, and 9, and a parameter-matched wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, learned gate values by layer, parameter count, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: causal_latent_registers
Title: Causal Latent Registers for In-Sequence Context Compression
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_registers, register_stride, registers_per_boundary, and prefix_register_control. Keep block_size as the number of real character tokens, but allocate positional embeddings for block_size plus the maximum number of inserted registers. Add a small set of learned register embeddings shared across boundaries. In GPT.forward(), compute token embeddings normally, then either insert register tokens after completed chunks such as every 64 real tokens, excluding the final chunk boundary, or place the same number of registers at the prefix for the control condition. Run the ordinary causal transformer over the augmented sequence, select hidden states corresponding only to real characters, and apply the tied lm_head so the returned logits still have shape batch by real sequence length by vocab size. The standard next-token cross-entropy, evaluation loop, and generation API remain unchanged. Compare the baseline with one shared register every 64 characters, one every 32 characters, and a prefix-register compute control. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, validation loss by distance since the previous register boundary, parameter count, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The key test is whether causal latent scratch slots improve long-context compression without requiring external memory, retrieval, or a changed inference objective.

Name: scheduled_attention_entropy
Title: Scheduled Attention Entropy Floors for Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept optional entropy_regularize and min_entropy_target arguments. When entropy_regularize is false, keep the existing flash-attention path unchanged. When true, use the manual causal attention path, compute attention probabilities, calculate normalized causal entropy per head and token while ignoring early positions with very small attention support, and return a scalar hinge penalty mean(relu(min_entropy_target - normalized_entropy)^2) plus lightweight diagnostics. Propagate the optional entropy penalty through Block.forward and GPT.forward. In the training loop, optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on every iteration; after warmup_iters, every entropy_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, enable entropy_regularize and add lambda_entropy times the accumulated penalty. Ramp lambda_entropy from 0.0 to small values such as 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01, while annealing min_entropy_target from about 0.65 to 0.35 over training. Evaluation and generation use the standard forward path, so parameter count and inference behavior remain unchanged. Extend logging to report ordinary train/validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, mean normalized attention entropy by layer, fraction of heads below the entropy floor, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: memory_neighbor_smoothing
Title: Memory-Bank Hidden-Neighbor Smoothing for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f in addition to logits and loss. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy objective on every iteration. Add a small FIFO memory bank in the training loop that stores detached, L2-normalized hidden states and their true next-character labels from recent batches, capped at a fixed size such as 4096 or 8192 positions. After warmup_iters, every neighbor_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, sample at most 512 current batch-time positions, find their top-k nearest neighbors in the memory bank by cosine similarity, and build a sparse soft target distribution from the neighbors' labels using softmax weights over similarity. Gate the auxiliary KL loss by mean neighbor similarity so low-quality neighborhoods contribute little or nothing, and ramp lambda_neighbor from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1 after warmup. Update the memory bank after the optimization step using detached hidden states from the current batch. Evaluation and generation use the unchanged ordinary forward path. Extend logging and estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation loss, expected calibration error, validation loss by predictive-entropy bucket, neighbor agreement rate, active gate fraction, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and fixed label smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, with calibration and generation diversity as secondary diagnostics.

Name: causal_prefix_thinning
Title: Causal Prefix Thinning for Robust Language Modeling with Sparse Histories
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to accept an optional position_ids argument; when absent, use the existing arange positions so ordinary training, evaluation, and generation are unchanged. After warmup_iters, on a scheduled fraction of training iterations, apply causal prefix thinning: always keep a contiguous recent suffix such as the last 64 or 128 tokens, randomly retain older prefix positions with probability 1 - p where p ramps to values such as 0.05, 0.10, or 0.20, and gather X, Y, and position_ids using one shared sorted index tensor for the whole batch. Mask targets for the thinned older prefix to -1 and compute ordinary cross-entropy only on the intact suffix, so the model predicts from sparse older context plus dense recent context. On non-thinning iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Extend estimate_loss to report clean validation loss plus validation under fixed prefix-thinning probabilities, clean-to-thinned degradation, retained prefix length, and effective supervised tokens. Compare against the baseline and a suffix-only context dropout control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best clean validation loss, robustness to sparse histories, convergence speed, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: capped_landmark_attention
Title: Capped Structural Landmark Attention for Efficient Character-Level Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional sparse attention mode based on structural character landmarks. Extend GPTConfig with use_landmark_attention, local_window, max_landmarks, landmark_token_ids, and random_landmark_control. In train(), after loading meta.pkl, derive landmark_token_ids from available characters such as space, newline, tab, punctuation, brackets, and quotes, then pass them into GPTConfig. Modify GPT.forward() to optionally build a batch-specific causal attention mask from idx: each query may attend to itself, the most recent local_window positions, and at most max_landmarks earlier structural landmark positions, preferring the most recent landmarks before that query. For the random control, replace those structural landmark positions with the same number of randomly selected earlier nonlocal positions per sequence. Propagate the mask through Block.forward into CausalSelfAttention.forward; when a sparse mask is provided, use an explicit masked attention path, while keeping the original full attention path unchanged. Keep the ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, data loader, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare full attention, local-only attention, local-plus-capped-landmark attention, and density-matched local-plus-random attention across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, train loss, effective attention density, local-to-full validation degradation, total train time, inference tokens per second, and generated samples. The key test is whether simple content-derived structural landmarks preserve useful long-range context better than distance-only or random sparse attention at matched sparsity.

Name: stride_conditioned_lm
Title: Stride-Conditioned Language Modeling for Multi-Scale Character Dynamics
Experiment: Modify GPTConfig and GPT to optionally include a learned stride embedding, added alongside token and position embeddings in GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, stride_id=0, position_ids=None). If position_ids is None, keep the current arange positional behavior. Use stride_id=0 for ordinary contiguous training, validation, and generation. In the training loop, always compute the standard next-token cross-entropy on the full contiguous batch. After warmup_iters, every stride_interval iterations such as 4, add an auxiliary compressed-time autoregressive loss for strides 2 and optionally 4. For each stride s, sample a random phase r in [0, s - 1], construct X_s = X[:, r:-s:s] and Y_s = X[:, r + s::s], pass position_ids = arange(r, r + s * X_s.size(1), s), and run model(X_s, Y_s, stride_id=stride_id, position_ids=position_ids). Add the auxiliary losses with a ramped total weight lambda_stride up to 0.1 or 0.25. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric plus stride-2 and stride-4 compressed-time validation losses. Keep sampling unchanged by always using stride_id=0. Compare against the baseline and a control without stride embeddings across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss, strided-view validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, total training time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: gated_suffix_embeddings
Title: Gated Hashed Suffix Embeddings for Tokenizer-Free Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add optional learned suffix embeddings to the input layer of the character-level GPT. Extend GPTConfig with use_suffix_embeddings, suffix_lengths such as [2, 4, 8], suffix_hash_buckets such as 2048 or 4096, and suffix_gate_init. In GPT.__init__, create one nn.Embedding table per suffix length, each with n_embd-dimensional outputs, plus one learned scalar gate per suffix length initialized to 0.0. In GPT.forward(), after computing tok_emb, build causal padded suffix hashes ending at each position using only idx tokens at or before that position, look up each suffix embedding, and add gate_l * suffix_emb_l to tok_emb before adding positional embeddings. Keep the loss, optimizer, batching, evaluation, and generation procedure unchanged. Compare the baseline, suffix lengths [2, 4], suffix lengths [2, 4, 8], and a parameter-matched wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, learned gate values by suffix length, parameter count, total train time, inference tokens per second, rare-token validation loss, and generated samples.

Name: bounded_logit_gradient_reweighting
Title: Bounded Logit-Gradient Reweighting for Efficient Character-Level Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute logits and unreduced per-token cross-entropy instead of relying only on the model-returned mean loss. After warmup_iters, compute a detached per-token logit-gradient proxy g = ||softmax(logits) - one_hot(target)||_2. Convert g into batch-local weights by clipping it to a percentile range such as the 10th to 95th percentiles, normalizing weights to mean 1, and clamping final weights to a conservative range such as [0.5, 2.5]. Optimize a ramped mixture loss = (1 - lambda_grad) * ordinary_ce + lambda_grad * mean(weight * token_ce), with lambda_grad increasing to 0.25 or 0.5. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, validation loss by logit-gradient bucket, expected calibration error, train-val gap, convergence speed, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, raw loss-based weighting, and random normalized weighting across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: internal_speculative_heads
Title: Internal Speculative Heads for Fast Character-Level Decoding
Experiment: Add optional auxiliary future-token heads to GPT for short horizons such as 2, 3, and 4, while keeping the tied lm_head as the primary next-token head. Modify get_batch() to sample block_size + max_horizon tokens and return shifted targets for each horizon. During training, optimize ordinary next-token cross-entropy plus a small ramped auxiliary loss, for example loss = ce_next + lambda_future * mean(ce_h2, ce_h3, ce_h4). Add a generate_speculative() path for deterministic decoding: one forward pass proposes a short chunk using the lm_head for horizon 1 and future heads for later horizons, then one verifier forward over the proposed chunk with the ordinary lm_head accepts the longest prefix whose tokens match the verifier top-1 predictions. If no proposed token is accepted, fall back to ordinary one-token decoding. Keep ordinary generate() unchanged for baseline timing. Evaluate ordinary validation loss, auxiliary horizon accuracy, accepted tokens per verifier pass, fallback rate, sample diagnostics, and greedy decoding tokens per second. Compare baseline GPT, auxiliary heads without speculative decoding, and auxiliary heads with speculative decoding across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: recurrent_depth_sharing
Title: Recurrent Depth Sharing for Parameter-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPTConfig to add n_unique_layers, recurrent_steps, and use_recurrence_step_embedding, while treating n_layer as the effective depth n_unique_layers * recurrent_steps for initialization and reporting. Refactor GPT.__init__ so transformer.h contains only n_unique_layers Blocks. In GPT.forward, repeatedly apply this shared block stack recurrent_steps times, giving the model baseline-like effective depth with fewer unique parameters. If use_recurrence_step_embedding is enabled, add a learned embedding for the current recurrence step to the hidden states before each shared pass. Keep the data loader, next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation procedure unchanged. Compare the standard 6 independent-layer baseline against shared-depth models such as 1 unique layer x 6 steps, 2 x 3, and 3 x 2. Include shallow independent models with the same number of unique layers as parameter controls, and narrower 6-layer independent models with roughly matched parameter counts as architecture controls. Report parameter count, best validation loss, validation loss per million parameters, final train loss, train-val gap, convergence speed, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Ablate recurrence step embeddings to test whether explicit depth identity helps shared blocks specialize across repeated applications.

Name: copy_pointer_auxiliary
Title: Causal Copy-Pointer Auxiliary Supervision for Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add an optional lightweight copy-pointer head to GPT with query and key projections from hidden states plus one learned null key. Keep the ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the main objective. After warmup_iters, every pointer_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, compute pointer labels for a subsampled set of batch positions: for prediction position t, the target is the most recent prefix position p <= t where X[:, p] equals Y[:, t], or a null class if the target character has not appeared in the visible prefix. Score all causal prefix positions with q_t dot k_p, mask invalid future positions, append the null logit, and compute cross-entropy pointer loss. Use a balanced subsample of copyable and null positions, capped at about 512 positions per auxiliary step, and optimize total_loss = lm_loss + lambda_pointer * pointer_loss with lambda_pointer ramped from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1 after warmup. Evaluation and generation use the normal lm_head only. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, pointer accuracy, null accuracy, validation loss on copyable versus novel targets, and validation loss by copy distance bucket. Compare against the baseline and a small parameter-matched control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, with copy-distance robustness, convergence speed, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second as secondary metrics.

Name: positional_extrapolation_biases
Title: Testing Positional Biases for Zero-Shot Context Extrapolation in Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Refactor training to separate train_seq_len from model max_seq_len: train all models on 256-token windows while allowing max_seq_len 512 for extrapolation tests. Modify GPTConfig with position_encoding in {absolute, alibi, learned_relative}. For absolute, keep the current learned wpe path with max_seq_len 512, meaning positions beyond 256 are present but not trained. For alibi, disable wpe and add fixed per-head causal distance biases to attention logits in CausalSelfAttention. For learned_relative, disable wpe and add a clipped per-head relative-distance bias table, with distances beyond the trained range mapped to the largest bucket. Use the manual attention path for bias variants and keep the language modeling objective, optimizer, batching, and generation API otherwise unchanged. Extend get_batch(split, seq_len) and estimate_loss() to report validation loss at context lengths 128, 256, 384, and 512, including both full-window loss and matched suffix loss on the final 256 positions for longer contexts. Compare absolute learned positions, ALiBi, and clipped learned relative bias across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best 256-token validation loss, zero-shot 384/512-token suffix loss, degradation from 256 to 512, parameter count, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: residual_state_vq
Title: Residual State Vector Quantization for Discrete Predictive Bottlenecks in Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional VectorQuantizer module to GPT and insert it after a single intermediate transformer block, for example after block 3 in the 6-layer model. The quantizer maps each batch-time hidden state to the nearest learned codebook vector using squared Euclidean distance, applies a straight-through estimator q_st = h + (q - h).detach(), and returns the standard VQ loss: a codebook loss ||q - stopgrad(h)||^2 plus a commitment loss beta * ||h - stopgrad(q)||^2. Extend GPTConfig with use_state_vq, vq_layer, codebook_size, vq_mix_max, and vq_commitment_weight. Modify GPT.forward() so the selected hidden state is replaced by h + alpha * (q_st - h), where alpha ramps from 0 after warmup_iters to vq_mix_max; this preserves the baseline early in training and gradually introduces the discrete bottleneck. Keep ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary objective and add the VQ loss only during training. Extend logging and estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation loss, validation loss with quantization enabled and disabled, codebook perplexity, dead-code fraction, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline against codebook sizes such as 64, 256, and 1024 with a fixed moderate vq_mix_max such as 0.5, plus a Gaussian hidden-noise control with matched perturbation scale across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The key test is whether a discrete internal predictive-state bottleneck improves generalization or calibration without changing the language modeling objective, tokenizer, data, or generation algorithm.

Name: overlap_window_consistency
Title: Overlap Window Consistency for Boundary-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify get_batch() to optionally return contiguous token chunks of length block_size + max_shift + 1. After warmup_iters, every consistency_interval iterations, sample a shift d from values such as 16, 32, or 64 and construct two overlapping windows from the same chunk: X_a = chunk[:, :block_size], Y_a = chunk[:, 1:block_size + 1], X_b = chunk[:, d:d + block_size], and Y_b = chunk[:, d + 1:d + block_size + 1]. Run the model on both windows. Optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on X_a, Y_a, and add a ramped KL consistency loss from detached logits_a to logits_b for target positions appearing in both windows. Use temperature 2.0, ignore overlap positions where the shifted window has fewer than min_context tokens such as 32 or 64, and use a small maximum consistency weight such as 0.05 to 0.2. On non-consistency iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Keep generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, overlap KL under fixed shifts, validation loss by distance from the left window boundary, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a compute-matched two-window control without the KL term across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: recency_bucket_auxiliary
Title: Recency-Bucket Auxiliary Prediction for Reuse-Aware Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small auxiliary classifier from hidden states to coarse logarithmic recency buckets for the next target token. For each position t, derive the label by finding the most recent visible prefix position p <= t where X[:, p] == Y[:, t], using buckets such as no previous occurrence, distance 1-4, 5-16, 17-64, and 65-255. Keep the ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary objective. After warmup_iters, every recency_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, compute recency labels for the current batch and optimize total_loss = lm_loss + lambda_recency * recency_loss, with class-balanced recency loss and lambda_recency ramped from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1. Evaluation and generation use only the standard lm_head, so inference behavior is unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, macro recency-bucket accuracy, validation loss by recency bucket, and loss on novel versus repeated targets. Compare against the baseline and a shuffled-label auxiliary control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss, repeated-target validation loss, convergence speed, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: identity_biased_attention
Title: Identity-Biased Attention for Token Reuse in Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_identity_attention_bias and identity_bias_init. Modify GPT.forward to pass input token ids into each Block, and modify Block.forward and CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept optional token_ids. When identity bias is enabled, use the manual causal attention path, build a boolean mask where each query token equals an earlier key token in the same sequence, exclude diagonal and future positions, and add a learned per-head scalar times this mask to the attention logits before softmax. Initialize all identity-bias scalars to 0.0 so the model starts equivalent to a manual-attention baseline. Keep the data loader, optimizer, ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the original flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention zero-bias control, learned identity-biased attention, and a shuffled-identity-mask control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, validation loss for repeated versus novel target characters, validation loss by distance to the previous occurrence of the target, learned identity biases by layer and head, attention mass on previous same-token positions, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: residual_ngram_lm
Title: Residual N-Gram Priors for Character-Level Transformer Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to build a frozen smoothed backoff n-gram model over character ids using suffix lengths 1, 2, and 4, pruning low-support contexts to control memory. Add helper functions that map each batch X to dense aligned log-probability tensors log_p_ngram with shape batch by block_size by vocab_size, using the longest supported causal suffix and unigram fallback. Keep the GPT architecture unchanged. In the training loop and estimate_loss, compute logits_gpt as usual but optimize cross-entropy on logits_total = logits_gpt + beta * log_p_ngram, with beta ramped from 0 to 1 after warmup. Also report GPT-only validation loss from logits_gpt, n-gram-only validation loss from log_p_ngram, and fused residual validation loss from logits_total, so improvements can be attributed clearly. Keep ordinary GPT-only generation as the default, with an optional fused-generation diagnostic. Compare baseline GPT, frozen n-gram-only, and residual-fused GPT across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best fused validation loss, GPT-only validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, memory/runtime overhead, and inference tokens per second.

Name: causal_copy_mixture
Title: Causal Copy Mixtures for Reuse-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add GPTConfig fields use_copy_mixture, copy_dim, and copy_gate_init. In GPT.__init__, when enabled, add query and key projections from final hidden states to copy_dim plus a scalar copy gate head initialized with a negative bias so training starts close to the ordinary vocabulary model. In GPT.forward(), compute the usual lm_head logits and vocabulary probabilities. Also compute causal copy scores q_t dot k_p over visible prefix positions p <= t, mask future positions, and softmax over prefix positions. During training, avoid constructing a dense copy vocabulary distribution: compute the copy probability of the true target by summing copy attention mass over prefix positions whose input token equals targets[:, t], then optimize negative log((1 - gate_t) * p_vocab_target + gate_t * copy_prob_target + eps). Keep the ordinary GPT cross-entropy as a diagnostic. In generate(), for the final position only, scatter-add copy attention mass into vocabulary space using the current context token ids and sample from the gated mixture. Extend estimate_loss() to report mixed validation loss, GPT-only validation loss, repeated-target loss, novel-target loss, loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, mean copy gate, copy hit rate, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare baseline GPT, learned causal copy mixture, and a shuffled-prefix copy control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: discounted_successor_auxiliary
Title: Discounted Successor Distributions for Long-Horizon Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add an optional successor_head Linear(n_embd, vocab_size) used only for auxiliary training and diagnostics. Modify get_batch() to optionally sample block_size + successor_horizon + 1 tokens so each training position has future tokens beyond the ordinary next-token target. In the training loop, always optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary objective. After warmup_iters, every successor_interval iterations, build for each position a normalized discounted histogram over future characters at offsets 2 through H+1, using weights gamma^k with H=32 by default and gamma around 0.95. Compute a soft cross-entropy or KL loss from this context-specific future distribution to successor_head(hidden_states), and add it with a small ramped weight such as lambda_successor up to 0.05 or 0.1. Keep generation unchanged by using only the tied lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, successor KL, validation loss at context lengths 64 and 256, generated character-frequency KL against validation, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a unigram label-smoothing control to test whether predicting context-specific discounted successor distributions improves representations beyond generic soft-label regularization.

Name: context_reset_consistency
Title: Context-Reset Consistency for Nonstationarity-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a spliced-batch auxiliary mode after warmup_iters. Sample two independent chunks A and B of length block_size + 1, choose a boundary b such as 64, 128, or 192, and form chunk_splice = concat(A[:, :b], B[:, :block_size + 1 - b]). Set X_splice = chunk_splice[:, :-1] and Y_splice = chunk_splice[:, 1:], masking Y_splice[:, b - 1] = -1 because the first token after the splice is not predictable from the old context. Train the ordinary clean next-token cross-entropy every iteration. On reset_interval iterations, run the model on X_splice and also on the unspliced B prefix; add spliced cross-entropy plus a small ramped KL loss that matches spliced logits after the boundary to detached reset-context logits from B for the first K post-boundary positions. Extend estimate_loss() to report clean validation loss, spliced validation loss, reset-consistency KL, and post-shift recovery loss by distance from the boundary. Compare against the baseline, spliced CE without consistency, and a compute-matched extra-batch control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best clean validation loss, post-shift recovery curves, clean-to-spliced degradation, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: multiscale_ema_memory
Title: Multi-Scale Causal EMA Memory for Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional MultiScaleEMAAdapter inside each transformer Block after self-attention and before the MLP. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects hidden states to a small bottleneck dimension such as n_embd // 4, applies several fixed causal exponential moving-average filters with log-spaced timescales such as 4, 16, 64, and 256 tokens, mixes the filtered states with a linear projection back to n_embd, and adds the result through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero, for example 1e-3. Implement the EMA filters efficiently as normalized causal depthwise Conv1d kernels truncated to the block size, avoiding a Python recurrence in the training loop. Extend GPTConfig with use_ema_memory, ema_bottleneck_mult, ema_timescales, and ema_gate_init. Keep the data loader, ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged. Compare the baseline, fixed-timescale EMA memory, a same-parameter local depthwise-convolution adapter control, and a parameter-matched wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, parameter count, learned gate values by layer, total train time, inference tokens per second, and validation loss by short versus long repeated-token distance buckets.

Name: projected_state_transition
Title: Projected Causal State Transition Prediction for Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a lightweight auxiliary transition module used only during training: a small predictor MLP takes concat(h_t, stopgrad(token_embedding(x_{t+1}))) and predicts a normalized projected representation of h_{t+1}. Use a small projection head for the target state, with the target representation detached to avoid changing the main hidden-state geometry directly. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-token cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every transition_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, run the normal forward pass with return_hidden=True and add a ramped cosine-distance or MSE loss between predicted and detached projected next states for positions 0 through T-2, optionally subsampling positions for speed. Keep evaluation and generation unchanged, using only the standard lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, one-step projected transition error, train-val gap, validation loss at context lengths 64 and 256, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a shuffled-next-token transition control, and a parameter-matched auxiliary MLP control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: lossy_span_context_training
Title: Lossy Span Context Training for Compression-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPT with a learned span_mask_embedding and a small span_summary_proj layer. Modify GPT.forward() to accept an optional lossy_span_ids tensor with shape batch by time, where -1 means normal token and nonnegative ids identify compressed spans within each sequence. After token embedding lookup and before adding positional embeddings, replace embeddings inside each compressed span with either the learned generic span embedding or a projected mean of the original token embeddings from that span, broadcast across the span. In train(), after warmup_iters, on a scheduled fraction of iterations sample a few non-overlapping completed spans from the older prefix while protecting a recent suffix such as the final 64 tokens. Clone Y and set targets inside compressed spans to -1, then optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on the remaining positions. Ramp the corrupted-prefix fraction up to about 0.25 with span lengths sampled from 8, 16, and 32, while keeping clean baseline-style iterations mixed throughout training. Keep generation unchanged by calling forward without lossy_span_ids. Extend estimate_loss() to report clean train/validation loss, validation loss under fixed lossy-span corruption, clean-to-lossy degradation, effective supervised tokens, and inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, independent token masking with the same corrupted-token rate, generic span replacement, and mean-summary span replacement across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best clean validation loss as the primary metric and lossy-context robustness as the main diagnostic.

Name: future_ngram_auxiliary
Title: Future N-Gram Auxiliary Supervision for Tokenizer-Free Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to build a compact vocabulary of frequent future n-grams of length 2 to 6, capped at 1024 or 2048 entries and excluding low-support chunks. Optionally precompute train and validation chunk-label arrays where each position is labeled by the longest frequent n-gram beginning at the next character, with -1 for unsupported positions. Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add an auxiliary chunk_head Linear(n_embd, chunk_vocab_size) used only during training and diagnostics. Modify get_batch() to return ordinary X, Y plus aligned chunk_labels. In the training loop, always optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy; after warmup_iters, every chunk_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, add a ramped auxiliary cross-entropy loss on valid chunk_labels with a small maximum weight such as 0.05 to 0.15. Keep evaluation and generation unchanged by using only the standard lm_head for next-character prediction. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, plus chunk-label accuracy, validation loss on frequent-chunk-start positions versus other positions, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a random chunk-label control with the same label frequency distribution across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: detached_draft_self_conditioning
Title: Detached Draft Self-Conditioning for Iterative Causal Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional second-pass self-conditioning path to GPT. Extend GPTConfig with use_draft_conditioning, draft_temperature, draft_interval, lambda_draft_max, and draft_gate_init. In GPT.__init__, add draft_proj = Linear(n_embd, n_embd) and a learned scalar draft_gate initialized to 0.0. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, draft_logits=None, return_full_logits=False) so the default path is unchanged. When draft_logits is provided, detach it, compute softmax(draft_logits / draft_temperature), form expected next-token embeddings with probs @ transformer.wte.weight.detach(), project them with draft_proj, and add draft_gate * projected_draft_embedding to token embeddings before positional embeddings. In training, always compute the ordinary one-pass next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every draft_interval iterations, run a second refined pass using detached first-pass logits and optimize total_loss = one_pass_loss + lambda_draft * refined_loss, with lambda_draft ramped up to 0.25 or 0.5. Extend estimate_loss to report one-pass validation loss, refined two-pass validation loss, refined-minus-one-pass improvement, and prediction agreement. Keep ordinary generation unchanged, and add an optional refined generation diagnostic that performs one draft pass and one refined pass per generated token.
