Compare against the baseline, a zero-draft adapter control, and a shuffled-draft control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, reporting best validation loss, train time, and one-pass versus refined inference tokens per second.

Name: ephemeral_context_adapters
Title: Ephemeral Context Adapters for Fast Prompt-Level Adaptation in Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to accept an optional context_adapter tensor of shape batch by n_embd. When provided, add adapter_scale * context_adapter to every token embedding before positional embeddings; when absent, keep the forward path unchanged. In the training loop, always optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, every adapt_interval iterations, split each sequence into an adaptation prefix and prediction suffix. Initialize a zero per-sequence adapter with requires_grad=True, compute prefix next-token loss, take one gradient step on only the adapter, optionally clip its norm, detach it, then run the full window again with prefix targets masked to -1 and add a small ramped suffix adaptation loss. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss, unadapted suffix loss, adapted suffix loss after 1 and 3 adapter steps, adaptation gain, and a shuffled-prefix adaptation control. Ordinary generation remains unchanged, with an optional diagnostic that adapts on the prompt before generation. Compare the baseline and adapter-trained model across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best ordinary validation loss, suffix adaptation gain, shuffled-control gap, adaptation overhead, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: free_run_state_alignment
Title: Free-Run State Alignment for Exposure-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Keep the ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective unchanged on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every free_run_interval iterations such as 8 or 16, take a short prefix from the current batch, for example 64 or 128 tokens, and use the current model under torch.no_grad() to sample a short continuation of 32 or 64 tokens. Run the model with return_hidden=True on the real prefix-plus-continuation under torch.no_grad() to compute detached continuation hidden-state means and variances. Then run the model with return_hidden=True on the sampled prefix-plus-continuation, and match only the sampled continuation hidden statistics to the detached real statistics using a lightweight mean-and-variance loss. Optimize total_loss = ce_loss + lambda_free_run * state_alignment_loss, with lambda_free_run ramped from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1 after warmup. Keep standard validation loss and ordinary generation unchanged. Extend diagnostics to report hidden-state drift on validation rollouts, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a compute-matched rollout control without the alignment loss across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: learned_reset_attention
Title: Learned Reset Attention for Segment-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_reset_attention, reset_penalty_scale, reset_gate_bias_init, reset_rate_target, and reset_reg_weight. In CausalSelfAttention, when use_reset_attention is enabled, use the manual attention path and add a small Linear(n_embd, n_head) that predicts sigmoid reset gates for each token and head, with the bias initialized negative so gates start nearly inactive. For each query-key pair, compute the cumulative reset mass between the key position and query position, then subtract reset_penalty_scale times this mass from the causal attention logits before softmax. Add a lightweight budget regularizer reset_reg_weight * (mean_gate - reset_rate_target)^2 to discourage all-zero or all-one gates, and add this scalar to the ordinary next-token cross-entropy during training. Keep batching, optimizer, generation, and primary validation loss unchanged. Log ordinary train/validation loss, best validation loss, mean reset rate by layer/head, attention mass crossing reset barriers, and inference tokens per second. Compare the original flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention no-reset control, learned reset attention, and a density-matched random-reset control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: prefix_time_warp_consistency
Title: Prefix Time-Warp Consistency for Alignment-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, ordinary next-token objective, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged by default. Add a helper that creates X_warp by leaving a recent suffix unchanged, such as the final 96 or 128 tokens, and replacing only the older prefix with a fixed-length monotone resampling of itself. The resampling uses a low edit rate: most source indices advance normally, while occasional stutter steps repeat the previous token and occasional skip steps jump ahead by one token, with indices clipped to remain valid and nondecreasing. In the training loop, always optimize the standard clean cross-entropy on X, Y. After warmup_iters, every warp_interval iterations, run a second forward pass on X_warp and add a ramped KL consistency loss between detached clean logits and warped logits only on the protected suffix, using temperature 2.0 and lambda_warp up to 0.05 or 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary clean train/validation loss as the primary metric, suffix validation loss under fixed prefix warp rates, clean-to-warp degradation, consistency KL, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, with small ablations over warp rate, protected suffix length, stutter-only warps, and skip-only warps.

Name: gated_fast_weight_memory
Title: Gated Fast-Weight Memory for Content-Addressed Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional CausalFastWeightAdapter module inside each transformer Block after the attention residual and before the MLP. Extend GPTConfig with use_fast_weight_memory, fast_weight_dim, and fast_weight_gate_init. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects hidden states to low-dimensional queries, keys, and values, applies a positive feature map such as elu(x)+1 to queries and keys, forms causal cumulative key-value outer products with torch.cumsum, retrieves a normalized memory vector at each position using an epsilon-stabilized denominator, projects it back to n_embd, and adds it through a learned scalar gate initialized to 0.0 so the model starts as the baseline. Keep the data loader, next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation procedure unchanged. Compare the baseline with fast_weight_dim values 8, 16, and 32 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, learned gate values by layer, parameter count, total train time, inference tokens per second, and validation loss on repeated versus novel target characters.

Name: paired_continuation_ranking
Title: Paired Continuation Ranking for Coherence-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, always optimize the ordinary next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every rank_interval iterations, choose a random split boundary b with room for a short continuation window K, such as K=32 or 64. Roll batch elements to create position-matched negatives: each negative sequence keeps prefix_i but replaces the continuation after b with continuation_j from another batch element. Use unreduced log probabilities from the clean forward pass to score each true continuation over target positions b-1 through b+K-2, and run one additional forward pass on the swapped batch to score each mismatched continuation over the same positions. Add a ramped per-example ranking loss such as mean(softplus(score_negative_i - score_positive_i + margin)), where each continuation appears once as matched and once as swapped to reduce suffix-difficulty bias. On non-ranking iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, plus matched-versus-swapped continuation ranking accuracy, average likelihood margin, boundary-window validation loss, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: gradient_alignment_weighting
Title: Gradient-Alignment Token Weighting for Generalization-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f in addition to logits and loss. In train(), sample a small fixed calibration offset pool from train.bin and add a get_batch mode that draws calibration batches from this pool; keep val.bin untouched for evaluation. After warmup_iters, every align_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, run one calibration batch with return_hidden=True under torch.no_grad(), compute the analytic lm_head gradient sketch from hidden states and p - one_hot(target), and update an EMA calibration sketch. On alignment iterations, run the ordinary training batch with return_hidden=True, compute unreduced next-token cross-entropy, compute each token's detached lm_head gradient alignment with the EMA sketch, standardize and clip the alignment scores, then form normalized token weights in a conservative range such as [0.5, 2.0]. Optimize a ramped mixture of ordinary mean CE and alignment-weighted CE, with lambda_align increasing from 0 after warmup to 0.25 or 0.5. On other iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Evaluation and generation remain unchanged. Log ordinary train/validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, mean alignment score, fraction of negative-alignment tokens, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, loss-based token weighting, random shuffled weights with the same distribution, and an ablation without the EMA sketch across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: prefix_sketch_auxiliary
Title: Causal Prefix-Sketch Prediction for Memory-Aware Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add one auxiliary prefix_sketch_head Linear(n_embd, vocab_size), used only during training and diagnostics. Keep ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary objective on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every sketch_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, build a target prefix sketch for each batch position from the visible input tokens X[:, :t+1]: update an exponentially decayed character-count vector count_t = decay * count_{t-1} + one_hot(X[:, t]) with a timescale such as 64, then normalize count_t into a distribution. Run the model with return_hidden=True and add a ramped auxiliary KL loss from the detached prefix-sketch target to log_softmax(prefix_sketch_head(hidden_states)), averaged over batch and time, with lambda_sketch increasing to 0.05 or 0.1. Keep generation unchanged and ignore the sketch head at inference. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, prefix-sketch KL, validation loss at context lengths 64, 128, and 256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and a shuffled-sketch control where sketch targets are permuted across batch elements, testing whether explicit causal memory supervision improves generalization rather than merely adding auxiliary computation.

Name: salience_weighted_summary
Title: Salience-Weighted Causal Summary Adapters for Compact Long-Context Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional SalienceWeightedSummaryAdapter inside each transformer Block after self-attention and before the MLP. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects hidden states to a compact summary dimension, predicts one positive salience weight per position, and uses exclusive causal cumulative sums to form a normalized weighted average of previous compressed states for every token. The summary is projected back to n_embd and added through a learned scalar gate initialized near 0 so the model starts close to the baseline. Extend GPTConfig with use_salience_summary, summary_dim_mult, and summary_gate_init. Keep the data loader, ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and default generation unchanged. Compare the baseline, fixed uniform cumulative summary, learned salience-weighted summary, and a parameter-matched wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, validation loss at context lengths 64, 128, and 256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, salience entropy and gate values by layer, parameter count, total train time, and inference tokens per second. The key test is whether a cheap learned causal compression path helps small Transformers retain useful global context without external memory, auxiliary labels, or changed inference objectives.

Name: causal_prefix_count_adapters
Title: Causal Prefix Count Adapters for Distribution-Shift-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_prefix_count_adapter, count_windows such as [16, 64, 256], count_adapter_dropout, and count_gate_init. Add a PrefixCountAdapter module that converts idx into one-hot token indicators, uses cumulative sums to compute normalized causal character-count histograms over each recent window ending at the current input position, concatenates the multi-scale histograms, projects them with a single Linear layer to n_embd, applies dropout, and adds the result to token embeddings through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero such as 1e-3. Modify GPT.forward() to apply this adapter before positional embeddings when enabled; the loss, optimizer, evaluation loop, and default generation remain unchanged. Compare the baseline, single-window counts, multi-window counts, a shuffled-count control where count features are permuted across batch elements, and a parameter-matched wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss, validation loss for targets seen versus unseen in recent windows, validation loss by local target-frequency bucket, learned gate value, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. The hypothesis is that explicit causal frequency state improves robustness to local nonstationarity and repeated-token prediction without external memory, retrieval, auxiliary labels, or changed supervision.

Name: transition_graph_embedding_prior
Title: Transition-Graph Embedding Priors for Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute smoothed predecessor and successor distributions for every character. Concatenate these distributions into one context vector per character, compute pairwise token similarities, exclude self-neighbors, and keep a top-k row-normalized transition-neighbor graph with a small uniform smoothing floor for stability. Add an embedding_graph_loss helper that L2-normalizes the tied token embedding matrix model.transformer.wte.weight, forms token-token similarity logits divided by a temperature, masks the diagonal, and minimizes KL divergence from the fixed transition graph to the embedding-induced neighbor distribution. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective on every iteration; after warmup_iters, add lambda_graph * embedding_graph_loss every graph_interval iterations, ramping lambda_graph to a small value such as 0.001 to 0.01. Evaluation and generation remain unchanged. Log ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, plus embedding graph KL, rare-token validation loss, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a random-neighbor graph control, and a unigram-frequency-only graph control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, with small ablations over top-k and lambda_graph.

Name: content_adaptive_span_bias
Title: Content-Adaptive Span Biases for Learned Context Allocation in Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_content_adaptive_span_bias, span_min, span_max, span_budget_target, span_budget_weight, and span_init_frac. In CausalSelfAttention, when enabled, use the manual causal attention path and add a small Linear(n_embd, n_head) that predicts one bounded span for each query token and head: span = span_min + (span_max - span_min) * sigmoid(logit). Initialize the predictor bias so spans start near span_max, making the model initially close to full-context attention. Add a causal distance bias to attention logits, -(query_position - key_position) / span, before softmax while preserving the future mask. Return diagnostics such as mean predicted span, mean attention distance, and span by layer/head. After warmup_iters, optionally add a ramped budget penalty such as span_budget_weight * relu(mean_span / span_max - span_budget_target)^2, so ablations can test different average context budgets without forcing collapse to purely local attention. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy objective, data loader, optimizer, evaluation, and generation interface otherwise unchanged. Compare the flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention no-bias control, static learned per-head spans, adaptive spans without a budget penalty, and adaptive spans with target budgets such as 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, train-val gap, validation loss at context lengths 64 and 256, mean span by layer/head, span usage for repeated versus novel target characters, total train time, and inference tokens per second. The goal is to test whether small transformers can learn interpretable, data-dependent context allocation without external memory, auxiliary labels, or changed supervision.

Name: late_swa_flatness
Title: Late-Phase SWA Consistency for Flat Character Language Models
Experiment: Train the GPT normally until a late start point such as 70% of max_iters. At swa_start, create a detached SWA copy of the uncompiled model. Every swa_update_interval steps, update the SWA model by equal-weight averaging with the current student weights. Keep the standard next-token cross-entropy on every iteration. After the SWA model has accumulated at least two snapshots, every consistency_interval iterations run the SWA model in eval mode under torch.no_grad() on the same batch and add a small KL loss from the detached SWA predictive distribution to the student logits using temperature 2.0, with lambda_swa ramped to 0.05 or 0.1. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss for both the student and SWA model, student-SWA prediction KL, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Add a simple final flatness diagnostic by evaluating validation loss at a few linear interpolations between student and SWA weights. Compare baseline training, SWA evaluation only, and SWA plus consistency across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged and uses either the student or SWA model as a drop-in final model.

Name: position_scale_consistency
Title: Position-Scale Consistency for Length-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Separate supervised sequence length from positional capacity: keep training windows at 256 tokens but initialize GPTConfig.block_size to 512. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, position_ids=None) so the default path uses ordinary dense positions arange(T), while optional position_ids index the learned position embeddings. Train with standard next-token cross-entropy on dense positions every iteration. After warmup_iters, every scale_interval iterations, sample a scale from values such as 1.25, 1.5, and 2.0, build strictly increasing integer position_ids = floor(scale * arange(T)), and run a second forward pass on the same X and Y. Add a small ramped auxiliary loss on the scaled-position pass: scaled next-token cross-entropy plus a temperature-2.0 KL consistency term from detached dense-position logits to scaled-position logits, with total auxiliary weight up to 0.05 or 0.1. Extend get_batch(split, seq_len) and estimate_loss() to report validation loss at context lengths 128, 256, 384, and 512, including suffix-only loss on the final 256 positions for longer contexts. Compare the original 256-position baseline, a 512-position learned-position baseline without dilation, and position-scale consistency across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best 256-token validation loss, 384/512-token extrapolation loss, degradation from 256 to 512, dense-to-scaled prediction KL, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Generation remains unchanged except that the trained model can use the expanded positional table for longer contexts.

Name: token_routed_adapters
Title: Token-Routed Low-Rank Adapters for Conditional Capacity in Character Language Models
Experiment: Add an optional TokenRoutedAdapter module inside each transformer Block after the attention residual and before the MLP. Extend GPTConfig with use_routed_adapters, num_adapter_experts, adapter_rank, adapter_gate_init, router_temperature, and router_balance_weight. The adapter applies LayerNorm, computes per-token router logits, forms a softmax over a small number of low-rank experts, and returns the weighted sum of expert outputs. Each expert is Linear(n_embd, adapter_rank) -> GELU -> Linear(adapter_rank, n_embd). Add the routed output as a residual branch through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero, such as 1e-3, so training starts close to the baseline while expert gradients are active. Train with the ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective, optionally adding a small batch-level load-balancing loss after warmup that encourages the mean router distribution to use all experts without forcing high entropy at every token. Keep the data loader, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the baseline, routed adapters with 2 and 4 experts, a single dense low-rank adapter with matched parameters, and a modest wider baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, parameter count, total train time, inference tokens per second, learned gate values by layer, router usage entropy, expert usage by character class, and validation loss broken down by rare versus common targets and repeated versus novel targets.

Name: self_rollout_unlikelihood
Title: Self-Rollout Unlikelihood for Degeneration-Resistant Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, standard next-token cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and default generation API unchanged. After warmup_iters, every rollout_interval iterations such as 16, temporarily run the model in eval mode under torch.no_grad() on a small subset of the current batch, for example 4 to 8 prefixes of length 128, and sample continuations of 32 to 64 characters. Switch back to train mode and feed each detached prefix-plus-rollout sequence through the model in one teacher-forced pass. Add a simple helper that marks only generated continuation tokens that complete a recently repeated 3-gram or 4-gram loop inside the generated continuation, optionally also marking immediate character runs longer than a conservative threshold. Ignore repeated patterns that occur only in the real prefix, and cap the number of marked positions per rollout batch. For marked positions, add an auxiliary unlikelihood loss -log(1 - p_bad + eps), where p_bad is the model probability of the sampled degenerate token at that position, with lambda_ul ramped from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1 after warmup. On non-rollout iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Add fixed validation-prefix rollout diagnostics reporting repeated n-gram rate, distinct n-gram fraction, marked bad-event rate, ordinary train and validation loss, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a random-negative unlikelihood control with the same number of marked positions, and a compute-matched rollout control without the unlikelihood loss across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: future_spectral_sketch
Title: Future Spectral Sketch Prediction for Multi-Scale Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add an auxiliary spectral_head MLP that maps each hidden state to K * D outputs, using concrete defaults such as spectral_horizon H=32, num_spectral_coeffs K=4, and token_sketch_dim D=32. Modify get_batch() so auxiliary iterations sample block_size + H + 1 contiguous tokens, while still returning the ordinary X and Y for next-token language modeling. After loading the dataset vocabulary size, create a fixed non-trainable random projection table from token ids to normalized D-dimensional token sketch vectors, and create a fixed low-frequency DCT basis over future offsets 1 through H. After warmup_iters, every spectral_interval iterations, run the model with return_hidden=True and build spectral targets by projecting each position's next H tokens through the sketch table and summing them against the first K DCT basis vectors. Train with the ordinary next-token cross-entropy on every iteration, and on spectral iterations add a ramped auxiliary MSE loss between spectral_head(hidden_states) and detached spectral targets, with lambda_spectral up to 0.05 or 0.1. Keep evaluation and generation using only the standard lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, spectral prediction error on validation chunks, repeated n-gram rate, distinct n-gram fraction, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a shuffled-future spectral target control, and a random-target auxiliary control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: td_belief_heads
Title: Temporal-Difference Belief Heads for Predictive-State Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states and auxiliary belief-head logits for future horizons such as 2, 4, and 8. Keep the ordinary tied lm_head and next-token cross-entropy unchanged as the primary objective. On auxiliary iterations after warmup_iters, run the usual forward pass once, then train each horizon head at position t to match the detached ordinary lm_head distribution at position t + h - 1, since that later state predicts the same token after observing the intervening ground-truth context. Use temperature-scaled KL divergence with T around 2.0, valid only where t + h - 1 is inside the block, and ramp lambda_td from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1. Evaluation and generation ignore the auxiliary heads and use the standard lm_head path unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, TD KL by horizon, horizon-head accuracy diagnostics, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare baseline GPT, hard future-token auxiliary heads, TD belief heads, and a shuffled-later-logits control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: ecoc_partition_loss
Title: Error-Correcting Partition Losses for Dense Character-Level Supervision
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged. After loading each dataset's vocab_size, create a fixed deterministic balanced binary codebook C of shape vocab_size by code_dim, with entries in {-1, 1} and code_dim values such as 16, 32, and 64. In the training loop, compute the ordinary next-character cross-entropy from logits as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, compute probs = softmax(logits), then for each code bit compute the model probability mass assigned to the target token's side of that binary partition. Add a ramped auxiliary binary cross-entropy loss that encourages high probability mass on the correct side of each partition, with lambda_code values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. This provides dense output supervision without adding parameters or changing inference. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, partition loss, expected calibration error, rare-token validation loss, and generated character-frequency KL. Compare against the baseline, uniform label smoothing, shuffled-code partitions, and random normalized token-weighting controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: midlayer_prefix_pooling
Title: Mid-Layer Prefix Pooling for Compressible Autoregressive Contexts
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return hidden states after a chosen merge_layer and to optionally continue computation from a provided hidden sequence through the remaining transformer blocks. On auxiliary iterations after warmup_iters, run the normal full-context forward pass, take the merge_layer hidden states, split them into an older prefix and a protected recent suffix such as the final 128 tokens, mean-pool the older prefix into causal chunks with stride 4 or 8, concatenate the pooled prefix summaries with the intact suffix hidden states, and run the remaining blocks on this shorter sequence. Compute logits only for suffix positions. Train every iteration with ordinary full-context next-token cross-entropy, and on compression_interval iterations add a small ramped auxiliary loss combining suffix cross-entropy and temperature-2.0 KL consistency from detached full-context suffix logits to compressed-path suffix logits. Keep ordinary generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report standard validation loss, compressed-suffix validation loss, full-to-compressed KL, suffix loss by distance from the compression boundary, upper-layer sequence-length reduction, total train time, and ordinary inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a suffix-only control with no pooled prefix summaries, and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: angular_margin_auxiliary
Title: Angular-Margin Auxiliary Regularization for Tied Output Embeddings
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, batching, ordinary evaluation, and generation API unchanged. Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a cosine_classifier_loss helper that L2-normalizes hidden states and the tied output embedding matrix model.transformer.wte.weight, multiplies their dot products by a fixed scale such as 16 or 32, subtracts a small margin from the target token's cosine logit, and computes cross-entropy with ignore_index=-1. During training, always optimize the standard next-token cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, add lambda_margin * cosine_margin_loss with lambda_margin ramped to 0.1 or 0.25 and margin values such as 0.05, 0.10, and 0.20. Evaluation and generation continue to use the original lm_head logits, so inference cost and sampling behavior are unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, cosine-classifier validation loss, rare-token versus common-token validation loss, expected calibration error, output-embedding norm statistics, and mean pairwise embedding cosine similarity. Compare against the baseline and a cosine no-margin auxiliary control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: surprisal_feedback_lm
Title: Causal Surprisal Feedback for Prediction-Error-Aware Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_surprisal_feedback, surprisal_gate_init, surprisal_clip, feedback_interval, and lambda_feedback_max. In GPT.__init__, add a Linear(1, n_embd) surprisal_proj and a learned scalar gate initialized near zero. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, surprisal_values=None) so the default path is unchanged, but when surprisal_values is provided it adds gate * surprisal_proj(surprisal_values.unsqueeze(-1)) to token embeddings before positional embeddings. In the training loop, always compute the ordinary clean next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every feedback_interval iterations, compute detached previous-token surprisal from the clean logits aligned to input positions: surprisal[:, 0] = 0 and surprisal[:, 1:] = -log p_clean(X[:, 1:] | X[:, :-1]). Clamp and normalize these values, run one feedback-conditioned second forward pass on the same X and Y, and optimize total_loss = clean_loss + lambda_feedback * feedback_loss with lambda_feedback ramped up to 0.25. Add one shuffled-surprisal control that permutes surprisal_values across batch elements before the second pass. Extend estimate_loss() to report clean train/validation loss, feedback-conditioned train/validation loss as the main augmented-model metric, validation loss binned by previous-token surprisal, clean-to-feedback KL, learned feedback gate value, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Optionally add generate_with_surprisal_feedback() that updates the scalar feedback after each generated token while keeping ordinary generate() unchanged. Compare baseline, true surprisal feedback, and shuffled-surprisal feedback across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: transition_cluster_curriculum
Title: Transition-Cluster Curricula for Coarse-to-Fine Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute smoothed predecessor and successor distributions for every token id. Concatenate these transition fingerprints with normalized log frequency, L2-normalize the features, and run deterministic numpy k-means to assign tokens to a modest number of clusters such as min(16, vocab_size). Add cluster_marginal_ce(logits, targets, token_to_cluster, num_clusters), which computes cluster log probabilities by logsumexp over vocabulary logits within each cluster minus the global logsumexp, then applies cross-entropy to the target token's cluster with ignore_index support. Keep the GPT architecture, batching, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, always compute ordinary next-token cross-entropy and add a decaying auxiliary term loss = token_ce + lambda_cluster(t) * cluster_ce, where lambda_cluster starts around 0.3 after warmup and decays to 0.0 or 0.05 by the end of training. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, plus cluster validation loss, cluster accuracy, validation loss by target-frequency bucket, expected calibration error, and train-val gap. Compare the baseline, transition-cluster curriculum, frequency-only clusters, and random balanced clusters across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best ordinary validation loss, convergence speed, calibration, rare-token loss, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: suffix_state_convergence
Title: Suffix-State Convergence for Prefix-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Keep ordinary next-token cross-entropy training unchanged on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every convergence_interval iterations, construct a prefix-replaced view of the current batch by swapping only the older prefix across batch elements while keeping a shared recent suffix of length S, such as 64 or 128, unchanged. Run the clean and prefix-replaced batches with return_hidden=True. Add a small ramped auxiliary loss on the later part of the shared suffix, after a burn-in of 16 or 32 tokens, that encourages normalized hidden states from matched-suffix pairs to be closer than hidden states from unrelated shuffled suffix pairs by a margin. Use detached targets for one branch or a symmetric stop-gradient formulation, and keep the ordinary LM loss as the dominant objective. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, suffix-state convergence distance under prefix replacement, matched-versus-random state margin, validation loss after random prefix replacement, loss by distance into the shared suffix, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, absolute hidden-state consistency, and a random-pair consistency control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The goal is to test whether encouraging predictive states to become prefix-invariant after enough shared recent context improves boundary robustness and generalization without changing generation or adding inference-time cost.

Name: dual_mode_span_infilling
Title: Dual-Mode Span Infilling for Representation-Rich Causal Character Models
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward, Block.forward, and GPT.forward to accept a causal flag. When causal=True, preserve the existing autoregressive path used for training evaluation and generation. When causal=False, use full bidirectional self-attention. Add a learned mask_embedding and a learned two-entry mode embedding to GPT, with mode 0 for causal language modeling and mode 1 for span infilling. In GPT.forward, optionally accept input_mask; masked token embeddings are replaced by mask_embedding before adding positional and mode embeddings. During training, always compute the ordinary next-character cross-entropy on X, Y with causal=True and mode_id=0. After warmup_iters, every infill_interval iterations, sample random contiguous spans in X with total mask rate around 0.10 to 0.20 and span lengths 2 to 8, run the model with causal=False and mode_id=1, and compute infill_loss only on the masked original input tokens, using -1 elsewhere. Optimize total_loss = lm_loss + lambda_infill * infill_loss, ramping lambda_infill to 0.1 or 0.25. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary causal train and validation loss as the primary metrics, plus bidirectional infilling loss and masked-input causal validation loss as diagnostics. Compare against the baseline and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation always uses causal=True and mode_id=0, so decoding behavior is unchanged except for any representation gains learned during training.

Name: slimmable_width_lm
Title: Slimmable Width Training for Anytime Character Language Models
Experiment: Add optional width controls so one GPT can run at several nested compute budgets while the default forward path remains unchanged. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept active_heads; when active_heads < n_head, compute q, k, and v only for the first active_heads heads using sliced c_attn weights, run causal attention on those heads, and project back to n_embd using the matching sliced input columns of c_proj. Modify MLP.forward to accept active_mlp_frac and use only the first active hidden channels of the 4 * n_embd expansion with sliced c_fc and c_proj weights. Propagate width_config through Block.forward, GPT.forward, and GPT.generate. During training, always optimize ordinary full-width next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every width_interval iterations, run one additional narrow-width pass on the same batch using fixed budgets such as 4/6 heads with 0.75 MLP width and 3/6 heads with 0.5 MLP width, adding a small ramped auxiliary loss combining narrow cross-entropy with temperature-2 KL distillation from detached full-width logits. Extend estimate_loss to report validation loss at each width budget, full-width loss as the primary metric, narrow-to-full degradation, and train-val gap. Benchmark generation tokens per second at each width budget. Compare normal training with post-hoc width truncation, slimmable CE-only training, and slimmable training with full-to-narrow distillation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using full-width validation loss, width-speed-quality Pareto curves, total train time, and inference throughput.

Name: latent_pause_suffix_compute
Title: Latent Pause Suffix Compute for Test-Time Scaling in Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_pause_tokens, max_pause_tokens, and pause_context_len. Add learned pause embeddings to GPT. Keep the default GPT.forward(idx, targets=None) path unchanged. Add an optional paused forward path, for example GPT.forward_with_pauses(idx, targets, num_pause_tokens), that takes only the most recent pause_context_len tokens, interleaves P learned latent pause embeddings after each real token, runs the existing causal transformer over the expanded sequence, selects the last pause state after each real token, and applies the tied lm_head to predict the ordinary next-character targets. No loss is computed on pause tokens themselves. Increase positional embedding capacity to cover pause_context_len * (1 + max_pause_tokens). In the training loop, always optimize the standard full-context next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every pause_interval iterations, add a small ramped auxiliary paused suffix loss, primarily with P=1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary full-context validation loss and matched suffix validation losses for P=0, P=1, and optionally P=2. Modify generate to optionally use the paused suffix path before sampling each next real character, while leaving ordinary generation unchanged. Compare the baseline, a pause-trained model, and a compute-matched extra suffix-loss control without pause tokens across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using full-context validation loss, paused suffix loss, total train time, and generation tokens per second at each pause budget.

Name: compressed_span_prefixes
Title: Compressed Span Prefixes for Variable-Rate Character Context Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to build a compact vocabulary of frequent token-id spans of length 2 to 8, capped at 512 or 1024 entries and filtered by minimum support. Extend GPTConfig with use_span_prefix_compression, span_vocab_size, span_prefix_len, protected_suffix_len, and span_gate_init. Add a learned span embedding table and scalar gate to GPT, and refactor GPT.forward to optionally accept inputs_embeds and position_ids while keeping the ordinary idx path unchanged. During normal iterations, train exactly as the baseline with standard character-level next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every span_interval iterations, split each batch into an older prefix and an uncompressed protected suffix. Greedily replace non-overlapping frequent spans only inside the older prefix with span embeddings, keep suffix characters as ordinary token embeddings, assign each compressed span the original position id of its final character, right-pad compressed examples after all valid tokens, and set targets to -1 for compressed-prefix tokens and pads. Compute auxiliary cross-entropy only on suffix targets, optionally adding a small temperature-2 KL consistency loss from detached full-context suffix logits to compressed-prefix suffix logits with a ramped weight up to 0.1 or 0.25. Keep standard evaluation and generation unchanged, and log compressed-prefix validation loss, suffix loss, compression ratio, frequent-span coverage, train-val gap, total train time, and ordinary inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, compressed frequent-span prefixes, random-span compression with matched compression ratio, and a suffix-only context control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: coarse_char_auxiliary
Title: Coarse Character Auxiliary Prediction for Representation-Shaped Language Modeling
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute a transition fingerprint for each character token by concatenating normalized predecessor counts, normalized successor counts, and log frequency. Cluster these fingerprints deterministically with numpy k-means into a small number of coarse character classes such as 8, 16, or min(32, vocab_size). Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add a small cluster_head Linear(n_embd, num_char_clusters) used only during training and diagnostics. Keep the ordinary tied lm_head and next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective. After warmup_iters, add a ramped auxiliary cross-entropy from cluster_head(hidden_states) to the cluster id of each next-character target, with ignore_index support and lambda_cluster values such as 0.05, 0.1, and 0.2. Evaluation and generation use only the original lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, coarse-cluster accuracy, validation loss by cluster, rare-token validation loss, expected calibration error, and train-val gap. Compare against the baseline, random balanced clusters, and frequency-only clusters across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, using best ordinary validation loss as the primary metric.

Name: evidence_calibrated_distillation
Title: Evidence-Calibrated Distillation for Short-Context Robust Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, ordinary full-context next-token cross-entropy, evaluation path, and default generation unchanged. In the training loop, compute the standard full-context logits and loss on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every distill_interval iterations, take a fixed limited-context suffix of the same batch, for example X_short = X[:, -64:] and Y_short = Y[:, -64:], and run one extra forward pass. Align full-context logits to the same suffix positions. Using detached logits, compute unreduced target losses for both views and define evidence_gain = clamp(short_ce - full_ce, min=0). Convert this to a bounded gate, such as gate = clamp(evidence_gain / gain_scale, 0, 1). Add a ramped auxiliary loss: gate-weighted temperature-2 KL from detached full-context logits to short-context logits, plus a low-gate overconfidence penalty (1 - gate) * relu(full_entropy - short_entropy)^2. On non-distillation iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, validation loss at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, expected calibration error at each context length, mean evidence gain, and short-context overconfidence gap. Compare against the baseline, ungated short-context distillation, and entropy-only regularization across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best full-context validation loss, short-context degradation, calibration, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: detached_context_router
Title: Detached Context Routing for Efficient Adaptive-Window Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a lightweight context_router head to GPT that maps the final hidden state from a short suffix context to logits over candidate context lengths such as 32, 64, 128, and 256. Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states. Train the base language model exactly as before with ordinary full-context next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every router_interval iterations, run no-grad forward passes on the same batch sliced to the candidate suffix lengths and compare each candidate's final-token prediction to the full 256-context prediction using excess target loss or KL divergence. Assign each sequence an oracle label equal to the shortest context whose regret is below a fixed threshold, otherwise 256. Train only the router head from the detached 32-context final hidden state using cross-entropy, so router learning does not alter the LM representations. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary full-context validation loss, fixed-context final-token losses, oracle adaptive-context loss, predicted adaptive-context loss, router accuracy, long-context recall, and mean selected context length. Add generate_adaptive_context() that first evaluates the last 32 tokens, uses the router to select a context length, reuses the 32-token logits if selected, otherwise reruns with the selected longer suffix before sampling. Compare full-context generation, fixed short-context generation, entropy-threshold routing, random budget-matched routing, and learned detached routing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using validation loss, generation tokens per second, mean processed context length, and speed-quality tradeoff curves.

Name: boundary_age_embeddings
Title: Causal Boundary-Age Embeddings for Tokenizer-Free Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_boundary_age_embeddings, boundary_age_num_buckets, boundary_age_gate_init, and boundary_token_ids. In train(), after loading meta.pkl, derive at most two simple boundary classes from characters present in the dataset: separators such as space, newline, and tab, and punctuation such as period, comma, colon, semicolon, quotes, brackets, question marks, and exclamation marks. Skip any unavailable class. In GPT.__init__, add a compact learned boundary-age embedding table for each active class and one learned scalar gate per class initialized near zero. Modify GPT.forward() so that, when enabled, it computes the causal distance from each position to the most recent earlier-or-current token in each boundary class using vectorized cumulative maxima, maps distances into capped logarithmic buckets, sums the gated boundary-age embeddings, and adds them to token embeddings before positional embeddings. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the baseline, boundary-age embeddings, a frequency-matched random-boundary control, and a separator-only ablation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, validation loss by distance-to-boundary bucket, learned gate values, total train time, and inference tokens per second. The key test is whether lightweight causal structural coordinates improve tokenizer-free language modeling without external data, auxiliary labels, sparse attention, or changed supervision.

Name: residual_positional_clock
Title: Residual Positional Clocks for Content-Adaptive Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_residual_positional_clock, pos_capacity, clock_delta_range, clock_gate_init, and clock_reg_weight. Keep the supervised training sequence length at 256 and use pos_capacity equal to 256 by default, with an optional 512-capacity diagnostic run. In GPT.__init__, add a lightweight clock_proj Linear(n_embd, 1), initialize its weights and bias to zero, and add one learned scalar clock_gate initialized so the residual clock path starts inactive. In GPT.forward(), compute token embeddings normally, predict bounded causal increments delta_t = 1 + clock_delta_range * tanh(clock_proj(tok_emb)), define learned positions with learned_pos[:, 0] = 0 and learned_pos[:, t] = sum_{i < t} delta_i, then mix them with ordinary positions as mixed_pos = arange(T) + sigmoid(clock_gate) * (learned_pos - arange(T)). Add a helper that linearly interpolates the learned position embedding table at fractional mixed_pos values, clamping to the valid range. Train with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective and, after warmup_iters, add a small regularizer penalizing mean(delta_t) deviating from 1 and excessive variance in delta_t. Evaluation and generation use the same learned-clock path when enabled, with no auxiliary heads or changed sampling objective. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss at context length 256, validation losses at context lengths 64 and 128, clock gate value, mean and standard deviation of learned increments, and simple increment statistics for whitespace, punctuation, and other characters. Compare the original baseline, a zero-gate clock control, residual positional clocks, and a shuffled-delta control where predicted increments are permuted across batch elements before integration. Report best validation loss, short-context robustness, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: future_softlabel_distillation
Title: Future-Softlabel Distillation for Privileged-Context Autoregressive Learning
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig and GPT with an optional learned two-entry direction embedding added to token and position embeddings in GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, direction_id=0). Use direction_id=0 for ordinary left-to-right training, validation, and generation. In the training loop, always compute the standard forward next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every distill_interval iterations, reconstruct each contiguous chunk as torch.cat([X[:, :1], Y], dim=1), reverse it, and run a reverse causal pass with direction_id=1 using X_rev = reversed_chunk[:, :-1] and Y_rev = reversed_chunk[:, 1:]. Add a small ramped reverse cross-entropy loss so the reverse direction becomes a competent privileged teacher. Align detached reverse logits to forward target positions with reverse_logits[:, :block_size - 1, :].flip(1), matching forward_logits[:, :block_size - 1, :] and Y[:, :block_size - 1]. Add a temperature-scaled KL distillation loss from softmax(aligned_reverse_logits / T) to log_softmax(aligned_forward_logits / T), multiplied by T * T, with T=2.0 and lambda_future ramped to about 0.05 to 0.15. Keep the final forward position trained only by ordinary CE because it has no right-context teacher. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary forward train/validation loss as the primary metric, reverse validation loss, future-distillation KL, train-val gap, and expected calibration error. Compare the baseline, reverse-auxiliary-only, future-softlabel distillation, and a shuffled reverse-alignment control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged and always uses direction_id=0, so inference throughput should be essentially unchanged.

Name: midlayer_state_jitter
Title: Mid-Layer State Jitter Consistency for Robust Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to accept optional hidden_jitter_layer and hidden_jitter_scale arguments. During the transformer block loop, if hidden_jitter_layer matches the current layer and the model is training, add Gaussian noise after that block with standard deviation hidden_jitter_scale times the detached RMS of the hidden state. Keep ordinary next-token cross-entropy training unchanged on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every jitter_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, run the normal clean forward pass to get logits and CE loss, then run one additional jittered forward pass on the same X and Y. Add a ramped temperature-2 KL consistency loss from detached clean logits to jittered logits, optionally applying the KL only to positions whose clean predictive entropy is below the batch median. Use a middle layer such as layer 3 in the 6-layer model, hidden_jitter_scale values such as 0.01, 0.03, and 0.05, and lambda_jitter up to 0.05 or 0.1. Evaluation and generation use the normal unjittered forward path. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, validation KL under hidden-state jitter, jittered validation loss, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, ungated jitter consistency, and an input-embedding noise control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: transition_affinity_attention
Title: Transition-Affinity Attention Biases for Tokenizer-Free Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute smoothed predecessor and successor distributions for every character token. Concatenate each token's predecessor distribution, successor distribution, and normalized log frequency into a transition fingerprint, L2-normalize the fingerprints, compute a vocab-by-vocab cosine affinity matrix, clamp negative affinities to zero, and keep only the top-k neighbors per token. Extend GPTConfig with use_transition_affinity_attention, affinity_topk, affinity_bias_max, and affinity_bias_init. Register the fixed affinity matrix as a non-trainable buffer in GPT, pass idx through GPT.forward into each Block and CausalSelfAttention, and when enabled use the manual attention path with an added logit bias scale_h * affinity[idx_query, idx_key] for each head, where scale_h = affinity_bias_max * tanh(raw_scale_h). Initialize raw_scale_h to 0.0 so the model starts as a manual-attention baseline. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, batching, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the original flash-attention baseline, manual-attention zero-bias control, transition-affinity attention, shuffled-affinity control, and identity-only attention bias across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, validation loss on repeated versus novel targets, validation loss by previous-occurrence distance, learned affinity scales by layer and head, attention mass on high-affinity prior positions, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: counterfactual_span_attention
Title: Counterfactual Span Attention Alignment for Causal Context Use
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward, Block.forward, and GPT.forward to optionally return attention probabilities on auxiliary iterations, using the manual attention path only when attention maps are requested and leaving the default flash-attention path unchanged. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every align_interval iterations, divide each input window into coarse prefix spans such as 16-token chunks and reserve a protected suffix such as the final 64 tokens as query positions. Name: causal_window_renorm
Title: Causal Window Renormalization for Nonstationary Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional CausalWindowRenorm adapter inside each transformer Block after the attention residual and before the MLP. The adapter computes feature-wise causal running mean and variance over a bounded recent window such as 64 or 128 tokens using torch.cumsum, forms normalized deviations z_t = (x_t - mean_window_t) / sqrt(var_window_t + eps), optionally detaches the statistics for stability, projects z_t back to n_embd with a Linear layer, applies dropout, and adds the result through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero. Extend GPTConfig with use_window_renorm, renorm_window_size, renorm_gate_init, renorm_eps, and detach_renorm_stats. Name: kv_state_quant_consistency

Experiment: Add a fake_quantize_kv helper that performs symmetric straight-through fake quantization with one scale per batch element and attention head. Name: attention_salience_erasure

Name: role_factorized_output_embeddings
Title: Role-Factorized Output Embeddings for Asymmetric Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT so the tied output matrix can optionally be relaxed by a small low-rank residual: W_out = W_token + scale * A @ B, where W_token is transformer.wte.weight. Initialize A randomly, B to zeros, and scale to a small nonzero value so the model starts exactly as the tied baseline while gradients can still enter the residual branch. Add GPTConfig fields use_role_factorized_output, output_residual_rank, output_residual_scale_init, and output_residual_l2. Name: information_budgeted_updates
Title: Information-Budgeted Predictive Updates for Stable Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute the ordinary next-token cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, add a no-extra-forward predictive update penalty from the same logits. Let p_prev be the detached predictive distribution from logits[:, :-1] before observing X[:, 1:], and let p_cur be the predictive distribution from logits[:, 1:] after observing those tokens. Compute normalized observed_surprisal = -log p_prev[X[:, 1:]] / log(vocab_size) and normalized previous_entropy = entropy(p_prev) / log(vocab_size). Measure adjacent predictive drift with Jensen-Shannon divergence between p_prev and p_cur. Define a detached allowed budget = base_budget + surprise_slope * observed_surprisal + entropy_slope * previous_entropy, and add mean(relu(js_drift - allowed_budget)^2) with lambda_update ramped to small values such as 0.005, 0.01, and 0.02. Ignore the first few positions for stability. Compare against the baseline, fixed-budget temporal smoothing, and a shuffled-budget control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, mean JS drift, budget violation rate, expected calibration error, validation loss by surprise bucket, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: repeat_frequency_group_dro

Add compute_repeat_frequency_groups(X, Y, token_freq_bucket), assigning each supervised token to one of nine causal groups from frequency bucket crossed with prefix status: target not seen in the visible prefix, target seen recently within a threshold such as 32 characters, or target seen only at longer distance. In the training loop, compute unreduced per-token cross-entropy from logits. Maintain EMA losses for the nine groups, update them only when a group has enough examples in the batch, and after warmup_iters form capped softmax Group-DRO weights mixed with a small uniform component for stability. Compare against the baseline, fixed rarity-balanced weighting, and a random group-weight control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: predictive_state_metric

Name: sparse_symbol_equivariance

Name: two_step_branch_marginal
Title: Two-Step Branch Marginalization for Autoregressive Rollout Calibration
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, ordinary next-character cross-entropy, evaluation path, and default generation unchanged. Add a helper two_step_branch_marginal_loss(model, X, Y, logits, top_k=4) that uses the penultimate input position in each sequence as an anchor. From detached logits[:, -2, :], take the top-k next-token candidates and their log probabilities. Repeat X top-k times, replace the final input token with each candidate, run one batched branched forward pass, and read the final-position log probability of the true final target Y[:, -1]. Compute the two-step marginal negative log likelihood using logsumexp(log p(c | prefix) + log p(Y_final | prefix, c)) over the top-k branches, treating this as a lower bound on the true two-step probability. After warmup_iters, every branch_interval iterations such as 8, optimize loss = ordinary_ce + lambda_branch * branch_marginal_nll, ramping lambda_branch to 0.05 or 0.1. Name: matched_context_monotonicity
Title: Matched-Position Context Monotonicity for Non-Interfering Long-Context Language Models

Name: progressive_depth_birth

Name: adaptive_logit_temperature

Add a logits_from_hidden helper: compute ordinary tied lm_head logits, predict bounded per-token log temperatures as log_temp = log_temp_max * tanh(temp_gate) * tanh(temperature_head(hidden)), set temp = exp(log_temp), and divide logits by temp. Name: anchor_temporal_targets

Name: orthogonalized_linear_updates

Name: causal_film_norm
