Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, learned gate values, modulation magnitude, validation loss near whitespace or punctuation boundaries when available, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: fisher_gated_continual_lm
Title: Fisher-Gated Continual Adaptation for Tokenizer-Free Language Models
Experiment: Train one GPT sequentially across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using a shared union character vocabulary built from each dataset's meta.pkl, with local-to-global token id remapping inside get_batch(dataset, split). After finishing each dataset phase, estimate a diagonal parameter-importance score on a small fixed train-only calibration set by accumulating squared gradients of the ordinary next-character loss. In later phases, compare naive sequential fine-tuning against Fisher-gated training, where each parameter gradient is scaled before clipping and AdamW by 1 / (1 + lambda_fisher * fisher_importance). Accumulate importance scores across completed domains, but keep only one running importance tensor per parameter to limit memory. Evaluate after every phase on all dataset validation sets using ordinary next-character loss, and report final mean validation loss, average forgetting from each domain's best prior loss, backward transfer, train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Optionally include a simple EWC quadratic penalty baseline if runtime permits.

Name: transition_gated_smoothing
Title: Transition-Gated State Smoothing for Temporally Structured Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small transition_head Linear(n_embd, 1) used only during training and diagnostics. Add a helper that computes self-supervised transition scores from each batch: using one-hot token indicators and cumulative sums, form normalized token histograms over a past window ending at each position and a future window beginning after that position, with window sizes such as 16 or 32. Define the transition score as the clipped Jensen-Shannon divergence between these two histograms, masking positions too close to the sequence edges. Keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every transition_interval iterations, run the model with return_hidden=True, regress the transition_head output to the detached transition score, and add a small hinge regularizer on adjacent normalized hidden-state drift: penalize drift only when it exceeds a margin that increases with the transition score. Ramp lambda_transition from 0.0 to 0.05 or 0.1. Evaluation and generation use only the standard lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss, transition prediction MSE, hidden-state drift by transition-score bucket, validation loss on low-transition versus high-transition positions, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, ungated hidden-state smoothing, and shuffled-transition-score controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: calibrated_hidden_knn_cache
Title: Calibrated Hidden-State kNN Caches for Nonparametric Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while leaving the default training, evaluation, and generation paths unchanged. After ordinary training finishes, build a bounded train-only datastore by running the model in eval mode on sampled train.bin windows and storing L2-normalized hidden states with their next-character labels, using a fixed budget such as 50000 or 100000 positions. Add a batched cosine top-k retrieval helper that returns neighbor labels, similarities, and a kNN target probability estimate from temperature-weighted votes. Tune k, retrieval temperature, interpolation weight alpha, and a simple confidence gate based on mean top-k similarity or neighbor-label entropy on a fixed calibration slice of val.bin, then evaluate on the remaining validation slice. Report GPT-only validation loss, kNN-only loss, fused loss, rare-token loss, repeated-target loss, fusion activation rate, neighbor-label entropy, mean retrieval similarity, datastore size, memory overhead, validation throughput, and ordinary versus fused generation tokens per second. Compare GPT-only, always-on hidden-kNN fusion, confidence-gated hidden-kNN fusion, shuffled-label datastore fusion, and a small exact-suffix n-gram cache baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: stochastic_segment_packing
Title: Stochastic Segment Packing for Granularity-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept inputs_embeds and position_ids while preserving the default idx path used for ordinary training, evaluation, and generation. Add a small learned span_length_embedding table for lengths 1 to 6. During training, always compute the standard full character-level next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every packing_interval iterations, build an auxiliary packed view of the same batch: keep a protected recent suffix such as the final 128 tokens uncompressed, randomly segment the older prefix into spans of length 1 to 6 using one shared stochastic packing pattern per batch, replace each span by the mean of its token embeddings plus the corresponding span-length embedding, and assign that packed token the original position id of the span's final character. Append the ordinary suffix token embeddings, set targets to -1 for packed-prefix positions while keeping normal next-character targets on the suffix positions, and run the packed sequence through the model. Add a ramped auxiliary loss on the packed view consisting of suffix cross-entropy plus an optional small temperature-2 KL consistency term from detached clean full-context suffix logits to packed-view suffix logits. Extend estimate_loss to report clean validation loss, packed-suffix validation loss at fixed compression ratios, clean-to-packed degradation, compression ratio, and loss by distance from the packed-prefix boundary. Compare the baseline, packed-view CE only, packed-view CE plus KL consistency, and a suffix-only no-prefix control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best clean validation loss, packed-context robustness, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged ordinary generation tokens per second.

Name: predictability_shift_auxiliary
Title: Predictability-Shift Auxiliary Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small predictability_shift_head Linear(n_embd, 3) used only during training and diagnostics, with classes corresponding to future-easier, stable, and future-harder. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective on every iteration, but compute unreduced per-token CE from logits. After warmup_iters, every shift_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, build detached labels from local loss dynamics: compare the mean CE over the next H positions to the mean CE over the previous H positions, with H such as 8 or 16, and assign future-harder if the difference exceeds a margin, future-easier if it is below the negative margin, and stable otherwise. Mask positions without enough past or future context. Add a small ramped auxiliary cross-entropy loss with lambda_shift up to 0.02 to 0.1. Include controls with shuffled shift labels and absolute future-risk labels. Evaluation and generation use only the ordinary lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, predictability-shift accuracy, validation loss near predicted and true harder/easier regions, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: context_band_distillation
Title: Context-Band Distillation for Robust Autoregressive Context Use
Experiment: Add a learned mask_embedding to GPT and modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, input_mask=None) so positions marked by input_mask replace their token embeddings with mask_embedding before positional embeddings; when input_mask is None, evaluation and generation are unchanged. In train(), always compute the standard clean full-context next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every band_interval iterations, sample one structured context-band mask for the same X: keep a protected recent suffix such as the final 96 or 128 tokens visible, divide the older prefix into coarse distance bands, and mask one band or an alternating set of old-prefix stripes. Run one masked-view forward pass and add a small ramped temperature-2 KL loss from detached clean logits to masked-view logits only on the protected suffix, with lambda_band up to 0.05 or 0.1. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary clean train/validation loss as the primary metric, validation loss under fixed far-band, middle-band, and striped-prefix masks, clean-to-masked degradation, and suffix KL. Compare against the baseline, random input masking at the same mask rate, and recent-only short-context distillation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best clean validation loss, masked-context robustness, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: error_weighted_confusion_smoothing
Title: Error-Weighted Confusion Smoothing for Self-Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In train(), after loading vocab_size, initialize a vocab_size by vocab_size EMA confusion table plus per-target support counts. After warmup_iters, compute logits normally, obtain detached softmax probabilities, zero the true target entry, and update each target character's EMA row using the remaining off-diagonal probabilities weighted by their total error mass. Rows with insufficient support or negligible off-diagonal mass are inactive. For optimization, use ordinary hard next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss, and add a small ramped nonuniform smoothing term where the target distribution is (1 - epsilon) * one_hot(target) + epsilon * confusion_row[target], with epsilon capped around 0.05 to 0.15 and gated by row support. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, expected calibration error, rare-token validation loss, high-confusion versus low-confusion target loss, confusion-row entropy, and train-val gap. Compare against the baseline, uniform label smoothing, unigram smoothing, and a row-shuffled confusion-table control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged, so inference tokens per second should be unaffected.

Name: selective_state_adapters
Title: Selective Causal State Adapters for Hybrid Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional lightweight SelectiveStateAdapter inside each transformer Block after the attention residual and before the MLP. Extend GPTConfig with use_selective_state_adapter, selective_state_dim, selective_gate_init, selective_forget_bias_init, and selective_dropout. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects each hidden state into a bottleneck value vector and a forget gate, then runs a causal diagonal recurrence over the sequence: state_t = forget_t * state_{t-1} + (1 - forget_t) * tanh(value_t). Initialize the forget-gate bias to a moderate positive value so the adapter begins with nontrivial memory, project the recurrent state back to n_embd, apply dropout, and add it through a learned scalar residual gate initialized to a small nonzero value such as 1e-3. Keep the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, data loader, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the baseline, selective adapters with state dimensions such as n_embd / 4 and n_embd / 2, a fixed-decay EMA adapter control, and a parameter-matched feedforward adapter control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, parameter count, learned residual gates, mean forget gate and implied timescale by layer, validation loss at context lengths 64 and 256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: fixed_budget_exemplar_retrieval
Title: Fixed-Budget Causal Exemplar Retrieval for In-Context Character Modeling
Experiment: Build a train-only suffix index for each dataset from train.bin, mapping short keys such as the previous 8 or 12 character ids to capped lists of continuation offsets. Modify get_batch() to optionally create retrieval-conditioned batches with the same total block_size as the baseline: use a fixed retrieval prefix budget such as 64 tokens for one retrieved train snippet, followed by a current-stream segment of length block_size - retrieval_len. During training, retrieve using only causal context before the supervised suffix and exclude offsets near the current training offset to avoid trivial self-retrieval. Set targets to -1 for retrieved tokens and for an initial current-stream query prefix, computing ordinary next-character cross-entropy only on the protected current suffix. Add optional learned segment embeddings in GPT.forward() to distinguish retrieved tokens from current-stream tokens; the default path without segment ids remains unchanged. Train with a mixture of ordinary and retrieval-conditioned batches. Extend estimate_loss() to report standard validation loss, retrieval-conditioned validation loss using only the train index, random-retrieval control loss, same-length local-prefix control loss, retrieval hit rate, loss on repeated versus novel target characters, total train time, and ordinary generation tokens per second. Compare baseline GPT, retrieval-prefix GPT, random retrieval, and retrieval-prefix without segment embeddings across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: soft_key_retention
Title: Soft Key-Retention Gates for Learned Sparse Memory in Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_key_retention, local_window, retention_budget, retention_reg_weight, retention_gate_bias_init, and retention_eps. In CausalSelfAttention, when enabled, use the manual causal attention path and add a small Linear(n_embd, n_head) that predicts a sigmoid retention gate for each token and head from the layer input. Keys inside each query's recent local_window remain fully visible. Older nonlocal keys receive an additive attention-logit bias log(gate + retention_eps), so low-retention tokens are softly suppressed as distant memory while training remains differentiable. Initialize gate biases positive so the model starts close to full attention, then after warmup_iters ramp a budget regularizer that discourages the mean retention gate from exceeding retention_budget. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, data loader, sampling, and default generation behavior unchanged. Extend evaluation to report ordinary validation loss plus retention diagnostics. Compare the flash-attention baseline, manual full-attention control, local-only attention, soft key-retention models with budgets such as 0.10, 0.20, and 0.40, and a random-retention control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, local-to-full degradation, mean retention rate, retention entropy by layer and head, validation loss on repeated versus novel target characters, loss by previous-occurrence distance, total train time, and generation tokens per second.

Name: conservative_on_policy_ranking
Title: Conservative On-Policy Continuation Ranking for Exposure-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, standard next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and default generation code unchanged. After warmup_iters, every ranking_interval iterations, take a small subset of the current batch, reconstruct contiguous chunks as torch.cat([X[:, :1], Y], dim=1), choose a prefix length such as 128 and continuation length such as 32 or 64, and sample one continuation from the current model under torch.no_grad(). Build two teacher-forced sequences with the same prefix: one followed by the real continuation and one followed by the sampled continuation. Run one batched scoring forward pass, mask prefix targets with -1, and compute length-normalized log probabilities over continuation tokens only. Add a conservative ramped pairwise loss such as lambda_rank * mean(softplus(score_sampled - score_real + margin)), with a small margin near 0 and lambda_rank capped around 0.05 to 0.1, while ordinary CE remains the dominant loss every iteration. Include ablations with swapped real continuations as negatives, a DPO-style frozen warmup reference model, and a compute-matched sampling control without the ranking loss. Extend diagnostics to report ordinary train and validation loss, real-versus-sampled ranking accuracy, average continuation score margin, sampled repetition rate, distinct n-gram fraction, fixed-prefix rollout quality, total train time, and unchanged default generation tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: agreement_gated_suffix_barycenter
Title: Agreement-Gated Suffix Barycenter Consistency for Prefix-Robust Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a helper that constructs prefix-replaced views of a batch by preserving a protected recent suffix of length S, such as 96 or 128 tokens, while replacing the older prefix with prefixes from rolled batch elements. During training, always compute the standard clean next-token CE loss. After warmup_iters, every consistency_interval iterations, run the model on the clean batch and one or two prefix-replaced views. Align logits on the shared suffix after a burn-in of 16 or 32 positions. Compute detached temperature-scaled probabilities for each view, form their barycenter distribution, and add a small symmetric KL loss from each view to the barycenter. Downweight each suffix position with a detached agreement gate based on the views' Jensen-Shannon disagreement, so strongly prefix-sensitive positions contribute less. Ramp lambda_suffix up to 0.05 or 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss, prefix-replaced validation loss, clean-to-replaced degradation, suffix JS disagreement, gated versus ungated consistency diagnostics, loss by distance into the suffix, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, ungated suffix barycenter consistency, clean-teacher-to-replaced-view KL, and replaced-view CE-only controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: shared_recency_logit_bias
Title: Shared Causal Recency Logit Biases for Reuse-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_recency_logit_bias, recency_num_buckets, recency_gate_init, and use_token_specific_recency_ablation. Add a vectorized helper that, given idx, computes for each batch position and vocabulary token the distance to that token's most recent occurrence in the visible prefix X[:, :t+1], maps distances into logarithmic buckets such as current, 1-4, 5-16, 17-64, 65+, and unseen, and returns bucket ids with shape batch by time by vocab_size. In GPT.__init__, add a small learned recency_bias table with one scalar per bucket and a learned scalar gate initialized to zero so the model starts exactly as the baseline. In GPT.forward(), after computing ordinary lm_head logits, add gate * recency_bias[bucket_ids] before the cross-entropy loss when enabled; the default path remains unchanged. Modify generate() for enabled models to recompute recency buckets from the current context before sampling each token. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss, validation loss with the recency bias disabled, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, validation loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned recency biases, gate value, and inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, shared recency-logit bias, token-specific recency-bias ablation, shuffled-recency control, and a recent-count-only control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: queried_prefix_recall
Title: Queried Prefix Recall for Memory-Rich Autoregressive Representations
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small training-only prefix recall head that receives hidden state h_t plus a learned embedding of a sampled lookback-distance bucket and predicts the character X[:, t - d]. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every recall_interval iterations, sample at most 512 valid batch-time positions and one log-balanced lookback distance per position from buckets such as 1-4, 5-16, 17-64, and 65-255. Add a ramped auxiliary recall cross-entropy with lambda_recall capped at 0.05 or 0.1. Evaluation and generation ignore the recall head and use the normal lm_head path. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, recall accuracy by distance bucket, validation loss by previous-occurrence distance of the next target, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a shuffled-recall-label control, and a short-distance-only recall control to test whether explicit queryable prefix memory improves language modeling beyond auxiliary-computation effects.

Name: sticky_regime_logits
Title: Sticky Latent-Regime Logit Adapters for Nonstationary Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_sticky_regime_logits, num_regimes, regime_rank, regime_gate_init, regime_router_temperature, regime_balance_weight, and regime_smooth_weight. Add a logits_from_hidden helper in GPT that computes the usual tied-output logits, then optionally adds a gated low-rank residual logit adapter selected by soft router probabilities predicted from each final hidden state. Initialize the residual output factors to zero and the scalar gate near zero so the enabled model starts exactly as the tied baseline. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, add small ramped router regularizers: a batch-level balance term to discourage collapse and an adjacent-position smoothness term to encourage temporally coherent regimes. Keep data loading, evaluation, and generation otherwise unchanged. Compare the baseline, a K=1 global low-rank logit residual, an unregularized regime mixture, a shuffled-router control, and sticky mixtures with 2 and 4 regimes across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, expected calibration error, parameter count, inference tokens per second, residual gate value, router entropy, regime switch rate, and validation loss by rare versus common target characters.

Name: surprisal_key_attention
Title: Surprisal-Key Attention Biases for Compression-Aware Character Transformers
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to build a frozen backoff n-gram scorer using short suffix lengths such as 1, 2, and 4 with additive smoothing and simple pruning or caps for memory control. Modify get_batch() to optionally return key_surprisal for X, where key_surprisal[:, t] is the frozen n-gram negative log probability of X[:, t] given only earlier tokens in that sampled window. Normalize surprisal within each sequence and clamp it to a conservative range for stability. Extend GPTConfig with use_surprisal_key_attention, surprisal_bias_max, and surprisal_bias_init. Add one learned per-layer per-head scalar initialized to zero and bounded with tanh. Modify GPT.forward, Block.forward, and CausalSelfAttention.forward to pass key_surprisal into attention. When enabled, use the manual causal attention path and add scale[layer, head] * key_surprisal[:, None, None, :] to attention logits before softmax, preserving the usual future mask. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation procedure otherwise unchanged; enabled models recompute surprisal scores for the current context during generation. Compare the original flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention zero-bias control, true n-gram surprisal-key attention, unigram-surprisal attention, and shuffled-surprisal control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, validation loss on rare and repeated targets, learned bias scales by layer/head, attention mass assigned to high-surprisal keys, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: edit_recovery_consistency
Title: Edit-Recovery Consistency for Robust Autoregressive State Formation
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a helper that constructs an edited-prefix view of each batch by preserving the final suffix of length S, such as 96 or 128 tokens, exactly at the same positions, while applying low-rate fixed-length edit surrogates only to the older prefix: adjacent swaps, local duplications compensated by nearby deletions, and local deletions compensated by nearby repeats. In the training loop, always optimize the clean next-token cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every edit_interval iterations, run one additional forward pass on the edited-prefix batch and add a small ramped temperature-2 KL consistency loss from detached clean logits to edited-view logits only on the preserved suffix after a burn-in of 16 or 32 tokens. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary clean train/validation loss, validation loss under fixed prefix edit noise, clean-to-edited degradation, suffix KL, an edit-recovery curve showing loss by distance into the preserved suffix, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, random prefix masking with the same corruption rate, prefix replacement consistency, and edited-prefix training without the KL term across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: softmax_nullspace_regularization
Title: Softmax-Nullspace Regularization for Tied-Embedding Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a softmax_nullspace_penalty(hidden, embedding_weight) helper that centers the tied output embedding matrix by subtracting its vocabulary mean, computes a detached orthonormal basis for the centered row space using SVD or QR, projects hidden states onto this probability-relevant subspace, and penalizes the residual softmax-null energy normalized by total hidden energy. Recompute the detached basis only on nullspace-regularization iterations to keep overhead small. In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective on every iteration; after warmup_iters, every nullspace_interval iterations, add lambda_null times this penalty with lambda_null ramped to values such as 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01. Include a matched random-subspace control and a simple hidden-norm penalty control to test whether gains come from tied-softmax geometry rather than generic shrinkage. Evaluation and generation remain unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss, softmax-null energy, row-space energy, train-val gap, expected calibration error, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, using ordinary validation loss as the primary metric and nullspace energy plus calibration as diagnostics.

Name: depth_logprob_fusion
Title: Depth-Wise Log-Probability Fusion for Self-Ensembled Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_depth_logprob_fusion, fusion_layers, fusion_final_anchor_weight, and fusion_weight_init. In GPT.__init__, add one LayerNorm for each selected intermediate depth and a learned vector of global fusion logits initialized to strongly favor the final layer, so the enabled model starts close to the baseline. Modify GPT.forward() so that, when enabled, it stores hidden states after selected transformer blocks plus the final ln_f state, applies the tied lm_head to each normalized state, computes log_softmax for each depth, and forms fused_log_probs as a softmax-weighted sum of these depth log probabilities. Compute the main loss with F.nll_loss on fused_log_probs and add a small ordinary final-layer cross-entropy anchor loss so the final representation remains independently useful. Modify generate() so enabled models use fused_log_probs as sampling scores before temperature scaling and top-k filtering, while the default baseline path remains unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report fused validation loss, final-only validation loss, per-depth validation losses, learned fusion weights, depth disagreement, expected calibration error, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare baseline GPT, static depth log-probability fusion using layers such as 2, 4, and 6, and a probability-mixture fusion ablation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: amortized_prefix_latents
Title: Amortized Prefix Latents for Prompt-Adaptive Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_prefix_latent, prefix_latent_dim, prefix_latent_len, prefix_latent_gate_init, and latent_interval. Add a lightweight PrefixLatentEncoder that reads only the first prefix_latent_len tokens of each sequence, embeds them with the model token embedding table, mean-pools them, and maps the pooled vector to a deterministic latent. Add a latent projection and learned scalar gate in GPT; modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, prefix_latent=None) so the default path is unchanged, but when prefix_latent is provided its projected vector is added to token embeddings before positional embeddings. In train(), keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every latent_interval iterations, infer a prefix latent from the same batch, run one latent-conditioned forward pass, mask targets in the prefix to -1, and add a small ramped suffix CE auxiliary loss. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, latent-conditioned suffix validation loss, zero-latent suffix loss, shuffled-prefix-latent suffix loss, a compute-matched suffix-loss control without prefix conditioning, adaptation gain, learned gate value, train-val gap, total train time, and ordinary versus prefix-conditioned generation tokens per second. Compare the baseline, deterministic prefix latents, shuffled-latent controls, and compute-matched suffix controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: in_context_transition_bias
Title: In-Context Transition Biases for Fast-Adaptive Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_transition_bias, transition_smoothing, transition_tau, transition_bias_max, and transition_gate_init. Add a helper that builds a leakage-free per-sequence transition logit bias from idx: at position t, use only previously visible adjacent pairs (idx[p], idx[p+1]) with p+1 <= t, retrieve the smoothed next-character distribution conditioned on the current character idx[t], and return a batch by time by vocab_size log-probability bias plus support counts. In GPT.__init__, add one learned scalar gate initialized to 0.0 and bounded by transition_bias_max. In GPT.forward, when enabled, add gate * support / (support + transition_tau) * transition_log_bias to the ordinary lm_head logits before computing cross-entropy. Modify generate() so enabled models recompute the same transition bias from the current generated context before sampling each token. Keep the optimizer, data loader, ordinary objective, and disabled baseline path unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, validation loss with the bias disabled, transition-only loss, support hit rate, learned gate value, loss on repeated-transition versus novel-transition positions, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, in-context transition bias, a global train-set bigram bias control, and a shuffled in-context transition control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: calibration_gradient_surgery
Title: Train-Only Calibration Gradient Surgery for Interference-Resistant Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify get_batch() to optionally sample from a small fixed train-only calibration offset pool initialized at the start of train(), keeping validation data untouched. Keep the GPT architecture, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged. After warmup_iters, every surgery_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, compute the usual training loss and scaled gradients on the current batch, clone gradients for matrix-shaped parameters, zero gradients, then compute scaled gradients on a calibration batch. If the global cosine or dot product between the training and calibration gradients is negative, replace each matrix-shaped training gradient with its PCGrad-style projection g = g - dot(g, c) / (||c||^2 + eps) * c; otherwise restore the original training gradients. Leave LayerNorm parameters and biases unchanged, then use the existing GradScaler unscale, gradient clipping, and AdamW step. On non-surgery iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Log ordinary train and validation loss, calibration loss, gradient cosine, projection frequency, projection norm ratio, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare baseline AdamW, calibration gradient surgery, and a compute-matched extra-calibration-backward control that discards the calibration gradient across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: layerwise_distance_coverage
Title: Layerwise Distance-Coverage Regularization for Context-Using Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward, Block.forward, and GPT.forward to accept an optional distance_coverage flag. When disabled, keep the current flash-attention path unchanged. When enabled after warmup_iters every coverage_interval iterations, use the manual causal attention path, compute attention probabilities, and aggregate attention mass into coarse causal distance bands such as 0-1, 2-7, 8-31, 32-127, and 128-255. Ignore query positions where a distance band is unavailable. For each layer, average band mass across heads and add a small hinge loss that only penalizes collapse of medium and far context use, for example relu(mid_floor - mid_mass)^2 + relu(far_floor - far_mass)^2, with lambda_coverage ramped to a small value such as 0.001 to 0.01. Do not force every head to match the same profile; log per-head band usage only as diagnostics. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective, and keep evaluation and generation unchanged by default. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, validation losses at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, attention mass by distance band, far-band usage by layer, and validation loss by previous-occurrence distance of the target character. Compare against the baseline, a manual-attention no-regularizer control, and a per-query attention-entropy floor control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, long-context robustness, repeated-token loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged default generation tokens per second.

Name: interior_position_bottleneck
Title: Interior Position-Information Bottlenecks for Origin-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f and optionally accept position_ids, defaulting to the existing arange positions so standard training, evaluation, and generation are unchanged. Add a small train-only position_adversary head that predicts coarse absolute-position buckets from hidden states through a gradient-reversal layer. During training, compute ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, add a weak ramped adversarial position loss with maximum weight 0.01 to 0.05, using 16 or 32 coarse buckets and applying it only to interior positions after a burn-in such as the first 32 tokens, where absolute position mostly reflects missing left context. The adversary learns to predict position, while the LM hidden states receive reversed gradients, discouraging unnecessary crop-origin information. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, validation loss by absolute-position bucket, detached position-probe accuracy, short-context validation losses at 32/64/128/256, and shifted-position validation loss when a larger positional table such as 512 is enabled. Compare the baseline, interior position bottleneck, random-position-offset training, and bottleneck plus random offsets across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, train-val gap, position leakage, shifted-origin degradation, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: local_marginal_calibration
Title: Local Marginal Calibration for Autoregressive Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, add a small ramped auxiliary loss that partitions each sequence into non-overlapping chunks at one or two scales such as 32 and 128 positions. For each chunk, average softmax(logits) over valid positions, compute a Dirichlet-smoothed empirical histogram of the target characters in that chunk, and minimize bounded Jensen-Shannon divergence between the predicted marginal and empirical marginal. Use conservative lambda_marginal values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 so token-level likelihood remains dominant. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, local marginal divergence by scale, expected calibration error, validation loss by local target-entropy bucket, generated character-frequency KL against validation, repeated-character rate, and distinct n-gram fraction. Compare against the baseline, uniform label smoothing, global batch-level marginal matching, and shuffled-chunk histogram controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Since generation uses the unchanged LM head, inference tokens per second should remain essentially unchanged.

Name: soft_stack_adapter
Title: Soft Causal Stack Adapters for Hierarchical Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional SoftStackAdapter inserted after one configurable transformer block, such as block 3 in the 6-layer model. Extend GPTConfig with use_stack_adapter, stack_layer, stack_depth, stack_dim, stack_gate_init, and stack_action_temperature. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects each hidden state to a candidate stack value and soft push/pop/keep action probabilities, then scans causally over the sequence while maintaining a fixed-depth differentiable stack. At each position, form three candidate next stacks: push shifts older slots down and inserts the candidate value, pop shifts slots up, and keep preserves the previous stack; the actual next stack is their probability-weighted mixture. Read from the stack with a small query projection and attention over stack slots, project the read vector back to n_embd, and add it through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero so the enabled model starts close to the baseline. Keep the data loader, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and default generation API unchanged. Compare the baseline, soft stack adapters with depths 4 and 8, a FIFO queue-memory control with matched parameters, and a no-action recurrent-memory control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, parameter count, learned gate value, push/pop/keep rates, stack action entropy, validation loss on repeated versus novel targets, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: topk_soft_rollin
Title: Top-k Soft Roll-In Teacher Forcing for Exposure-Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept input_embeds. When input_embeds is None, keep the existing token embedding path unchanged; otherwise use input_embeds before adding positional embeddings. In train(), always compute the standard clean next-character cross-entropy on X, Y. After warmup_iters, every soft_rollin_interval iterations, build detached soft roll-in embeddings from the clean logits: position 0 uses the true token embedding, while position t may replace the true embedding of X[:, t] with the expected embedding under the top-k truncated softmax of clean_logits[:, t - 1] / rollin_temperature. Apply replacements only on a Bernoulli mask with probability p_rollin ramped from 0 to a conservative maximum such as 0.25. Run one auxiliary forward pass on the mixed embeddings and add lambda_rollin * soft_rollin_ce, with lambda_rollin ramped to 0.1 or 0.25. Keep evaluation and default generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, plus validation loss under soft roll-in inputs, sampled-prefix-corruption validation loss, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, total train time, and ordinary generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a random top-k soft-embedding control with the same replacement rate, and discrete self-corruption recovery across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: stickbreaking_token_halting
Title: Stick-Breaking Token Halting for Adaptive-Depth Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_token_halting, halting_layers, ponder_weight, halting_threshold, and halting_gate_bias_init. Add one exit LayerNorm and one Linear(n_embd, 1) halting head for each selected transformer depth, reusing the tied lm_head for exit logits. Modify GPT.forward() so the default full-depth path is unchanged. When token halting is enabled, collect hidden states at selected depths, compute per-token halting probabilities, convert them into stick-breaking depth weights with any remaining probability mass assigned to the final depth, and compute the next-character loss from the logsumexp mixture of per-depth log probabilities. Add a small final-depth cross-entropy anchor loss plus a ramped ponder penalty proportional to expected depth. Extend estimate_loss() to report final-depth validation loss, halting-mixture validation loss, mean expected depth, halt-depth histograms, and validation loss by predicted halt depth. Add generate_adaptive_depth() that runs layers sequentially during decoding and stops once the final-position cumulative halt probability exceeds a threshold, falling back to the final layer when needed. Compare the baseline, auxiliary exits without learned halting, confidence-threshold exits, learned halting without ponder cost, and learned halting with ponder costs across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 using best final-depth validation loss, adaptive validation loss, average layers used, generation tokens per second, and train-val gap.

Name: variational_residual_rate
Title: Variational Residual Rate Bottlenecks for Predictive Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional VariationalResidualBottleneck after one configurable middle transformer block, for example block 3 in the 6-layer model. Extend GPTConfig with use_variational_residual_bottleneck, bottleneck_layer, bottleneck_dim, bottleneck_mix_max, kl_beta_max, and kl_free_nats. The bottleneck applies LayerNorm to hidden states, predicts mu and logvar in bottleneck_dim, samples z = mu + eps * std during training, projects z back to n_embd with a zero-initialized output projection, and adds it residually as h = h + mix * z_proj. The mix value ramps from 0.0 after warmup_iters to bottleneck_mix_max, so the model starts exactly as the baseline. Add a per-token KL(q(z|h) || N(0,I)) term with free-nats clipping, and optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy plus ramped beta_kl times the KL. Evaluation and generation use the deterministic mean path by default. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, mean KL rate per token, validation loss by KL-rate bucket, train-val gap, deterministic versus stochastic validation loss, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, residual bottleneck without KL, variational residual bottlenecks with bottleneck_dim values such as n_embd / 2 and n_embd / 4, and a matched Gaussian residual-noise control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: leave_one_domain_reptile
Title: Leave-One-Domain Reptile Initialization for Fast Character-LM Adaptation
Experiment: Add a meta_train_reptile mode alongside the existing train() function. Build a union character vocabulary from the available dataset meta.pkl files and add local-to-global remapping inside get_batch(dataset, split, shard_id=None). For each held-out target dataset, meta-train one GPT initialization on the other two source datasets only. Each meta-episode samples a source dataset and train-only shard, copies the current model weights, runs a small number of ordinary next-character cross-entropy inner-loop steps, then applies a first-order Reptile update that moves the base initialization toward the adapted weights. Keep the GPT architecture, objective, evaluation, and generation path unchanged. After meta-training, fine-tune copies of the learned initialization on the held-out target for fixed budgets such as 100, 500, and 2000 steps. Compare against random initialization and pooled source-domain pretraining followed by the same target fine-tuning budgets, with matched pretraining token budgets where practical. Report held-out validation loss versus adaptation steps, best validation loss under each budget, train-val gap, total meta-training cost, adaptation time, and post-adaptation generation tokens per second. The central test is whether a meta-optimized character-LM initialization transfers useful sequence structure to unseen text domains without extra data or inference-time changes.

Name: causal_multiscale_state_dropout
Title: Causal Multiscale State Dropout for Scale-Robust Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally apply a train-time multiscale hidden-state perturbation after a fixed middle block such as block 3. Add a helper that computes edge-corrected causal moving averages of hidden states with cumulative sums using two windows such as 16 and 64. Decompose the hidden state h into fast = h - ma16, medium = ma16 - ma64, and slow = ma64. When enabled, randomly choose one component per batch, attenuate it by a scheduled factor ramping from 0.0 to about 0.5, recombine the components, and continue through the remaining transformer blocks. Keep the default forward path and generation path unchanged. In train(), always compute ordinary clean next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every state_dropout_interval iterations, run one additional perturbed forward pass on the same X and Y, adding a ramped auxiliary loss consisting of perturbed cross-entropy plus temperature-2 KL consistency from detached clean logits to perturbed logits. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, validation loss under fixed fast-drop, medium-drop, and slow-drop perturbations, clean-to-perturbed KL, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged clean generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, Gaussian hidden-state jitter at the same layer, and input token dropout controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: prompt_local_hidden_knn
Title: Prompt-Local Hidden kNN for Causal In-Context Prediction
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while keeping the default training, evaluation, and generation paths unchanged. After ordinary training, add a prompt_local_hidden_knn helper that normalizes hidden states within each sequence and, for each prediction position t, retrieves only earlier states h_p with p < t. Each retrieved state votes for its causally observed next token X[:, p + 1], forming a temperature-weighted local kNN distribution over the vocabulary. Fuse this distribution with the GPT log probabilities using a bounded gate based on mean top-k similarity and neighbor-label entropy. Tune k, retrieval temperature, and maximum fusion weight on a small calibration slice of val.bin, then report results on the remaining validation data. Add diagnostics for GPT-only loss, prompt-kNN-only loss, fused loss, activation rate, mean similarity, neighbor entropy, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, previous-occurrence-distance buckets, and validation throughput. Add an optional generate_prompt_knn() that recomputes the prompt-local hidden cache from the current context before each sampled token, while leaving ordinary generate() unchanged. Compare against GPT-only, a prompt-local exact n-gram cache, and a shuffled-neighbor-label hidden-kNN control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: confident_depth_refinement
Title: Confident Depth Refinement for Non-Degrading Autoregressive Transformers
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return hidden states after selected transformer blocks, for example layers 2 and 4, plus the final hidden state. Add one LayerNorm probe for each selected intermediate depth and reuse the tied lm_head to produce intermediate logits. Train with the ordinary final-layer next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every depth_interval iterations, compute a small auxiliary CE loss for the intermediate probes and an additional monotonic refinement loss. For each adjacent pair of depths, compute unreduced target NLLs and define a detached confidence gate selecting positions where the shallower probe's NLL is below the batch median. Add mean(gate * relu(nll_deeper - detach(nll_shallower) - margin)), ramped with lambda_depth values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Compare against the baseline, auxiliary-probe-only, and ungated monotonicity controls. Evaluation and generation use only the final-layer logits unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report final validation loss, per-depth validation losses, confident depth-regression rate, mean regression magnitude, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: query_adaptive_attention_temperature
Title: Query-Adaptive Attention Temperatures for Content-Dependent Context Use
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_query_attention_temperature, attn_log_temp_max, and attn_temp_gate_init. In CausalSelfAttention.__init__, when enabled, add temperature_head = Linear(n_embd, n_head) plus a learned scalar gate initialized to 0.0, so the enabled model starts equivalent to the baseline. In CausalSelfAttention.forward, use the manual causal attention path when this feature is enabled: compute ordinary scaled qk attention logits, predict bounded per-query per-head log inverse temperatures as attn_log_temp_max * tanh(gate) * tanh(temperature_head(x)), multiply each query's attention logits by exp(log_inv_temp), apply the usual causal mask, softmax, dropout, and value aggregation. Keep the data loader, optimizer, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the original flash-attention baseline, a manual-attention no-temperature control, static learned per-head temperatures, and query-adaptive temperatures across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, attention entropy, learned temperature statistics by layer and head, validation loss by predictive-entropy bucket, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: residual_update_diversity
Title: Residual Update Diversity for Layer-Specialized Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify Block.forward to optionally return the full residual update contributed by each block, defined as x_after_block - x_before_block, and propagate a return_residual_updates flag through GPT.forward. Train with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every diversity_interval iterations such as 4 or 8, run the normal forward pass with residual updates returned, sample at most 1024 valid batch-time positions, flatten each layer's sampled residual updates into a matrix, center it across sampled positions, L2-normalize the flattened matrix, and add a penalty equal to the mean squared cosine similarity between different layers' residual-update matrices. Ramp lambda_update_diversity from 0.0 to small values such as 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01. Log per-layer residual-update norms so collapse can be detected, and include a residual-norm penalty control to distinguish diversity from simple shrinkage. Evaluation and generation use the unchanged ordinary forward path. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss, residual-update similarity, per-layer update norms, effective update rank, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and residual-norm control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: transition_marginal_consistency
Title: Transition-Marginal Consistency for Autoregressive Character Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to build a smoothed empirical transition matrix P(x_{t+2} | x_{t+1}) over character ids, interpolating low-support rows with the unigram distribution. Keep the GPT architecture, batching, optimizer, ordinary next-character cross-entropy, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a helper transition_marginal_nll(logits, two_step_targets, log_transition) that uses log_softmax(logits[:, :-1, :]) and computes -logsumexp_c log p_model(c | prefix_t) + log P(x_{t+2} | c), where two_step_targets are Y[:, 1:]. In the training loop, after warmup_iters and every transition_interval iterations, optimize total_loss = ce_loss + lambda_transition * transition_marginal_nll, with lambda_transition ramped conservatively to values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, transition-marginal validation NLL, rollout calibration error, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, unigram-transition control, shuffled-transition control, and an identity-transition control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: nucleus_set_calibration
Title: Nucleus Set Calibration for Autoregressive Character Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. Add a helper that, for each batch position and coverage threshold such as 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, and 0.95, builds a detached nucleus prediction-set mask from the sorted softmax probabilities. For each threshold, compute the differentiable predicted mass assigned to the detached set and the non-differentiable indicator of whether the true target lies inside that set. After warmup_iters, add a small ramped calibration penalty equal to the squared difference between mean predicted set mass and mean empirical inclusion, optionally averaged over thresholds. Sweep lambda_cal values such as 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation NLL as the primary metric, expected calibration error, Brier score, nucleus coverage error, average nucleus set size, validation loss by predictive-confidence bucket, generated character-frequency KL, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, uniform label smoothing, and a learned global-temperature control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: two_step_belief_consistency
Title: Two-Step Belief Consistency for Autoregressive Character Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add one lightweight horizon-2 belief head Linear(n_embd, vocab_size), used only during training and diagnostics; ordinary evaluation and generation continue to use the tied lm_head. Train every iteration with the standard next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every belief_interval iterations, subsample a modest number of valid anchor positions t < block_size - 1. For each anchor, take the detached next-character distribution from the ordinary lm_head at position t, keep the top_k candidates, create branched copies where X[:, t + 1] is replaced by each candidate, run one extra batched forward pass, and collect detached one-step distributions at position t + 1. Form a normalized top-k approximation to the model-implied two-step predictive distribution by marginalizing over candidate next characters. Add a small ramped KL loss from this detached branched two-step distribution to the horizon-2 belief-head distribution at h_t, optionally anchored by a weak hard horizon-2 cross-entropy to Y[:, t + 1]. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, horizon-2 NLL, branch-consistency KL, top-k branch coverage, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare the baseline, hard horizon-2 head only, two-step belief consistency, and a shuffled-branch-target control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: context_ramp_supervision
Title: Context-Ramp Supervision for Boundary-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify the training loss to support position-dependent weights over each block. Instead of treating all target positions equally, assign reduced weight to low-context crop-boundary positions and full weight to interior positions, using schedules such as hard burn-in weights w_t=0 for t < B and w_t=1 afterward, or a soft linear ramp from 0 to 1 over the first B positions. Implement this by computing unreduced cross-entropy from logits and targets, multiplying by a fixed length-T weight vector, masking ignore_index targets, and normalizing by the sum of active weights. Keep GPT architecture, optimizer, data loader offsets, evaluation generation path, and sampling unchanged. Compare baseline uniform weights against ramp lengths B in {32, 64, 128}, plus a random-position weight control with the same total supervised weight. Run both equal-step and effective-supervised-token-matched comparisons by adjusting max_iters or gradient accumulation. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary full-window validation loss, interior suffix validation loss, loss by position bucket, boundary-to-interior loss gap, effective supervised tokens, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The key test is whether downweighting artificial crop-boundary predictions improves interior next-character modeling without changing inference cost.

Name: span_tokenization_dropout
Title: Reversible Span Tokenization Dropout for Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin only to build a compact vocabulary of frequent character spans of length 2 to 8, capped at sizes such as 256, 512, or 1024, while retaining all original character ids as atomic fallback tokens. Add build_span_vocab(), encode_spans(), and decode_spans() helpers. Precompute deterministic greedy span-tokenized train and validation streams, and add a tokenization-dropout training mode where greedy span matches are randomly skipped with probability p so the model sees a reversible mixture of span tokens and raw characters. Modify train() to optionally train GPT on this tokenized stream with vocab_size equal to character_vocab_size plus span_vocab_size and the same ordinary next-token cross-entropy objective. Report validation as character-normalized negative log likelihood by dividing total token NLL by decoded character count. To separate tokenization effects from longer effective context, compare both equal-token-budget runs and character-context-matched runs where token block_size is reduced so the average decoded characters per window is close to 256. Compare raw character baseline, deterministic span tokenization, span tokenization dropout, and a random-span vocabulary control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Log character-normalized validation loss, token-level loss, average characters per token, effective character context length, generation validity after decoding, total train time, and decoded-character generation speed.

Name: upper_block_recycling
Title: Upper-Block Recycling for Test-Time Refinement in Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_block_recycling, recycle_num_layers, max_recycle_steps, recycle_gate_init, and use_recycle_step_embedding. Modify GPT.__init__ to optionally add one learned scalar recycle gate initialized negative so sigmoid(gate) is near zero, plus learned recycle-step embeddings. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, recycle_steps=0, return_base_loss=False) so the model first runs the ordinary transformer stack and saves the pre-final-LayerNorm hidden state h_base. Compute the normal logits and base loss from ln_f(h_base). If recycle_steps > 0, repeatedly reuse the final recycle_num_layers transformer blocks on the current hidden state, optionally adding the recycle-step embedding before each recycled pass, then update h with a gated residual blend h = h + sigmoid(gate) * (h_refined - h). Compute recycled logits and loss from ln_f(h). In train(), always optimize the ordinary base next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every recycle_interval iterations, sample recycle_steps from {1, 2} and add a ramped auxiliary recycled loss with lambda_recycle up to 0.25 or 0.5. Extend estimate_loss and sampling diagnostics to report validation loss, train-val gap, expected calibration error, gate value, and generation tokens per second for recycle_steps 0, 1, and 2. Compare the standard baseline, block recycling evaluated at each recycle depth, a no-step-embedding ablation, and a zero-gate or no-recycle control.

Name: local_reset_segment_packing
Title: Local-Position Reset Segment Packing for Data-Efficient Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add optional segment_ids and position_ids arguments to GPT.forward, Block.forward, and CausalSelfAttention.forward. When segment_ids is None, preserve the existing flash-attention causal path and default arange positional embeddings. When segment_ids is provided, use an explicit causal attention mask that permits each query to attend only to positions at or before itself within the same packed segment, and use position_ids that reset to zero at each segment start. Add get_packed_batch(split), initially packing each 256-token example from four independently sampled 64-token segments; set targets at each segment start to -1 to avoid artificial cross-segment prediction. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy using a packed_batch_probability that mixes standard contiguous batches with reset-masked packed batches. Compare the contiguous baseline, naive packed batches without reset masks, reset-masked packing with global positions, reset-masked packing with local reset positions, and a variable-length packing ablation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary contiguous validation loss, reset-packed validation loss, validation loss by distance from segment start, short-context validation loss at 64 tokens, effective supervised tokens per step, total train time, and unchanged ordinary generation tokens per second. Generation remains unchanged by calling GPT.forward without segment_ids or position_ids.

Name: blue_noise_window_sampling
Title: Blue-Noise Window Sampling for Redundancy-Reduced Language Model Training
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, next-character objective, optimizer, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged. Modify get_batch() so training offsets can be supplied by an OffsetSampler rather than always sampled iid. Implement a blue-noise window sampler over valid memmap offsets: divide the corpus into equal strata, shuffle strata each epoch, sample jittered offsets within selected strata, and reject candidates that fall within a minimum distance such as block_size or 2 * block_size of offsets already chosen for the current batch or stored in a short recent-offset ring buffer. If rejection fails after a small number of attempts, fall back to jittered stratified sampling so the method is robust on small datasets. Compare four samplers: original iid uniform, simple shuffled-stratified, blue-noise without recent-history exclusion, and full blue-noise with recent-history exclusion. Use identical validation and generation for all models. Log ordinary train and validation loss, best validation loss, convergence speed, batch loss variance, offset duplicate rate, recent-window overlap rate, corpus coverage fraction, rejection rate, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The hypothesis is that uniform but repulsive crop sampling lowers gradient redundancy and improves sample efficiency or seed stability without changing the model, objective, data, or inference cost.

Name: budgeted_structural_gates
Title: Budgeted Structural Gates for Transferable Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Add optional structured gates to attention heads and MLP expansion groups while keeping the ordinary GPT architecture path unchanged when disabled. Extend GPTConfig with use_structural_gates, mlp_group_size, gate_temperature, target_compute_frac, gate_penalty_weight, and gate_threshold. In CausalSelfAttention, add one learnable sigmoid gate per head and multiply each head output before concatenation. In MLP, divide the 4 * n_embd hidden dimension into fixed groups and multiply each group by a learned sigmoid gate after GELU. Train with standard next-character cross-entropy; after warmup_iters, add a ramped penalty encouraging the expected active compute fraction to match targets such as 0.75 and 0.50. After training, threshold gates into binary masks, freeze them, and run a short fixed-budget recovery fine-tune. Compare against the full baseline, random structured masks at matched compute, magnitude-based structured pruning, and uniform width reduction. Report ordinary validation loss, validation loss per estimated FLOP, active heads and MLP groups by layer, train-val gap, parameter count, recovery-finetune gain, and generation tokens per second if the pruned masks are materialized by slicing attention and MLP weights. Also compare learned mask overlap and cross-dataset mask transfer across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8 to test whether efficient substructures are domain-specific or reusable.

Name: cheap_context_selection
Title: Cheap Prediction-Preserving Context Selection for Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Add optional position_ids and input_keep_gates arguments to GPT.forward while preserving the default idx-only path. Add a learned mask_embedding and a lightweight ContextSelector that scores each token from token embeddings plus positional information using a small causal Conv1d or Linear head, so selection can be computed before the main Transformer. During normal iterations, train exactly as the baseline with ordinary full-context next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every selection_interval iterations, reuse the clean full-context logits from the ordinary pass as detached teacher logits on a protected recent suffix such as the final 96 or 128 tokens. Compute selector gates for the older prefix, always keep the protected suffix, and run one auxiliary soft-masked pass where old-prefix embeddings are interpolated as gate * token_embedding + (1 - gate) * mask_embedding. Add a ramped auxiliary suffix loss combining masked-view cross-entropy and temperature-2 KL from detached clean logits, plus a budget penalty and mild saturation penalty so the mean old-prefix gate approaches target budgets such as 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary clean validation loss, soft-masked validation loss at fixed budgets, clean-to-masked degradation, mean retained fraction, selector entropy, and retention by distance bucket. Add a hard-selection evaluation path that gathers the top-scored older prefix tokens plus the full suffix using original position_ids, measuring sparse-context validation loss and generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, random prefix thinning at matched budgets, suffix-only context, and a simple learned selector without distillation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: echo_copy_curriculum
Title: Separator-Free Echo Copy Curricula for In-Context Reuse in Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, vocabulary, optimizer, ordinary evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. For horizons such as 2, 4, 8, and 16, compare the logit assigned at position t to the immediate next target Y[:, t] against the logit assigned at the same position to the later true token Y[:, t + h - 1]. Use a conservative pairwise softplus margin loss with horizon-decayed weights and a detached confidence gate that downweights high-entropy or high-CE positions, so ambiguous contexts contribute little. Name: spectral_depth_sharing

Name: prompt_suffix_residuals
Title: Prompt-Local Suffix Residuals for In-Context Character Prediction
Experiment: Scan train.bin once to compute a smoothed unigram prior. Add build_prompt_suffix_prior(idx, vocab_size, suffix_lengths, unigram_prior, smoothing) that scans each sequence left to right. For each position t, choose the longest suffix length from values such as [8, 4, 2] whose suffix ending at t appeared earlier in the same sequence, use only those earlier occurrences and their visible following characters to form a smoothed next-character distribution, and return its log probabilities, support count, and matched suffix length. Extend GPTConfig with use_prompt_suffix_residuals, suffix_lengths, suffix_tau, suffix_gate_init, and suffix_max_bias. In GPT.forward(), when suffix priors are supplied, compute ordinary lm_head logits and add a bounded support-gated residual bias gate_l * support / (support + tau) * (log_prior - log_unigram_prior), using only the matched suffix length for each position, then compute the usual cross-entropy. Name: ordered_prefix_state_auxiliary
Title: Ordered Prefix-State Supervision for Causal Character Language Models
Experiment: After loading each dataset vocabulary, create a small fixed set of coarse finite-state sketches. For each sketch, assign token ids to 4 or 8 balanced event groups, and assign each group a random permutation over 16 or 32 automaton states. Scanning X left to right gives an ordered causal state label at each position after consuming X[:, :t+1]. Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add small training-only state heads, one Linear(n_embd, num_states) per sketch. Name: transition_kernel_scoring
Title: Transition-Kernel Proper Scoring for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute smoothed predecessor and successor distributions for every token. Concatenate these distributions with normalized log frequency to form transition fingerprints, L2-normalize them, and build a positive-definite token kernel using an RBF kernel mixed with an identity kernel, for example K = (1 - rho) * I + rho * K_transition with rho in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}. Normalize the kernel diagonal to 1 so the loss scale is comparable across datasets. Add a kernel_score_loss(logits, targets, kernel) helper that computes the finite-space kernel proper score p^T K p - 2 K[y]^T p + K[y,y] for valid target positions, where p = softmax(logits). In the training loop, keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, every kernel_interval iterations such as 4, add a ramped lambda_kernel times the kernel score with conservative values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation NLL as the primary metric, kernel score, expected calibration error, Brier score, rare-token validation loss, generated character-frequency KL, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Name: latent_symbol_senses

Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_latent_symbol_senses, num_senses, sense_router_window, sense_gate_init, sense_balance_weight, and sense_diversity_weight. Name: crop_deficit_weighting
Title: Crop-Deficit Weighted Training for Missing-Context-Aware Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add a small optional crop_deficit_head Linear(n_embd, 1) used only during training and diagnostics. Modify get_batch() on auxiliary iterations to sample chunks of length block_size + extra_left + 1. From each chunk, create an extended-context view X_ctx = chunk[:, :block_size], Y_ctx = chunk[:, 1:block_size + 1] and a cropped view X_crop = chunk[:, extra_left:extra_left + block_size], Y_crop = chunk[:, extra_left + 1:extra_left + block_size + 1]. The aligned predictions are crop positions 0 through block_size - extra_left - 1 and context positions extra_left through block_size - 1, which correspond to the same absolute target characters but different left-context lengths. Train ordinary batches with the standard next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every deficit_interval iterations, run both aligned views, compute detached deficit = clamp(nll_crop - nll_ctx, min=0, max=deficit_cap) / deficit_cap, and optimize an auxiliary cropped-view loss whose per-token weights are reduced for high-deficit positions with a floor such as 0.25 and normalized to mean 1. Also train crop_deficit_head(hidden_crop) to predict the detached deficit with MSE or BCE, with a small ramped weight. Keep evaluation and generation through the ordinary lm_head unchanged. Name: predictive_bisimulation_loss
Title: Predictive Bisimulation Loss for Stable Autoregressive Belief Updates
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute the ordinary next-character cross-entropy from logits as usual. The helper samples valid positions t < block_size - 1, computes detached current predictive distributions from logits[:, :-1, :] / pred_temperature, and forms neighbor pairs only when the observed next character targets[:, t] is identical and the current predictive distributions are among each other’s nearest neighbors by Jensen-Shannon distance. It then adds a small weighted Jensen-Shannon penalty between the trainable successor predictive distributions at t + 1 for those pairs, with all pair weights detached. Optimize total_loss = ce_loss + lambda_bisim * bisim_loss, ramping lambda_bisim conservatively to 0.01, 0.02, or 0.05. Name: conditional_varentropy_matching

Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a conditional_varentropy_loss(logits, targets, num_buckets=5) helper. From log_softmax(logits), compute predicted entropy H and predicted varentropy V = E_p[(-log p)^2] - H^2. For valid targets, compute realized surprisal nll = -log p(y), then form a detached empirical target r = detach((nll - detach(H))^2). After warmup_iters, bucket valid positions by detached predicted entropy or detached predicted varentropy. For buckets with enough examples, add a small Huber or squared penalty between mean predicted V and mean detached r. Name: finite_diff_block_gain

Name: antithetic_dropout_ensembling

Name: zero_value_attention_sinks

Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_attention_sinks, num_attention_sinks, sink_logit_init, and sink_value_mode. Name: compositional_belief_updates
Title: Compositional Token-Conditioned Belief Updates for Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small training-only TokenTransition module that maps a hidden state h_t and an observed next token Y_t to a predicted next state h_hat_{t+1}. Implement it as a low-rank token-conditioned update: down-project h_t, modulate it with learned per-token scale and bias embeddings, up-project back to n_embd, and add the result residually to h_t. The one-step term matches h_hat_{t+1} to detached h_{t+1} using normalized MSE or cosine loss and matches lm_head(h_hat_{t+1}) to detached logits_{t+1} with temperature-2 KL. The compositional term applies the same transition module again using Y_{t+1}, producing h_hat_{t+2}, and matches detached h_{t+2} and logits_{t+2}. Name: prequential_attention_transport
Title: Prequential Attention Transport for Stable Autoregressive Context Tracking

Name: compute_matched_fork_merge
Title: Compute-Matched Same-Initialization Fork-Merge Training for Single-Model Ensemble Gains
Experiment: Refactor train() into reusable model initialization, train_steps(), evaluate(), and final sampling routines. Name: logit_laplace_calibration
Title: Logit-Space Laplace Calibration for Character Language Models

Name: counterfactual_prefix_contrast

Name: stateful_cipher_equivariance
