Title: Lie-Strang Block Consistency for Residual Transformer Language Models
Experiment: Modify Block.forward to accept a block_mode argument. The default 'lie' mode preserves the existing path x = x + attn(ln_1(x)); x = x + mlp(ln_2(x)). Add a 'strang' mode that applies x = x + 0.5 * mlp(ln_2(x)), then x = x + attn(ln_1(x)), then x = x + 0.5 * mlp(ln_2(x)), sharing all existing parameters and adding no new weights. Propagate block_mode through GPT.forward while keeping ordinary evaluation and generation on the default 'lie' path. In train(), always compute the standard next-character cross-entropy on the lie path. After warmup_iters, every split_interval iterations, run one auxiliary strang-path forward on the same X, Y and add a small ramped auxiliary loss: strang CE plus temperature-2 KL consistency from detached lie logits to strang logits, with lambda_split values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report lie-path validation loss as the primary metric, strang-path validation loss, lie-to-strang KL, train-val gap, total train time, and lie-path generation tokens per second. Compare the baseline, Lie-Strang consistency, strang CE without KL, and a compute-matched extra-lie-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: delayed_global_linear_attention
Title: Delayed Global Linear Attention for Local-Exact Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_delayed_global_linear_attention, local_window, global_gate_init, and linear_attention_eps. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward so enabled models use a two-branch manual attention path after computing the usual q, k, and v. The local branch performs exact causal softmax attention over only the most recent local_window tokens. The delayed global branch performs causal linear attention over only older prefix tokens outside that local window, using phi(x) = elu(x) + 1 and cumulative sums of phi(k) and phi(k) outer v shifted by local_window positions. Positions without older context receive a zero global output. Mix local and delayed-global outputs with a learned per-head scalar gate initialized near zero global contribution, then apply the existing c_proj and dropout. Keep the data loader, optimizer, next-character objective, evaluation, and generation otherwise unchanged. Compare full flash-attention baseline, manual full-attention control, local-only attention, and delayed-global linear attention with local_window values such as 32, 64, and 128 across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report ordinary validation loss, validation loss by context length, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned global gates by layer and head, estimated attention FLOPs, total train time, and generation tokens per second.

Name: task_vector_surgery
Title: Task-Vector Surgery for Mergeable Cross-Domain Character Language Models
Experiment: Build a union character vocabulary across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8, and remap each dataset's local token ids to global ids inside get_batch(dataset, split). Initialize one GPT with the union vocabulary, save its initial state_dict, then train same-initialization specialist copies separately on each dataset for matched token budgets. Compute task vectors delta_d = theta_d - theta_init. Evaluate merged models formed by theta_init plus: uniform averaged task vectors, train-calibration-tuned scalar task-vector weights, and module-wise task-vector surgery where, before averaging, any pair of module deltas with negative cosine similarity has the conflicting projection removed in a PCGrad-style update. Include controls using random task-vector permutations and same-domain branch averaging. Extend evaluation to report per-dataset validation loss, mean and worst-domain loss, merge gap versus separate specialists, improvement over naive pooled multitask training, module-wise task-vector cosine similarities, output-embedding row agreement, total train time, parameter count, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Optionally run a short balanced consolidation fine-tune from the best merged model to test whether surgical merging provides a better multitask initialization.

Name: activation_aligned_seed_merging
Title: Activation-Aligned Seed Merging for Single-Model Ensemble Compression
Experiment: Train several ordinary baseline seeds per dataset with the existing GPT architecture, objective, data loader, evaluation, and generation unchanged, and save each final uncompiled state_dict. Add post-hoc merging utilities that choose one seed as a reference and align the other seeds using exact local permutation symmetries: reorder attention heads by permuting q/k/v head blocks and matching c_proj input slices, and reorder MLP hidden channels by permuting c_fc output rows and matching c_proj input columns. Estimate permutations from a small train-only calibration set by comparing per-head attention outputs and per-channel MLP activations to the reference, using greedy matching by default and exhaustive search for the 6 attention heads. Average the aligned state_dicts into a normal single GPT, optionally followed by a short recovery fine-tune using the original training loss only. Compare individual seeds, log-probability ensembles, raw weight averages, weight-similarity alignment, activation-aligned averages, random-permutation controls, and activation-aligned averages with recovery fine-tuning. Report validation loss, merge loss barrier, gap to ensemble loss, calibration metrics such as ECE or Brier score, train-val gap, generation samples, total training and recovery time, and single-model inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: head_subspace_factorization
Title: Low-Rank Head Subspace Factorization for Parameter-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_head_subspace_factorization, head_basis_dim, and head_coeff_type. Modify CausalSelfAttention so that, when enabled, each attention head's Q, K, V, and output projection matrices are generated as linear combinations of a small bank of learned basis matrices using per-head coefficients. Implement the projections explicitly with einsum over head-specific generated weights, while keeping the default dense c_attn and c_proj path unchanged when disabled. Use learned per-head coefficients as the main setting, fixed DCT coefficients as an interpretable control, and head_basis_dim = n_head as a full-rank factorized sanity check. Keep the MLP, embeddings, optimizer, batching, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation API unchanged. Compare the standard independent-head baseline, full-rank factorized control, compressed basis sizes such as 1, 2, and 3, fixed-DCT coefficients, and a parameter-matched narrower baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report parameter count, best validation loss, validation loss per million parameters, convergence speed, train-val gap, inter-head projection similarity, basis-coefficient usage, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: source_index_warp_consistency
Title: Source-Indexed Prefix Warp Consistency for Rate-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add get_warp_pair_batch(split), which samples longer memmap chunks and constructs two block_size-length views: a clean contiguous view and a warped view whose older prefix is generated by a monotone source-index map with low-rate skips and duplicates. Preserve a recent source suffix of roughly 96 or 128 characters, but allow that same suffix to appear at shifted absolute positions in the two views by using small bounded prefix-length differences. Return X_clean, Y_clean, X_warp, Y_warp, and source-index maps for the prediction targets. Train ordinary clean CE every iteration. After warmup_iters, every warp_interval iterations, run both views, gather logits whose target source indices match inside the protected suffix, and add a small ramped temperature-2 KL consistency loss from detached clean logits to warped logits, optionally plus warped-view CE with a conservative weight. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss, warped-prefix validation loss, source-aligned suffix KL, clean-to-warp degradation, loss by distance into the aligned suffix, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, same-position prefix edit consistency, random prefix masking, and a shuffled-source-alignment control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: mtf_mass_calibration
Title: Move-to-Front Mass Calibration for In-Context Character Prediction
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, optimizer, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add compute_mtf_rank_buckets(X, Y, vocab_size, bucket_edges), which scans each sequence causally. After consuming X[:, t], each vocabulary token is assigned to a dynamic move-to-front bucket according to how recently that token type appeared in X[:, :t+1]: rank 0, rank 1, ranks 2-3, 4-7, 8-15, 16+, or unseen. Record both bucket ids for all vocabulary tokens at each batch-time position and the bucket containing the true target Y[:, t]. Add mtf_partition_loss(logits, bucket_ids, target_buckets), which computes log_softmax(logits), aggregates log probability mass per bucket with logsumexp, and applies cross-entropy to the true target bucket with ignore_index support. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration; after warmup_iters, every mtf_interval iterations such as 4, add a ramped auxiliary term loss = ce_loss + lambda_mtf * mtf_partition_loss, sweeping lambda_mtf values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation loss, MTF partition loss, partition accuracy, validation loss by target MTF bucket, seen versus unseen target loss, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a coarse seen-versus-unseen partition ablation, shuffled MTF buckets preserving bucket sizes, and a fixed unigram-frequency partition control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: complementary_partition_consistency
Title: Complementary Partition Consistency for Redundancy-Distributed Character Transformers
Experiment: Add optional structured mask arguments to CausalSelfAttention.forward and MLP.forward. Attention masks multiply per-head outputs before concatenation, and MLP masks multiply fixed expansion-channel groups after GELU, with keep-fraction rescaling. Propagate these masks through Block.forward and GPT.forward while keeping the default unmasked path unchanged. In train(), always compute the ordinary full-model next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every partition_interval iterations, sample two complementary binary partitions per layer, each keeping about half of attention heads and half of MLP groups, with their union covering all units. Run the two masked forwards on the same X, Y and add a ramped auxiliary loss consisting of masked-view cross-entropy plus temperature-2 KL from detached full-model logits to each masked view. Extend estimate_loss to report full validation loss, fixed held-out half-partition validation losses, complementary log-mean-exp ensemble validation loss, full-to-partition KL, post-hoc structured pruning degradation, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged full-model inference tokens per second. Compare the baseline, ordinary random structured dropout, complementary CE-only training, and complementary partition consistency across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: denominator_survival_training
Title: Stochastic Denominator Survival Training for Robust Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In the training loop, compute ordinary full-vocabulary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration as the primary loss. Add a helper denominator_survival_loss(logits, targets, num_hard_negatives, num_random_negatives) that flattens valid batch-time positions, always includes the true target token, adds detached hard negatives from the top non-target logits, adds uniformly sampled random negative token ids, removes duplicate candidates when practical, gathers the resulting candidate logits, and computes cross-entropy with the true target as the correct candidate. After warmup_iters, every survival_interval iterations, add lambda_survival times this auxiliary loss, ramping lambda_survival to values such as 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. Sweep candidate sizes such as 8, 16, and 32, and compare mixed hard-random candidates against hard-only, random-only, and random logit-dropout controls. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation NLL as the primary metric, denominator-survival validation loss, target rank statistics, top-k accuracy, expected calibration error, Brier score, rare-token validation loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline and uniform label smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: suffix_evidence_prefix_ranking
Title: Suffix-Evidence Counterfactual Prefix Ranking for In-Context Character Reuse
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, optimizer, ordinary next-character cross-entropy, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. In train(), after warmup_iters and every prefix_rank_interval iterations, create a counterfactual view by preserving a protected recent suffix such as the final 96 or 128 tokens while replacing the older prefix with prefixes from rolled batch elements. Run both the clean batch and the counterfactual-prefix batch. For protected suffix positions after a short burn-in, compute true-target log probabilities from both views. Add a small ramped ranking loss softplus(logp_counterfactual - logp_clean + margin), weighted by a detached suffix-evidence gate. The gate is active only when a short suffix pattern ending at the current input position, using lengths such as 2 and 4, previously appeared in the clean older prefix followed by the true target, and has lower continuation support in the counterfactual older prefix. Use a bounded support weight such as support / (support + tau), and do not apply ordinary CE to the counterfactual view. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, evidence-gated ranking accuracy, active gate fraction, clean-to-counterfactual suffix degradation, validation loss on supported suffix-match positions, repeated versus novel target loss, previous-occurrence-distance loss buckets, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, ungated prefix ranking, repeated-character count gating, shuffled evidence gates, and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: support_shrunk_role_embeddings
Title: Support-Shrunk Role Embeddings for Long-Tailed Autoregressive Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to compute token frequencies and smoothed predecessor/successor distributions for every character. Cluster normalized transition fingerprints into a small number of role clusters, such as 8, 16, or min(32, vocab_size), using deterministic numpy k-means. Modify GPT with an optional tied effective embedding matrix W_eff[token] = role_embedding[token_to_cluster[token]] + alpha[token] * residual_embedding[token], where alpha[token] is a fixed support-based shrinkage coefficient such as sqrt(freq / (freq + tau)). Use W_eff for both F.embedding(idx, W_eff) and output logits hidden @ W_eff.T, preserving the existing tied baseline path when disabled. Keep the optimizer, data loader, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation, and generation otherwise unchanged. Compare the original tied baseline, support-shrunk transition-role embeddings, frequency-only clusters, random balanced clusters, alpha=1 residual control, and a small tau sweep. Optionally include a learnable-alpha ablation only after the fixed-shrinkage result is established. Report ordinary validation loss, rare/common token loss, repeated versus novel target loss, expected calibration error, fixed shrinkage statistics, cluster assignments, parameter count, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: noise_adaptive_token_batching
Title: Noise-Adaptive Token Batching for Efficient Character Language Model Training
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged except for an optional GPT.forward(return_hidden=True) diagnostic path. Modify train() so the effective batch size is controlled online by choosing gradient_accumulation_steps for the next optimizer update from values such as 1, 2, 4, and 8. Train all methods to the same fixed supervised-token budget, and make warmup plus cosine learning-rate decay depend on consumed supervised tokens rather than optimizer-step count. Every adaptation_interval updates after warmup, run the current batch with return_hidden=True and compute a detached output-layer gradient-noise proxy by splitting valid batch-time positions into two groups, sketching each group's lm_head gradient from hidden states and softmax(logits) - one_hot(target), and measuring cosine agreement plus loss variance. Use EMA-smoothed hysteresis rules: increase accumulation when agreement is low or variance is high, and decrease it when gradients are coherent. Compare fixed accumulation levels, a simple hand-scheduled accumulation ramp, random accumulation with the same average token budget, and noise-adaptive token batching across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, validation loss per supervised token, validation loss per wall-clock time, optimizer steps used, selected accumulation schedule, gradient agreement, train-val gap, seed variance, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: crosslayer_kv_memory
Title: Gated Cross-Layer Key-Value Memory for Representation-Persistent Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional cross-layer memory path to GPT. Extend GPTConfig with use_crosslayer_kv_memory, memory_source_layer, memory_target_layers, memory_gate_init, memory_dropout, and detach_memory_source. Modify GPT.forward to store one early hidden stream, either the token-plus-position embedding stream or the output after block 1, and pass it only to selected upper Blocks such as the final two layers. Modify Block.forward and CausalSelfAttention.forward so target layers keep their normal causal self-attention, but also project the stored early stream into memory keys and values with a separate Linear layer. Reuse the current layer queries to attend causally over memory positions p <= t, concatenate the per-head memory outputs, and add them to the normal attention output through a learned scalar or per-head gate initialized to a tiny nonzero value such as 1e-3. Keep the data loader, optimizer, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation procedure unchanged. Compare the baseline, embedding-stream memory, block-1 memory, detached-memory ablation, and batch-shuffled-memory control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report ordinary train and validation loss, best validation loss, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, rare-token loss, validation loss at context lengths 64 and 256, learned memory gate values, memory attention distance profiles, parameter overhead, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: depth_gated_positions
Title: Depth-Gated Positional Signals for Crop-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_depth_gated_positions, position_gate_l2, and position_gate_init. In GPT.__init__, keep the existing learned positional embedding table and add scalar positional gates for the input stream and before each transformer block. Initialize the input gate to 1.0 and all block gates to 0.0 so the enabled model begins exactly as the baseline. Modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None) to compute pos_emb once, add input_gate * pos_emb to token embeddings before dropout, and add block_gate_l * pos_emb to the residual stream immediately before block l. Train with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optionally adding a tiny L2 penalty on non-input gates as an ablation. Compare the original baseline, learnable depth-gated positions, fixed evenly distributed gates, fixed late-only gates, and a no-position control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, validation loss at context lengths 64, 128, and 256, validation loss by absolute-position bucket, learned gate values by depth, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: activation_matched_width_birth
Title: Activation-Matched Width Birth for Compute-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional staged-width training mode that starts with a narrower GPT and widens once into the existing final architecture, for example from n_embd=256,n_head=4 to n_embd=384,n_head=6 while keeping head dimension 64. Implement build_width_stage_config() and widen_gpt_model(old_model, new_config), copying token embeddings, positional embeddings, LayerNorm weights, attention Q/K/V head blocks, attention output projections, MLP projections, and the tied output embedding into the leading shared subspace of the wider model. Initialize newly introduced channels, heads, and cross-subspace couplings conservatively so the widened model starts close to the narrow model but can quickly use the extra capacity. Rebuild AdamW after widening and avoid optimizer-state transfer. For a short recovery window after widening, keep a frozen copy of the pre-widen model and add a decaying temperature-2 KL distillation loss from old logits to new logits on the same batch, while ordinary next-character cross-entropy remains the main objective. Compare full-width baseline training, narrow-only controls, width birth without distillation, width birth with distillation recovery, and compute-matched full-width baselines. Report ordinary train and validation loss, best validation loss, loss spike after widening, validation loss per wall-clock time, effective parameter-token budget, seed variance, total train time, final parameter count, and final generation tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: symmetric_weight_neighborhood_distillation
Title: Symmetric Weight-Neighborhood Distillation for Flat and Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, standard validation, and ordinary generation path unchanged. Add a helper that temporarily perturbs selected trainable matrix weights in attention and MLP blocks, excluding embeddings, LayerNorms, and biases, and always restores the exact original parameters afterward. When this regularizer is enabled, disable torch.compile or apply perturbations through the uncompiled model handle for reliability. After warmup_iters and every neighborhood_interval iterations such as 8, compute the normal clean logits and next-character cross-entropy. Then evaluate the same batch under torch.no_grad() with antithetic perturbations +epsilon and -epsilon, normalized per tensor to a small fraction of that tensor's RMS. Form a detached local-neighborhood teacher by log-mean-exp averaging the two perturbed log probability distributions. Add a small ramped KL loss from this teacher to the clean logits, optionally only on a sampled subset of positions or the final suffix to control overhead, while ordinary cross-entropy remains dominant. Compare against the baseline, one-sided random weight-jitter consistency, random logit-noise consistency, and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report ordinary validation loss, local-neighborhood ensemble validation loss, clean-to-neighborhood KL, perturbation sensitivity, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged clean generation tokens per second.

Name: conformal_quantile_sets
Title: Conformal Quantile Prediction Sets for Reliable Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small conformal_head Linear(n_embd, num_coverages) used only for uncertainty prediction, with coverages such as 0.8, 0.9, and 0.95. Train the GPT normally with ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss. After warmup_iters, every conformal_interval iterations, compute detached per-token nonconformity scores as the true-target NLL from the current logits and train conformal_head(hidden_states) with quantile pinball loss for the desired coverage levels, using a small auxiliary weight so language modeling remains dominant. At evaluation time, split val.bin into calibration and held-out slices. On the calibration slice, compute one empirical conformal correction per coverage level from residuals score - predicted_quantile, then evaluate held-out prediction sets defined by tokens whose -log p(token | context) is below predicted_quantile + correction. Report ordinary validation loss as the primary LM metric plus held-out coverage error, average prediction-set size, singleton rate, coverage by predictive-entropy bucket, rare versus common target coverage, repeated versus novel target coverage, and set size by context length. Compare against the CE-only baseline with global conformal thresholds, entropy-bucket conformal thresholds, learned global temperature scaling, and the learned conditional quantile head across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged.

Name: optional_stopping_calibration
Title: Optional-Stopping Calibration for Adaptively Queried Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add helpers that construct detached stopping-time masks from model predictions within each sequence, such as the first position after a burn-in where top-1 confidence exceeds a threshold, the first position where entropy falls below a threshold, and fixed-position controls. In the training loop, always optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every calibration_interval iterations, add a small ramped calibration penalty only on stopped positions: for each stopping rule with enough selected examples, compute mean predicted top-1 confidence and detached empirical top-1 accuracy, then penalize their squared gap. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation NLL as the primary metric, standard ECE, stopped ECE under training and held-out stopping rules, stopped accuracy-confidence gaps, selective risk-coverage curves, average stopping position, and train-val gap. Compare the baseline, ordinary confidence calibration on all positions, optional-stopping calibration, and shuffled stopping-mask controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged, so inference tokens per second should be unaffected.

Name: boundary_conflict_gating
Title: Boundary-Conflict Gated Training for Crop-Robust Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. In the training loop, compute unreduced next-character cross-entropy and split target positions into low-context boundary tokens, such as the first 32 or 64 positions, and higher-context interior tokens. After warmup_iters, estimate boundary-interior gradient agreement from the same forward pass using detached output-layer gradient sketches: for each region, average outer-product sketches between hidden states and softmax(logits) - one_hot(target), optionally projected with a fixed random matrix for speed. Convert the cosine agreement into a bounded boundary weight, using full boundary weight when agreement is positive and reducing toward a floor such as 0.25 when agreement is negative, with EMA smoothing for stability. Optimize the weighted token loss, normalized by effective token weight. Compare against the original uniform loss, fixed context-ramp weighting, boundary-drop weighting, and a random-position split control. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, interior-suffix validation loss, loss by absolute position bucket, boundary-interior gradient agreement, active boundary weight, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: query_future_hits
Title: Query-Conditioned Future-Hit Prediction for Predictive Character States
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small training-only FutureHitHead that takes a hidden state and a queried token embedding, for example concat(h_t, e_q, h_t * e_q), and predicts binary logits for whether the queried token appears within future horizons such as 4, 16, 64, and 128 characters. On auxiliary iterations, sample batches with block_size + max_horizon + 1 tokens, keep ordinary X and Y for next-character cross-entropy, and sample a modest number of position-query pairs per batch. Query tokens should include the true next token, tokens sampled from later in the same future window, and random vocabulary negatives. Build multi-horizon binary labels by checking whether each queried token occurs within each horizon after the current position. Train every iteration with ordinary next-token CE; after warmup_iters, every future_hit_interval iterations, add a ramped auxiliary BCE loss with lambda_future_hit around 0.05 to 0.15. Use detached token embeddings for the query input as the default so the auxiliary mainly shapes hidden states rather than directly distorting the tied embedding/output matrix. Evaluation and generation ignore the auxiliary head and use the standard lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss, future-hit BCE and AUROC by horizon, repeated-target versus novel-target validation loss, validation loss by future-hit bucket, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, shuffled-query-label controls, and a non-query future-histogram auxiliary control.

Name: prequential_ridge_fastheads
Title: Prequential Ridge Fast Heads for Prompt-Local Language Model Calibration
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. After loading each dataset vocab_size, create fixed normalized random projection matrices R_vocab of shape vocab_size by sketch_dim and R_hidden of shape n_embd by fast_dim, with sketch_dim and fast_dim set to small values such as 32 or 64. During ordinary training, optimize the standard next-character cross-entropy unchanged. After warmup_iters, every fasthead_interval iterations, split each batch into an adaptation prefix and protected suffix. From a normal forward pass, compute detached prefix residual sketches e_t = R_vocab[target_t] - softmax(logits_t) @ R_vocab, fit a per-sequence ridge map W from projected prefix hidden features to these residual sketches using a small batched fast_dim by fast_dim solve, detach W, and apply it to projected suffix hidden features. Map predicted residual sketches back to vocabulary space with R_vocab.T and add a bounded scaled correction to suffix logits. Add a small ramped auxiliary suffix cross-entropy loss on the corrected logits, optionally with a weak KL anchor to the base logits. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, fasthead-corrected suffix validation loss, adaptation gain, expected calibration error, residual-sketch prediction error, shuffled-prefix-residual control loss, correction scale diagnostics, total train time, and unchanged base generation tokens per second. Default generation uses the base model unchanged, with an optional diagnostic that fits the fast head on the prompt prefix before sampling.

Name: causal_hawkes_logit_bias
Title: Causal Hawkes Logit Biases for Multi-Timescale Character Reuse
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_hawkes_logit_bias, hawkes_timescales, hawkes_rank, hawkes_gate_init, and hawkes_l2. Add a CausalHawkesLogitBias module that scans idx left to right and builds leakage-free normalized exponentially decayed one-hot history traces at fixed timescales such as 4, 16, 64, and 256 tokens. For each prediction position, map these causal history traces into an additive vocabulary-logit bias using a small signed low-rank source-to-target interaction trace @ A_tau @ B_tau, with the final factor or scalar gate initialized to zero so the enabled model starts exactly as the baseline. Modify GPT.forward and generate so enabled models add the Hawkes bias to the ordinary tied lm_head logits before cross-entropy or sampling; the disabled path remains unchanged. Train with the standard next-character cross-entropy objective, optionally adding a small L2 penalty on the Hawkes factors after warmup. Compare the baseline GPT, diagonal self-excitation-only Hawkes bias, low-rank cross-token Hawkes bias, shuffled-history Hawkes control, and fixed local-count prior control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, base-logit-only validation loss with the Hawkes bias disabled, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, validation loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned gate values by timescale, strongest learned excitation and inhibition pairs, train-val gap, total train time, and generation tokens per second.

Name: switching_compressor_regret
Title: Switching-Compressor Regret for Sequentially Adaptive Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Before training each dataset, compute a smoothed unigram prior from train.bin. Add lightweight causal expert helpers that use only visible in-window context to score the true next character: unigram, recent-window count models with windows 16 and 64, in-context bigram transitions, and suffix-copy models with suffix lengths 2 and 4. During training, compute ordinary next-character cross-entropy every iteration. After warmup_iters and every regret_interval iterations, compute detached per-token NLLs and support counts for all experts on the current batch, then run a small Viterbi dynamic program per sequence with switch costs such as 0.5 and 1.0 nats to find the best temporally coherent expert path. Add a conservative one-sided auxiliary penalty on valid supported positions, gate * relu(model_nll - oracle_nll - margin)^2, where gate depends on selected-expert support and lambda_regret ramps to 0.02, 0.05, or 0.1. Name: predictive_innovation_codebooks
Title: Predictive Innovation Codebooks for Discrete Autoregressive Belief Updates
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, ordinary evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. After loading each dataset vocabulary, create a fixed zero-mean normalized random projection matrix R from vocab_size to a small innovation_dim such as 32 or 64, and add a train-only learnable innovation codebook with 8, 16, or 32 vectors. In train(), always optimize standard next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every innovation_interval iterations, reuse the same logits from the normal forward pass, compute probs = softmax(logits), and form adjacent predictive innovation sketches delta_t = (probs[:, 1:, :] - probs[:, :-1, :].detach()) @ R, ignoring the first few positions for stability. Assign each detached delta_t to its nearest codebook vector and add a small ramped VQ-style auxiliary loss: ||delta_t - code.detach()||^2 + ||delta_t.detach() - code||^2. Optionally downweight the auxiliary for very high-surprisal observed tokens so rare large updates are not over-compressed. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, innovation reconstruction error, code usage entropy, dead-code fraction, predictive update norm by observed-surprisal bucket, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, continuous L2 update-smoothing, random code assignments, and multiple codebook sizes across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_legendre_memory

Experiment: Add an optional CausalLegendreMemoryAdapter inside each transformer Block after the attention residual and before the MLP. The adapter applies LayerNorm, projects hidden states to a bottleneck dimension, then applies fixed leakage-free causal depthwise Conv1d filters. Compare the baseline, causal Legendre memory, a same-parameter local Conv1d adapter, and an EMA-memory control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, final train loss, train-val gap, validation loss at context lengths 64, 128, and 256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned gate values by layer, moment-feature norms, parameter overhead, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: context_depth_mixture_distillation
Title: Sparse Context-Depth Mixture Distillation for Character-Level Transformers

Add a depth_mixture_teacher(X) helper that, for each batch position, looks up the visible suffix ending at X[:, t], recursively mixes the available depth-specific distributions with support gates such as support / (support + tau), and returns a dense teacher distribution plus diagnostics including effective context depth, teacher entropy, and support. Name: role_factorized_softmax
Title: Role-Factorized Softmax for Structured Character-Level Prediction
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to compute smoothed predecessor counts, successor counts, and log frequency for every token. Cluster these transition fingerprints deterministically into K token roles, such as 8, 16, or min(32, vocab_size), and compute empirical role frequencies for initialization. Extend GPTConfig with use_role_factorized_softmax, num_token_roles, role_anchor_weight, and role_cluster_type. Name: burnin_virtual_prefixes

Name: causal_span_aliasing

Name: soft_edit_alignment_ranking
Title: Banded Soft Edit-Alignment Ranking for Sequence-Robust Character Language Models

Name: repeat_switch_factorization
Title: Repeat-Switch Output Factorization for Character Language Models
Experiment: Add GPTConfig fields use_repeat_switch_factorization, repeat_switch_gate_init, and base_anchor_weight. The baseline branch computes ordinary tied-softmax log probabilities. The repeat-switch branch predicts p_repeat = sigmoid(repeat_head(hidden)); the current input token idx[:, t] receives log p_repeat, while all other tokens receive log(1 - p_repeat) plus a log-softmax over the tied lm_head logits with the current token masked out. The final training distribution is a probability mixture between the baseline branch and the repeat-switch branch using the learned gate. Name: counterfactual_influence_profiles

Evaluation and generation ignore the auxiliary head and use the standard lm_head unchanged. Name: adversarial_prefix_forgetting

Name: bigram_information_positions
Title: Bigram Information-Time Position Embeddings for Character Language Models

The disabled path is unchanged. Generation automatically recomputes information positions from the visible context inside forward. Keep the next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, batching, evaluation, and sampling otherwise unchanged. Compare the baseline, gated bigram information positions, information positions without absolute positions, unigram-surprisal positions, and shuffled-increment controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Name: diagonal_anchored_alignment

Name: heteroscedastic_logit_noise

Name: confidence_adaptive_dropout

Name: transition_tree_auxiliary
Title: Transition-Structured Hierarchical Output Supervision for Character Language Models
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to compute token frequencies and smoothed predecessor/successor transition fingerprints for every character. Title: BWT Suffix-Order Auxiliary Modeling for Compression-Aware Character LMs

For each sequence, sort cyclic rotations of the 257-token chunk lexicographically with original position as a deterministic tie-breaker, then form the BWT token stream from the token immediately preceding each sorted rotation. Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Name: manifold_confidence_cap
Title: Hidden-Manifold Confidence Caps for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f while keeping the default evaluation and generation path unchanged. In train(), maintain a FIFO train-only memory bank of detached L2-normalized final hidden states sampled from recent ordinary training batches, capped at a modest size such as 8192 or 16384 positions. Train every iteration with ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every density_interval iterations, subsample at most 1024 valid batch-time positions, compute their mean top-k cosine similarity to the memory bank in chunks, and treat this detached score as a hidden-manifold density estimate. Maintain an EMA low-density percentile, such as the 20th percentile, and add a weak one-sided confidence penalty only for positions below that threshold: low_density_gate * relu(max_prob - confidence_cap)^2, with confidence_cap around 0.90 and lambda_density ramped to 0.01 to 0.05. Name: latent_prefix_imputation
Title: Latent Prefix Imputation for Uncertainty-Aware Missing-Context Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a learned mask_embedding and an optional input_mask argument to GPT.forward so selected input tokens can be hidden while default training, evaluation, and generation remain unchanged. Train ordinary next-character cross-entropy every iteration. After warmup_iters and every impute_interval iterations, use a small auxiliary subbatch, choose one older-prefix position m per sequence, and reserve a later protected suffix for regularization. From the detached clean logits at position m - 1, take the top-k candidate identities for X[:, m]. Build k branch views with X[:, m] replaced by each candidate. Under torch.no_grad(), score only the observed evidence tokens between m and the protected suffix to form posterior weights over candidates, then compute a posterior-mixture teacher distribution on the protected suffix by log-mean-exp averaging branch log probabilities. Run one trainable masked forward pass where X[:, m] is replaced by mask_embedding, and add a small ramped KL loss from the posterior-mixture teacher to the masked-view suffix logits. Extend estimate_loss to report clean validation loss, masked-prefix validation loss, masked-to-mixture KL, posterior entropy, and loss by distance from the hidden token. Compare against the baseline, clean-to-mask distillation, uniform top-k branch mixtures, and random prefix masking across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: function_preserving_depth_birth
Title: Function-Preserving Depth Birth for Compute-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Refactor train() to support a two-stage depth schedule. Stage 1 trains a genuinely shallow GPT, for example 2 or 3 transformer layers, for an initial fraction of the normal training budget. Add expand_gpt_depth(old_model, new_n_layer) that creates the final 6-layer GPT, copies token embeddings, positional embeddings, final LayerNorm, tied output weights, and places the trained shallow blocks at evenly spaced depths. Newly inserted blocks are initialized as near-identity residual blocks using a residual gate or residual_scale initialized near zero, such as 1e-3, then ramped to 1 during a short recovery phase so the expanded network starts close to the shallow model while new block parameters still receive gradients. Rebuild AdamW after expansion and continue ordinary next-character cross-entropy training; optionally add a short temperature-2 KL loss from the pre-expansion shallow model only during recovery. Compare the standard 6-layer baseline, shallow-only controls, function-preserving depth birth, random new-block initialization, and a compute-matched full-depth baseline trained for the same estimated layer-token budget. Report best validation loss, validation loss per wall-clock time, estimated layer-token compute, loss spike after expansion, recovery speed, train-val gap, seed variance, total train time, and unchanged final-model inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: context_band_submodularity
Title: Context-Band Submodularity for Non-Interfering Long-Context Language Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional learned mask_embedding to GPT and modify GPT.forward(idx, targets=None, input_mask=None) so masked input positions replace token embeddings before positional embeddings; the default path remains unchanged. In train(), always optimize ordinary clean full-context next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters, every submod_interval iterations, protect a recent suffix such as the final 64 or 96 tokens and partition the older prefix into two contiguous distance bands A and B. Reuse the clean logits as the full S+A+B view, where S is the protected recent suffix context. Run three additional masked forward passes on the same X,Y: S only, S+A, and S+B. Compute unreduced target NLL only on protected suffix positions. Add safe monotonicity penalties such as relu(nll_SA - nll_S.detach() - margin), relu(nll_SB - nll_S.detach() - margin), relu(nll_full - nll_SA.detach() - margin), and relu(nll_full - nll_SB.detach() - margin), so richer contexts are trained not to underperform poorer contexts. Add a stop-gradient submodularity penalty that reduces excessive context synergy without encouraging clean degradation, for example relu((nll_SB + nll_SA) - (nll_full.detach() + nll_S.detach()) - margin), optionally downweighted for very high-entropy clean predictions. Keep clean CE dominant and leave generation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, fixed-band masked validation losses, negative context-gain rate, submodularity violation rate, repeated versus novel target loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, random band masking, clean-to-masked band distillation, and short-vs-full monotonicity across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: markov_regime_softmax
Title: Markov-Regime Softmaxes for Nonstationary Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_markov_regime_softmax, num_regimes, regime_rank, transition_diag_bias, and base_anchor_weight. In GPT.__init__, add K regime-specific low-rank output residuals, learned initial-regime logits, and a learned K by K transition-logit matrix. Initialize the residual factors so all regimes start identical to the ordinary tied-softmax baseline, and initialize transitions with a mild diagonal bias to favor persistent regimes. Modify GPT.forward to compute ordinary base logits, and when enabled also compute per-regime logits from base_logits plus the low-rank residuals. Add markov_regime_nll(logits_by_regime, targets, init_logits, transition_logits), using a log-space HMM forward algorithm over sequence positions; ignored targets contribute zero emission likelihood and the loss is normalized by valid target count. Train with the Markov-regime marginal NLL plus a small ordinary base-logit cross-entropy anchor. Extend estimate_loss to report base validation loss, Markov-marginal validation loss, static-mixture validation loss with transitions disabled, posterior regime entropy, expected switch rate, learned transition matrix, train-val gap, total train time, and base-path inference tokens per second. Add an optional generate_markov_filtered() diagnostic that maintains the causal posterior over regimes after each sampled token and samples from the filtered emission mixture. Compare baseline GPT, a single low-rank output-residual control, static regime mixtures, Markov-regime softmaxes, and shuffled-transition controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: counterfactual_entropy_temperature
Title: Counterfactual Entropy Temperatures for Context-Sensitive Character Language Models
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig/GPT with use_counterfactual_temperature, log_temp_max, temp_gate_init, base_anchor_weight, and entropy_target_weight. Add a small temperature_head Linear(n_embd, 1) and a learned scalar gate initialized so the model starts as the ordinary baseline. In GPT.forward, compute ordinary tied lm_head logits, predict a bounded per-token log temperature from final hidden states, and divide logits by exp(log_temp) before the calibrated cross-entropy; also expose a diagnostic path with temperature disabled. Train with calibrated CE plus a small base-logit CE anchor on every iteration. After warmup_iters and every temperature_interval iterations, preserve a recent suffix such as the final 96 or 128 tokens, replace the older prefix with a rolled same-batch prefix, and run the counterfactual view under torch.no_grad() with temperature disabled. On the protected suffix, form a detached teacher distribution by averaging clean base probabilities and counterfactual base probabilities, then compute its entropy. Add a small ramped Huber loss matching the entropy of the calibrated clean logits to this counterfactual-mixture entropy, while low-disagreement positions naturally stay near the base entropy. Extend estimate_loss to report calibrated validation loss, base validation loss, expected calibration error, Brier score, mean temperature, entropy-target error, validation loss by counterfactual-disagreement bucket, and held-out prefix-counterfactual robustness. Compare against the baseline, learned global temperature, unsupervised adaptive temperature, and a shuffled-counterfactual-target control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation uses the learned one-pass calibrated logits and requires no counterfactual views.

Name: butterfly_mlp_projections
Title: Butterfly-Structured MLP Projections for Parameter-Efficient Character Transformers
Experiment: Add a ButterflyLinear module that pads the larger of input and output channel dimensions to a power of two, applies log2(width) learned butterfly 2x2 mixing stages with variance-preserving initialization, slices to the requested output dimension, and optionally adds a small low-rank residual branch. Extend GPTConfig with use_butterfly_mlp, butterfly_low_rank_residual, butterfly_residual_rank, and use_butterfly_attention_ablation. Replace only MLP c_fc and c_proj with ButterflyLinear in the main experiment, keeping attention, embeddings, optimizer, batching, next-character cross-entropy, evaluation, and generation unchanged. Add an optional ablation that also replaces attention c_attn and c_proj. Compare the dense baseline, butterfly MLP without residuals, butterfly MLP with low-rank residuals, pure low-rank MLP controls, and parameter-matched narrower dense baselines across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report parameter count, best validation loss, validation loss per million parameters, convergence speed, train-val gap, total train time, inference tokens per second, and diagnostics such as butterfly stage norms and residual-branch norm.

Name: suffix_automaton_auxiliary
Title: Causal Suffix-Automaton Signals for Compression-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add small training-only auxiliary heads for bucketed suffix-automaton signals. Add compute_suffix_automaton_targets(X), used only on scheduled auxiliary iterations, that scans each sequence left to right on CPU and builds an online suffix automaton over the visible prefix. For each input position, record three causal labels: longest repeated suffix length bucket from len(link(last)), continuation-branching bucket from the outgoing transitions of that suffix-link state, and suffix-link depth bucket as a multiscale reuse signal. Train every iteration with ordinary next-character cross-entropy; after warmup_iters and every automaton_interval iterations, run the normal forward pass with return_hidden=True and add a small ramped auxiliary cross-entropy over these labels, with lambda_automaton in the range 0.02 to 0.10. Evaluation and generation ignore the auxiliary heads and use the standard lm_head unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train and validation loss as the primary metric, automaton-label accuracy, validation loss by repeated-suffix and branching buckets, repeated-substring versus non-repeated loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, shuffled-label controls, prefix-function auxiliary controls, and LZ-match auxiliary controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_value_innovation_attention
Title: Causal Value-Innovation Attention for Redundancy-Reduced Character Transformers
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_value_innovation_attention, value_innovation_window, value_innovation_gate_max, value_innovation_gate_init, and value_innovation_gate_l2. In CausalSelfAttention.__init__, add one learned raw gate per head when enabled, initialized so the path starts exactly as the baseline. In CausalSelfAttention.forward, after computing v with shape batch by heads by time by head_dim, compute a leakage-free rolling causal mean of v over the most recent W positions using cumulative sums. Define innovation = v - mean_v and use v_eff = v + value_innovation_gate_max * tanh(raw_gate_h) * innovation in place of v for the existing attention computation. This keeps q, k, masks, loss, optimizer, batching, evaluation, and generation unchanged, and remains compatible with flash attention because only the value tensor changes. Compare the baseline, window sizes W in {16, 64, 256}, a fixed-gate ablation, and a matched per-head value-scaling control that has gates but no causal centering. Extend diagnostics to report ordinary train and validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned gates by layer and head, innovation-to-value norm ratio, total train time, and inference tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: learned_slot_memory
Title: Learned Slot Memory Adapters for Parametric Associative Character Modeling
Experiment: Add an optional LearnedSlotMemoryAdapter inside selected transformer Blocks after the attention residual and before the MLP. Extend GPTConfig with use_slot_memory, slot_memory_layers, num_memory_slots, memory_key_dim, memory_gate_init, memory_dropout, and optional slot_balance_weight. The adapter applies LayerNorm to the residual stream, projects each token state to a query, attends over learned key slots with ordinary softmax attention, reads learned value slots, projects the retrieved value back to n_embd, applies dropout, and adds it through a learned scalar gate initialized to a small nonzero value such as 1e-3 so the model starts close to the baseline while slot parameters still train. Keep the ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, optimizer, batching, evaluation, and generation unchanged. Compare the baseline, slot memory with 64/128/256 slots, slot memory only in upper layers, a frozen-random-slot control, and a parameter-matched feedforward adapter or wider-MLP baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, train-val gap, parameter count, validation loss per parameter, rare-token loss, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, learned gate values, slot usage entropy, dead-slot fraction, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: innovation_gated_event_martingales
Title: Innovation-Gated Future-Event Martingales for Sequentially Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. After loading each dataset vocabulary, create fixed random frequency-balanced binary vocabulary partitions, for example 16 or 32 events whose positive side has roughly half of the train-set unigram mass. Add a training-only future_event_head Linear(n_embd, num_horizons * num_events), with dense horizons such as 1 through 8. On auxiliary iterations after warmup_iters, sample block_size + max_horizon + 1 contiguous tokens while still training ordinary next-character cross-entropy on the first block_size positions. Build binary labels indicating whether the character at each future horizon belongs to each event partition, masking positions without enough future context, and add a small ramped BCE loss. Add the key innovation-gated consistency term: for each horizon h > 1, align the forecast at position t for horizon h with the forecast at position t+1 for horizon h-1 for the same event, but weight the stop-gradient Bernoulli KL by a detached gate that is high only when the observed next token Y[:, t] had low surprisal under the ordinary LM logits. This encourages stable future-event beliefs after predictable observations while allowing large updates after surprising observations. Keep ordinary CE dominant and ignore the event head during evaluation and generation. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary train/validation loss as the primary metric, event BCE, event calibration error, gated and ungated martingale disagreement, forecast-update magnitude by observed-surprisal bucket, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, direct future-event BCE without consistency, ungated martingale consistency, and shuffled future-event labels.

Name: sampled_attention_commutation
Title: Sampled Attention Commutation for Stable Multi-Hop Context Routing
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to optionally return attention probabilities, using the manual causal attention path only when return_attention=True while preserving the default flash-attention path for ordinary training, evaluation, and generation. Propagate return_attention through Block.forward and GPT.forward. Add sampled_attention_commutator_loss(attn_maps, band_edges, max_queries, max_heads), which samples a small set of adjacent layer pairs, heads, and suffix query positions. For each selected query row, compute only the row-wise two-hop distributions A_next[q] @ A_prev and A_prev[q] @ A_next, avoiding full attention-matrix products. Aggregate each two-hop distribution into logarithmic causal distance bands such as 0-3, 4-15, 16-63, 64-127, and 128-255, then penalize symmetric KL or squared Hellinger distance between the two band distributions. In train(), optimize ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration; after warmup_iters, every commutation_interval steps, request attention maps and add a small ramped lambda_commute times the commutator loss. Evaluation and generation use the unchanged default forward path. Extend diagnostics to report ordinary train and validation loss, attention commutator divergence, validation loss at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a manual-attention no-regularizer control, attention distance-coverage regularization, and a shuffled-layer-pair commutation control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: blackwell_context_dominance
Title: Blackwell Context-Dominance Regularization for Non-Interfering Long-Context Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation, and generation path unchanged. After loading each dataset, scan train.bin once to compute unigram frequencies and create fixed unigram-balanced random binary event matrices, with one bank for training and a disjoint bank for diagnostics, using num_events such as 16 or 32. In the training loop, always compute ordinary full-context logits and CE on X,Y. After warmup_iters and every dominance_interval iterations, run one additional short-context forward on X[:, -L:], Y[:, -L:] with L such as 64 or 128, and align the final L positions of the full-context logits with the short-context logits. Add an event_context_dominance_loss helper that converts logits to probabilities, sums probability mass for each binary event, derives event labels from the true targets, and computes binary cross-entropy for full and short contexts. Add a small ramped hinge penalty mean(relu(full_event_bce - detach(short_event_bce) - margin)), so full-context predictions are discouraged from being worse than short-context predictions on coarse predictive decisions without directly distilling the short distribution. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, train-bank and held-out-bank event dominance violation rates, mean full-versus-short event regret, true-token negative-context-interference rate, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged full-context generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, true-token matched-context monotonicity, full-to-short KL consistency, and shuffled event-label controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: counterfactual_gradient_agreement
Title: Counterfactual Gradient Agreement for Prefix-Robust Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add make_rolled_prefix_view(X, Y, suffix_len) that preserves a recent suffix such as the final 96 or 128 tokens while replacing only the older prefix with rolled same-batch prefixes. Add compact_output_gradient_sketch(logits, hidden, targets, R_vocab, R_hidden), which approximates the suffix output-layer gradient by projecting residuals softmax(logits) - one_hot(target) with R_vocab, projecting hidden states with R_hidden, averaging their outer product over protected suffix positions, and flattening one sketch per sequence. Train every iteration with ordinary clean next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every agreement_interval iterations, run one rolled-prefix forward pass on the same batch, compute clean and counterfactual suffix sketches, detach the clean sketch, and add a small ramped hinge loss relu(margin - cosine(clean_sketch, counterfactual_sketch)). Weight the hinge by a detached gate based on counterfactual suffix NLL increase, so examples whose older prefix genuinely changes the prediction contribute little. Keep generation and ordinary evaluation unchanged. Extend estimate_loss() to report clean validation loss, rolled-prefix validation loss, gradient-sketch agreement, clean-to-rolled degradation, suffix loss by distance from prefix boundary, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, rolled-prefix KL consistency, rolled-prefix CE-only augmentation, and shuffled-suffix sketch controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: decaying_simplex_embeddings
Title: Decaying Simplex Anchors for Tied Character Embeddings
Experiment: Add an optional simplex-frame initialization and early decaying anchor for the tied token/output embedding matrix. For vocab_size <= n_embd + 1, initialize transformer.wte.weight from a centered regular-simplex-like row geometry, scaled to match the baseline embedding standard deviation; otherwise use a normalized random frame approximation. Add a simplex_frame_loss(weight) helper that L2-normalizes rows, penalizes nonzero embedding mean, and penalizes deviation of the row Gram matrix from the simplex target with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal -1 / (vocab_size - 1). In train(), keep ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary objective and optionally add lambda_frame * simplex_frame_loss only after warmup, decaying lambda_frame to zero by mid-training so the embedding geometry can adapt. Compare baseline random initialization, row-norm-only control, simplex warm start only, decaying simplex anchor only, and warm start plus decaying anchor across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, convergence speed, train-val gap, rare versus common token loss, expected calibration error, embedding pairwise cosine statistics, embedding mean norm, seed variance, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second.

Name: forecast_tape_ctc
Title: Forecast-Tape CTC for Alignment-Free Future Prediction in Causal Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a training-only future_ctc_head Linear(n_embd, vocab_size + 1), where the extra class is a CTC blank. Train every iteration with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every ctc_interval iterations, run the normal forward pass with return_hidden=True, sample a prefix boundary such as 128, 160, or 192 and a future length such as 16 or 32, ensuring prefix_len + future_len <= block_size. Use only the forecast tape hidden[:, prefix_len - tape_len:prefix_len, :] with tape_len around 2 to 3 times future_len, feed it through future_ctc_head, and apply torch.nn.CTCLoss(blank=vocab_size, zero_infinity=True) to the future target string Y[:, prefix_len - 1:prefix_len - 1 + future_len]. Add the CTC loss with a small ramped weight such as lambda_ctc up to 0.05 or 0.15 while keeping ordinary CE dominant. Evaluation and generation ignore the CTC head and use the standard lm_head. Extend estimate_loss() to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, forecast-CTC validation loss, greedy CTC future-string edit distance, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, fixed-horizon auxiliary future heads, shuffled-future CTC targets, and tape-length ablations across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: rotary_band_dropout
Title: Rotary Band Dropout for Length-Robust Character Transformers
Experiment: Add GPTConfig fields position_encoding, train_seq_len, max_seq_len, rope_base, rope_num_bands, rope_band_dropout_p, rope_consistency_interval, and lambda_rope_max. Set train_seq_len to 256 while allowing max_seq_len values such as 512. Modify GPT.forward so position_encoding='absolute' uses the existing learned wpe path, while position_encoding='rope' disables wpe and applies rotary embeddings to q and k inside CausalSelfAttention. Train every iteration with ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every rope_consistency_interval iterations, run one additional forward pass on the same X,Y with one randomly selected contiguous rotary frequency band replaced by identity rotations, and add a small ramped temperature-2 KL loss from detached full-RoPE logits to band-dropped logits. Keep generation unchanged except that RoPE models use rotary positions for the visible context. Extend get_batch and estimate_loss to evaluate validation loss at context lengths 64, 128, 256, 384, and 512, including suffix-only loss for contexts longer than 256. Compare learned absolute positions, absolute positions with max_seq_len=512, plain RoPE, RoPE with band dropout consistency, and a compute-matched extra-forward control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best 256-token validation loss, short-context robustness, 512-token extrapolation degradation, per-band ablation sensitivity, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: prequential_codelength_td
Title: Prequential Codelength TD for Predictive-State Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a training-only value_head Linear(n_embd, 1) that predicts discounted future codelength from each hidden state. Train with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters and every value_interval iterations, compute unreduced per-token NLL from the current logits, detach it, and build a truncated discounted return target G_t = sum_{k=0}^{H-1} gamma^k nll_{t+k}, masking positions without enough future context. Add a small ramped Huber loss between value_head(hidden_t) and G_t. After the value head has warmed up, optionally add a weak one-step TD consistency penalty value_t ≈ detach(nll_t + gamma * value_{t+1}). Evaluation and generation ignore the value head and use the standard lm_head unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, value prediction error, TD residual, correlation between predicted codelength and realized future NLL, validation loss by predicted-codelength bucket, expected calibration error, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a detached-hidden value probe that does not shape GPT representations, fixed-horizon future-NLL regression without TD consistency, and shuffled-return controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: prequential_bridge_calibration
Title: Prequential Bridge Calibration for Drift-Controlled Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a prequential_bridge_calibration_loss(logits, targets, chunk_len=64, huber_delta=0.05) helper. From softmax(logits), build residuals probs - one_hot(target) with ignore_index support, split each sequence into non-overlapping chunks, and compute cumulative residual paths over time for each vocabulary token. For each chunk, subtract the straight-line bridge from zero to the final cumulative residual, so the loss focuses on within-chunk temporal drift rather than endpoint marginal mismatch. Apply a Huber or squared penalty to the bridge residuals, normalized by the number of valid positions and vocabulary size. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration; after warmup_iters and every bridge_interval iterations, add a small ramped lambda_bridge times this loss, sweeping values such as 0.005, 0.01, and 0.05. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train and validation NLL as the primary metric, bridge calibration error, endpoint chunk-marginal error, prefix residual drift curves, expected calibration error, generated character-frequency KL, repeated-character rate, distinct n-gram fraction, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged inference tokens per second. Compare against the CE-only baseline, local marginal calibration, temporal spectral calibration, and a shuffled-time target control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: attention_spectral_rank
Title: Nonlocal Attention Spectral Rank Regularization for Context-Rich Character Transformers
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward, Block.forward, and GPT.forward to optionally return attention probabilities from selected layers, using the manual causal attention path only on scheduled auxiliary iterations while preserving the default flash-attention path for ordinary training, evaluation, and generation. Add attention_spectral_rank_loss(attn_maps, local_window=16, num_queries=64, min_nonlocal_mass=0.05, target_rank=4) that samples one or two layers, a small subbatch, and query positions with enough visible history. For each sampled head, exclude each query's recent local window, renormalize nonlocal attention rows only when sufficient nonlocal mass is present, L2-normalize the sampled rows, and compute a cheap participation-ratio effective rank from the row Gram matrix rather than a full SVD. Add a small ramped hinge penalty only when effective rank falls below target_rank, while ordinary next-character cross-entropy remains dominant. Extend diagnostics to report ordinary train/validation loss, nonlocal attention mass, effective rank by layer/head, attention sink concentration, validation loss at context lengths 64/128/256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, and previous-occurrence-distance loss buckets. Compare against the baseline, a manual-attention no-regularizer control, rowwise attention-entropy regularization, and attention head-diversity regularization across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged.

Name: causal_layout_equivariance
Title: Causal Layout Equivariance for Packed Autoregressive Language Modeling
Experiment: Add optional position_ids and attn_mask arguments to GPT.forward, Block.forward, and CausalSelfAttention.forward, keeping the existing flash-attention path unchanged when no mask is provided. Implement get_layout_pair_batch(split, num_streams=4, stream_len=64), which samples independent contiguous streams and returns two equivalent packed views: a contiguous layout with streams concatenated and a round-robin layout with stream tokens interleaved by logical time. For both views, reset position_ids to each token's logical time within its stream, use a block-causal attention mask so tokens attend only to earlier tokens from the same stream, and set targets at each stream's final token to -1. During normal iterations, train exactly as the baseline. After warmup_iters and every layout_interval iterations, train on a layout-pair batch using average CE from both layouts plus a small ramped symmetric temperature-2 KL between aligned logits for the same stream and logical position. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, contiguous-packed loss, round-robin-packed loss, layout KL, loss by logical position, and default generation tokens per second. Compare the baseline, packed CE without consistency, layout-equivariant training, and a physical-position control that uses the packed masks but does not reset logical position_ids across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: semi_markov_copy_spans
Title: Semi-Markov Copy-Span Marginalization for In-Context Character Reuse
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a lightweight CopySpanHead with a copy gate, span-length logits for lengths 2 through 8, and query/key projections for scoring earlier visible source positions. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters and every copyspan_interval iterations, reconstruct each chunk as torch.cat([X[:, :1], Y], dim=1), focus on a protected suffix such as the final 64 characters, and enumerate copy-span actions whose emitted substring exactly matches an earlier fully visible substring in the same sequence. For each suffix position, define a literal one-character transition from the ordinary lm_head and optional copy-span transitions from the CopySpanHead. Run a small log-space semi-Markov dynamic program over the protected suffix to marginalize all valid segmentations into literal emissions and copied spans. Add a ramped auxiliary loss ce_loss + lambda_copyspan * span_marginal_nll, keeping CE dominant. Default evaluation and generation use the ordinary lm_head unchanged. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, semi-Markov suffix NLL, copy posterior rate, mean copied span length, repeated-substring versus non-repeated loss, loss by previous-match distance, train-val gap, total train time, and ordinary inference tokens per second. Compare against the baseline, a single-token copy-mixture control, a random-source copy-span control, and copy-span scoring without marginalization across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: temporal_disagreement_sampling
Title: Temporal Disagreement Sampling for Learning-Progress-Aware Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Modify get_batch() so it can optionally return sampled memmap offsets and load explicit offsets. Keep the GPT architecture, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation code unchanged. Name: adversarial_residual_exchangeability

Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, ordinary next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Name: stopgrad_soft_rollout_matching

Name: embedding_fisher_moments
Title: Embedding-Fisher Moment Calibration for Tied-Softmax Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Name: natural_repeat_continuation_invariance

Name: depth_velocity_extrapolation

Name: leave_one_block_dominance

Name: causal_token_state_memory
Title: Causal Token-State Memory for In-Context Symbol Reuse
Experiment: Add an optional TokenStateMemoryAdapter to one or two upper transformer Blocks, placed after the attention residual and before the MLP. Experiment: Modify GPT with an optional rowwise variational tied-embedding mode. Keep transformer.wte.weight as the embedding mean and add one learned log_sigma scalar per vocabulary token row. Add a logits_from_hidden helper so enabled models use the same effective embedding matrix for both F.embedding(idx, W) and output logits hidden @ W.T, preserving input-output tying. Name: orthogonal_output_tying
Title: Orthogonal Output Tying for Role-Separated Character Embeddings
Experiment: Modify GPT so all output logits are computed through a logits_from_hidden helper. Name: prequential_innovation_sketch
Title: Prequential Innovation Sketching for Evidence-Aware Character Language Models
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f in addition to logits and loss. Train innovation_head(hidden[:, t, :]) to predict this detached sketch using Huber or MSE loss, optionally clipping or RMS-normalizing targets for stability, with lambda_innovation ramped to 0.02 to 0.10. Evaluation and generation ignore the auxiliary head and use the ordinary lm_head unchanged. Name: iterative_exposure_attention
