Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_iterative_exposure_attention, exposure_balance_iters, exposure_gate_init, exposure_target_gamma, and exposure_eps. In CausalSelfAttention.forward, when enabled, use the manual attention path. Compute ordinary causal softmax attention as a control branch. For the exposure-balanced branch, start from the same softmax probabilities, compute each key's current attention load summed over causal query positions, compare it to a fixed feasible exposure target derived from uniform causal attention, and rescale attention columns by a detached factor target_load / (current_load + eps). Repeat this rescale plus row-renormalization for 1-3 iterations. Optionally flatten or sharpen the target with exposure_target_gamma. Mix ordinary softmax attention and exposure-balanced attention using a learned per-head gate initialized at zero, then aggregate values normally. Keep the data loader, optimizer, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation, and generation API unchanged. Compare flash-attention baseline, manual-softmax control, one-step exposure correction, and iterative exposure-balanced attention across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, attention load ratio versus exposure target, early-token sink mass, attention entropy, validation loss at context lengths 64/128/256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, learned gates by layer/head, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: causal_key_innovation_attention

Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_key_innovation_attention, key_innovation_window such as 64 or 128, key_innovation_gate_max, and key_innovation_l2. Keep the data loader, optimizer, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation API otherwise unchanged. Compare against the baseline across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report train and validation loss, best validation loss, train-val gap, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, validation loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned gates by layer and head, key-innovation norm ratios, attention entropy, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: boundary_position_gradient_surgery

Name: delayed_onpolicy_rtd
Title: Delayed On-Policy Replaced-Token Detection for Evidence-Aware Character LMs
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f, and add a small training-only delayed_rtd_head Linear(n_embd, num_rtd_delays), with delays such as [0, 4, 16]. For each delay d, train delayed_rtd_head(hidden[:, d:, delay_id]) to predict whether X_corrupt[:, :-d] was replaced, ignoring unavailable positions and using positive-class balancing if needed. Name: event_martingale_calibration
Title: Event-Martingale Calibration for Sequentially Reliable Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. After loading each dataset vocabulary, create fixed random binary event partitions over token ids, balanced by train-set unigram mass, with one event bank for training regularization and a disjoint bank for diagnostics. Name: evidence_gated_prefix_bottleneck

Name: causal_token_phase_memory

Name: folded_axial_sparse_attention
Title: Folded-Axial Sparse Attention for Multiscale Causal Context
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_folded_axial_attention, fold_widths such as [16, 32, 64], folded_local_window such as 32, and folded_random_control. Give each Block a layer_id. In CausalSelfAttention, when folded attention is enabled, disable the flash path and use a precomputed causal boolean mask for that layer. For fold width W, map token position t to row floor(t / W) and column t mod W. A query may attend to all tokens in its recent folded_local_window plus all earlier tokens in the same folded column from previous rows; future tokens remain masked. Assign fold widths cyclically across layers so different layers expose different temporal scales. Keep model size, optimizer, data loader, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation, and generation otherwise unchanged. Compare full causal attention, local-only attention with matched recent window, deterministic log-skip attention, folded-axial attention, and density-matched random nonlocal masks across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report validation loss, validation loss at context lengths 64/128/256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, previous-occurrence-distance buckets, effective attention density, layerwise graph reachability, total train time, and generation tokens per second.

Name: soft_text_gradient_replay
Title: Soft-Text Gradient Replay for Condensed Character Language Modeling
Experiment: Add a train-only SoftTextReplayBank containing a small number of learnable token-logit windows of length block_size + 1, initialized from random train.bin chunks. Modify GPT.forward to optionally accept inputs_embeds and return final hidden states after ln_f, leaving the normal idx path unchanged. Build synthetic inputs as softmax(bank_logits[:, :-1]) @ transformer.wte.weight and synthetic targets as softmax(bank_logits[:, 1:]). Add soft_cross_entropy and an output_gradient_sketch helper that uses fixed random projections of hidden states and prediction residuals. During training, optimize ordinary real next-character CE on every iteration. After warmup_iters, every condense_interval, freeze GPT parameters and update only the replay bank for a few steps to match the detached gradient sketch of a fresh real batch, with small entropy and diversity regularizers. Every replay_interval, add a ramped soft-replay CE loss to the GPT update. Compare CE-only baseline, random real-window replay with matched extra compute, static soft replay without gradient matching, and soft-text gradient replay across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Include a frozen-bank transfer diagnostic where a learned bank is reused for a fresh seed. Report validation loss, best validation loss per step and wall-clock time, train-val gap, seed variance, frozen-bank transfer gain, synthetic entropy/diversity, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: monotone_logit_warping
Title: Rank-Preserving Monotone Logit Warping for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a logits_from_hidden helper to GPT. Extend GPTConfig with use_monotone_logit_warping, warp_num_knots, warp_range, warp_gate_init, base_anchor_weight, and warp_smooth_l2. When enabled, compute ordinary tied lm_head logits, center and RMS-normalize logits per batch-time position, then apply a learned global monotone piecewise-linear scalar warp initialized to the identity. Parameterize spline slopes as positive values so token ordering is preserved, unnormalize back to the original logit scale, and mix the warped logits with the base logits using a nonnegative learned scalar gate or a small hidden-state context gate initialized near zero. Train with next-character cross-entropy on the mixed logits plus a small base-logit CE anchor and a smoothness penalty on adjacent spline slopes after warmup. Modify estimate_loss and generate to use logits_from_hidden, while also reporting base-only validation loss with the warp disabled. Compare baseline GPT, learned global temperature, ungated monotone warp, and context-gated monotone warp across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report mixed validation loss, base-only validation loss, expected calibration error, Brier score, top-k ordering preservation, validation loss by confidence and target-rank buckets, learned warp curve, gate statistics, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: coded_sequence_multiplexing
Title: Coded Sequence Multiplexing for Separable Autoregressive Belief States
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to accept optional inputs_embeds and return_hidden while preserving the default idx-only path for ordinary training, evaluation, and generation. Create two fixed random sign code vectors over n_embd, code_a and code_b, and add two small train-only demix LayerNorms. Train every iteration with ordinary clean next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every multiplex_interval iterations, sample a second independent batch X2,Y2, compute token embeddings for X and X2, form multiplexed embeddings as (emb(X) * code_a + emb(X2) * code_b) / sqrt(2), and run one auxiliary forward pass from inputs_embeds. Demix final hidden states by multiplying by code_a and code_b, apply the corresponding demix LayerNorm, apply the tied lm_head, and add a small ramped auxiliary loss 0.5 * (CE(stream_a,Y) + CE(stream_b,Y2)) with lambda_multiplex in the range 0.02 to 0.15. Evaluation and generation use the ordinary path only. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, multiplex validation loss on paired validation batches, single-coded validation loss as a control, train-val gap, expected calibration error, and robustness to small embedding noise. Compare against the baseline, compute-matched extra clean forward, single-stream coded auxiliary training, standard embedding mixup, and shuffled-target multiplexing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: prefix_count_hierarchical_softmax
Title: Prefix-Count Hierarchical Softmax for Exchangeable Character Prediction
Experiment: Add compute_prefix_count_buckets(idx, vocab_size, bucket_edges), which uses a cumulative one-hot scan over the visible prefix idx[:, :t+1] to assign every vocabulary token at every position to a count bucket such as 0, 1, 2, 3-4, 5-8, and 9+. Extend GPTConfig with use_count_hierarchical_softmax, count_bucket_edges, count_mix_init, and flat_anchor_weight. In GPT.__init__, add a count_bucket_head Linear(n_embd, num_count_buckets) and a learned scalar mixture gate initialized so the model starts close to the ordinary flat softmax. Replace direct lm_head loss computation with a log_probs_from_hidden(hidden, idx, disable_count_hierarchy=False) helper: compute ordinary tied-softmax logits, compute count-bucket log probabilities from hidden states with empty buckets masked out, normalize the same token logits within each count bucket using masked logsumexp, and combine bucket mass plus within-bucket probabilities into a valid token distribution. Mix this hierarchical distribution with the ordinary flat softmax and train with NLLLoss plus a small flat-softmax anchor loss for stability. Modify generate() so enabled models recompute prefix-count buckets from the current context before sampling. Extend estimate_loss to report hierarchical validation loss, flat-only validation loss, count-bucket accuracy, count-bucket calibration error, target loss by prefix-count bucket, unseen versus repeated target loss, learned mixture gate, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare the flat baseline, seen-versus-unseen support gating, additive recent-count logit bias, prefix-count hierarchical softmax, and shuffled-count-bucket controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: graph_diffusion_softmax
Title: Graph-Diffusion Softmaxes for Transition-Aware Character Prediction
Experiment: Before training each dataset, scan train.bin to compute smoothed predecessor distributions, successor distributions, and token frequencies for every character. Build a fixed row-stochastic token graph from top-k nearest transition-fingerprint neighbors, with self-loops and light smoothing. Extend GPTConfig with use_graph_diffusion_softmax, graph_topk, graph_gate_init, base_anchor_weight, graph_gate_l2, and random_graph_control. Add a logits_from_hidden helper in GPT: compute ordinary tied-softmax logits and probabilities, then when enabled compute one-step lazy graph diffusion p_diff = p_base P. Predict a bounded per-token mixture gate from final hidden states, initialized to zero, and form p_mix = (1 - gate) * p_base + gate * p_diff. Train with NLL on log(p_mix), plus a small ordinary base-softmax CE anchor and optional gate L2 after warmup to discourage unnecessary smoothing. Modify estimate_loss and generate to use logits_from_hidden, while also reporting base-only validation loss with graph diffusion disabled. Compare the baseline, fixed global diffusion gate, context-adaptive gate, random graph control, and uniform label smoothing across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report mixed validation loss, base-only validation loss, expected calibration error, rare-token loss, transition-neighbor error rates, learned gate statistics, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second.

Name: self_metric_energy_scoring
Title: Self-Metric Energy Scoring for Calibrated Character Language Models
Experiment: Keep the GPT architecture, data loader, optimizer, evaluation path, and generation code unchanged. Add a self_metric_energy_loss(logits, targets, embedding_weight) helper. After warmup_iters and every energy_interval iterations, detach and L2-normalize the tied token/output embedding matrix, compute a vocab-by-vocab Euclidean distance matrix, and compute the categorical energy score over valid targets: E_p[d(z, y)] - 0.5 * E_{p,p}[d(z, z')], where p = softmax(logits). Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy as the primary loss plus a small ramped lambda_energy term, sweeping conservative values such as 0.01, 0.02, and 0.05. Because the distance matrix is detached, the auxiliary shapes predictive distributions but cannot collapse the embedding metric. Compare against the CE baseline, a fixed random-metric energy score, a row-shuffled learned-metric control, and identity-kernel Brier regularization. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary train/validation NLL as the primary metric, energy score, expected calibration error, Brier score, rare versus common token loss, repeated versus novel target loss, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: uncertainty_gated_head_coverage
Title: Uncertainty-Gated Head Coverage for Belief-Aware Context Use
Experiment: Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward, Block.forward, and GPT.forward to optionally return attention probabilities on scheduled auxiliary iterations, using the manual attention path only when attention maps are requested and preserving the default flash-attention path otherwise. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters and every coverage_interval iterations, run the current batch with attention maps enabled, compute detached normalized predictive entropy from the model logits, and aggregate attention maps from selected middle and late layers. For high-uncertainty query positions only, encourage the head-averaged attention distribution to have sufficient normalized causal entropy, while leaving individual heads unconstrained so sharp specialized heads remain possible. Use a small ramped one-sided hinge loss with a conservative entropy floor derived from predictive entropy, and ignore early positions with too few visible keys. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, expected calibration error, head-averaged attention entropy by predictive-entropy bucket, validation losses at context lengths 32, 64, 128, and 256, and train-val gap. Compare against the baseline, a manual-attention no-regularizer control, a fixed head-coverage floor, a per-head entropy-floor control, and a shuffled-predictive-entropy control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Generation remains unchanged and uses the ordinary fast path.

Name: cloze_lookahead_distillation
Title: Target-Masked Lookahead Distillation for Causal Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a learned mask_embedding to GPT and modify GPT.forward to accept input_mask, replacing masked token embeddings before positional embeddings. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward to accept lookahead_tokens, defaulting to 0 for the existing causal path; when lookahead_tokens > 0, use a manual mask that permits each position to attend to its causal prefix plus a bounded future window. Train every iteration with ordinary strictly causal next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every lookahead_interval iterations, sample a sparse nonadjacent set of prediction anchor positions t, create a teacher input where X[:, t + 1] is replaced by mask_embedding, and run one target-masked lookahead forward with lookahead sampled from values such as 4, 8, and 16. Add a small ramped auxiliary loss on only the anchor positions: weak cloze-lookahead CE plus temperature-2 KL from detached lookahead logits to the ordinary causal logits. Keep validation and generation strictly causal by default. Extend estimate_loss to report causal validation loss, target-masked lookahead loss, causal-lookahead KL, and validation loss by predictive-entropy or cloze-gain bucket. Compare against the baseline, target-masked causal auxiliary training without lookahead, unmasked lookahead as a leakage diagnostic excluded from main claims, and reverse-direction distillation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: crossfit_antigram_unlikelihood
Title: Cross-Fit Anti-N-Gram Unlikelihood for Negative Evidence in Character Language Models
Experiment: Partition each dataset's train.bin into K contiguous folds and build suffix-to-next-character count tables for suffix lengths such as 2, 4, and 6, storing total counts and per-fold counts. Modify get_batch() to return sampled offsets and fold ids. Train with ordinary next-character cross-entropy on every iteration. After warmup_iters and every antigram_interval iterations, look up the longest supported visible suffix for each token position using counts with the example's own fold subtracted. For high-support, low-entropy suffixes, define anti-continuation candidates as characters with zero or very low cross-fit count but nontrivial unigram frequency, excluding the true target. From these candidates, select a few detached high-probability negatives under the current model and add a capped support-gated unlikelihood loss, such as -log(1 - p_neg + eps), with a small ramped weight while keeping CE dominant. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric, anti-continuation probability mass, validation false-negative diagnostics, high-support-context loss, expected calibration error, generated anti-continuation rate, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare against CE-only training, random-negative unlikelihood with matched negative counts, full-train anti-dictionaries without cross-fitting, and positive n-gram distillation across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: in_context_rewrite_transduction
Title: In-Context Rewrite Transduction Curricula for Program-Aware Character Language Models
Experiment: Add a get_rewrite_batch(vocab_size, batch_size, block_size, device) helper that creates synthetic auxiliary sequences using only token ids already present in the dataset vocabulary. Each sequence reserves a few frequent tokens as delimiters when possible, writes a compact rule table in the prefix, then writes a query string followed by an answer string produced by deterministic left-to-right longest-match rewriting. Keep the rule system bounded and simple: start with one-token substitutions, then gradually introduce two-token patterns, short insertions, and short deletions while constraining the full sequence to fit block_size + 1. Construct X and Y as usual, but set targets to -1 outside the answer region so the auxiliary loss trains only execution of the in-context rewrite program. In train(), keep ordinary real-text next-character cross-entropy on every iteration; after warmup_iters, every rewrite_interval iterations add one rewrite batch with total_loss = lm_loss + lambda_rewrite * rewrite_loss, ramping lambda_rewrite to 0.05 to 0.15. Evaluation and generation on real text remain unchanged. Extend diagnostics to report ordinary validation loss as the primary metric plus held-out rewrite accuracy by rule type, query length, unseen symbol assignments, and overlapping-rule cases. Compare against the baseline, a copy-only synthetic curriculum, shuffled-rule controls, and random synthetic controls across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report best validation loss, train-val gap, repeated-substring validation loss, rewrite accuracy, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second.

Name: refreshable_state_stepper
Title: Refreshable Predictive-State Steppers for Fast Character LM Decoding
Experiment: Modify GPT.forward() to optionally return final hidden states after ln_f. Add a small StateStepper module, implemented as a gated residual MLP or GRUCell, that starts from a full-GPT hidden state at a refresh position and updates a surrogate hidden state using the newly observed token embedding plus a learned refresh-age embedding. Train the GPT with the ordinary next-character cross-entropy unchanged. After warmup_iters and every stepper_interval iterations, run the normal forward pass with return_hidden=True, sample anchor positions with room for a short rollout, and train only the StateStepper on detached full-GPT targets. Use teacher-forced unrolls of 2-8 steps, matching detached hidden states with normalized MSE or cosine loss and matching detached full-GPT logits with temperature-2 KL after applying the tied output weight to surrogate states. Keep standard validation and generation unchanged, but add a refreshable validation mode and generate_refreshable(refresh_interval), where the full GPT is run every R tokens and the stepper predicts intermediate tokens. Compare exact GPT decoding, linear hidden extrapolation, token-only recurrent stepping, and learned StateStepper with R in {2, 4, 8, 16} across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report ordinary validation loss, refreshable validation loss, KL drift from full GPT, hidden prediction error, generation tokens per second, repetition and distinct n-gram diagnostics, total train time, and stepper parameter overhead.

Name: periodic_extragradient_lm
Title: Periodic Extragradient Training for Stable Character-Level Transformers
Experiment: Add an optional periodic extragradient mode to train() while keeping the GPT architecture, batching, next-character objective, evaluation, and generation unchanged. After warmup_iters, every extragradient_interval iterations, replace the ordinary update with a two-pass same-batch step. First compute the ordinary loss and use torch.autograd.grad to obtain probe gradients for selected parameters without touching optimizer state; by default select matrix-shaped attention and MLP weights, with an all-parameter ablation. Temporarily move selected parameters by an RMS-normalized lookahead step, delta = -rho * rms(param) * grad / (rms(grad) + eps), then recompute the ordinary cross-entropy loss at the lookahead weights. Restore the exact original parameters, backpropagate only the lookahead loss through the normal GradScaler/AdamW path, and apply the existing gradient clipping and optimizer step. On non-extragradient iterations, train exactly like the baseline. Disable torch.compile for this experiment if temporary parameter edits are unreliable. Log train and validation loss, best validation loss, lookahead loss change, probe-gradient versus lookahead-gradient cosine, gradient norm, update norm, train-val gap, total train time, and inference tokens per second. Compare standard AdamW, compute-matched extra-forward AdamW without lookahead, matrix-only periodic extragradient, and all-parameter periodic extragradient across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: effective_context_length_scaling
Title: Effective Context Length Scaling in Small Character Transformers
Experiment: Refactor train() to accept n_layer, n_head, n_embd, block_size, batch_size, and max_iters as configurable arguments. Train a compact capacity grid at the standard 256-token context, for example a small, medium, and current-size GPT, using matched optimizer steps or matched token budgets. Modify get_batch(split, seq_len) and estimate_loss() so validation can be computed on identical suffix target positions while restricting visible context to lengths such as 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 tokens. For each model and dataset, report full-context validation loss, suffix-matched loss at each context length, marginal gain from additional context, and an effective context length defined as the shortest context whose loss is within epsilon of the 256-token loss. Add a small secondary ablation training selected models directly at shorter block sizes to distinguish context availability during training from context use at evaluation. Report parameter count, wall-clock time, inference tokens per second, and results across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. The key test is whether larger models extract longer usable context and whether short-context validation predicts full-context performance.

Name: last_block_tangent_matching
Title: Last-Block Tangent Matching for Stable Predictive Geometry
Experiment: Refactor GPT.forward() to optionally return the residual stream before a chosen late transformer block, such as the final block, plus the clean logits. Add continue_from_layer(hidden, start_layer) to run the remaining blocks, final LayerNorm, and tied lm_head. Train every iteration with ordinary next-character cross-entropy. After warmup_iters and every tangent_interval iterations, subsample valid batch-time positions, compute detached predictive distributions, and pair positions with similar predictions using coarse entropy buckets plus a low Jensen-Shannon distance or shared top-1 prediction. Build a sparse perturbation tensor where each paired position receives the same small RMS-normalized random hidden-space perturbation, run one extra continue_from_layer pass from the perturbed late hidden sequence, and compute logit-change sketches from perturbed_logits - clean_logits using a fixed random vocabulary projection. Add a small ramped auxiliary loss that matches normalized response sketches within each predictive pair, skipping tiny-response pairs for stability. Include random-pair, hidden-cosine-pair, and hidden-jitter consistency controls. Evaluation and generation use the unchanged ordinary forward path. Extend estimate_loss to report ordinary validation loss, expected calibration error, late-state perturbation KL, tangent-matching error, response similarity by predictive-similarity bucket, train-val gap, total train time, and unchanged generation tokens per second across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8.

Name: causal_novelty_key_bias
Title: Causal Novelty Key Biases for Redundancy-Aware Transformer Memory
Experiment: Extend GPTConfig with use_novelty_key_bias, novelty_window, novelty_support_tau, novelty_bias_max, novelty_gate_init, and novelty_random_control. Modify CausalSelfAttention.forward so enabled models use the manual causal attention path. For each layer, compute detached L2-normalized representations from the layer input x, then build a leakage-free key novelty score for each position by comparing it only to earlier positions within novelty_window: novelty_t = 0.5 * (1 - max_previous_cosine), with novelty_t set to 0 when no previous positions are available. Shrink novelty toward zero when few previous positions are available using support / (support + novelty_support_tau), and clamp it to [0, 1] without any future-dependent sequence normalization. Add a learned bounded per-head scalar times the key novelty score to attention logits before the causal softmax, with all gates initialized to zero so the model starts as a manual-attention baseline. Keep the data loader, optimizer, next-character cross-entropy objective, evaluation loop, and generation procedure unchanged, recomputing novelty from the visible context during generation. Compare the flash-attention baseline, manual-attention zero-bias control, causal novelty key bias, randomly permuted novelty scores, and a simple token-frequency novelty control across shakespeare_char, enwik8, and text8. Report ordinary validation loss, train-val gap, validation loss at context lengths 64/128/256, repeated-target versus novel-target loss, loss by previous-occurrence distance bucket, learned novelty gates by layer and head, attention mass assigned to high-novelty keys, novelty-score statistics, total train time, and inference tokens per second.
